-module(tmux_buffer).
-moduledoc """
Load, inspect and paste tmux byte buffers through an explicit endpoint.

Use `load/3` for binary payloads, including NUL bytes, and `show/2` to read
them back without terminal escaping or an added newline. `list/1` returns
captured metadata in tmux's newest-first order; it never loads payloads.
`paste/3` sends a named buffer to a registered pane. Direct input is available
through `tmux_pane:send_text/2`.

Names are NUL-free binaries, distinct from payload bytes. New names retain
tmux's storage rules: 3.7+ cleans names and can reject control bytes or escape
backslashes. Use observed names from `list/1` for subsequent calls. Empty load
input is tmux's no-op; it neither creates nor clears a buffer. `delete/2`
removes a buffer explicitly. Names have no persistent object identity, and
concurrent commands can replace a buffer between calls.

All operations except `capabilities/1` perform explicit I/O. They use the
one-shot transport and preserve operational errors and ownership checks.
The [buffer guide](buffers.md) shows a complete byte round trip.
""".
-export([load/3, show/2, show/3, list/1, delete/2, rename/3, paste/3, capabilities/1]).
-export_type([target/0, info/0, read_options/0, paste_options/0, capabilities/0]).

-doc "A stored buffer name, or latest to let tmux select its newest buffer.".
-type target() :: binary() | latest.
-doc "Captured name, payload byte count and Unix creation time; not a live handle.".
-type info() :: #{name := binary(), size := non_neg_integer(), created := non_neg_integer()}.
-doc "Read bounds: max_bytes defaults to 1 MiB; deadline_ms defaults to 2500.".
-type read_options() :: #{max_bytes => 0..1048576, deadline_ms => 1..600000}.
-doc """
Paste controls. separator defaults to LF; delete and bracketed default to
false. sanitize defaults to false, preserving bytes. Explicit sanitization
requires tmux 3.7+. Bracketing occurs only when the pane enables bracketed paste.
""".
-type paste_options() :: #{separator => binary(), delete => boolean(),
    bracketed => boolean(), sanitize => boolean()}.
-doc "Source-defined buffer behavior for a parsed daemon version.".
-type capabilities() :: #{paste_sanitize := boolean(), cleaned_names := boolean(),
    rename_replaces := boolean(), strict_named_target := boolean()}.

-doc """
Describe version differences without I/O. This does not qualify an untested
release. `paste/3` uses paste_sanitize to gate sanitization and render raw paste.

```erlang
1> {ok, V} = tmux_version:parse(<<"tmux 3.3">>), ok.
ok
2> tmux_buffer:capabilities(V).
#{paste_sanitize => false,cleaned_names => false,
  rename_replaces => false,strict_named_target => false}
```
""".
-spec capabilities(tmux_version:t()) -> capabilities().
capabilities(Version) ->
    #{paste_sanitize => tmux_version:at_least(Version, {3, 7}),
      cleaned_names => tmux_version:at_least(Version, {3, 7}),
      rename_replaces => tmux_version:at_least(Version, {3, 4}),
      strict_named_target => tmux_version:at_least(Version, {3, 4})}.

-doc """
Load binary bytes under a name, or create an automatic buffer. Input may
contain NUL. Empty input succeeds without changing the buffer store, including
an existing name. The command payload, including argv and stdin, must fit the
endpoint's 256 KiB admission limit. See `tmux_server:command/3`.

Returns the completed command result, not a persistent buffer handle. No
clipboard write is requested. Native stored-name rules still apply.
""".
-spec load(tmux_server:t(), binary() | automatic, binary()) ->
    {ok, tmux_operation:completed()} | {error, map()}.
load(Server, Name, Bytes) ->
    maybe
        ok ?= payload(Bytes),
        {ok, Args} ?= case Name of automatic -> {ok, []}; _ -> named(Name) end,
        run(Server, <<"load-buffer">>, Args ++ [<<"--">>, <<"-">>], #{stdin => Bytes})
    end.

-doc "Read exact payload bytes with default bounds. See `show/3` for limits.".
-spec show(tmux_server:t(), target()) -> {ok, binary()} | {error, map()}.
show(Server, Buffer) -> show(Server, Buffer, #{}).

-doc """
Read exact payload bytes from an unattached one-shot client. No print decoding
or newline removal applies. max_bytes is 0 through 1 MiB; exceeding it returns
output_limit with partial command evidence, never a successful truncated value.
deadline_ms is 1 through 600000. Missing buffers return buffer_not_found.
""".
-spec show(tmux_server:t(), target(), read_options()) -> {ok, binary()} | {error, map()}.
show(Server, Buffer, Options) ->
    maybe
        {ok, ReadOptions} ?= read_options(Options),
        {ok, Args} ?= target(Buffer),
        {ok, #{stdout := Bytes}} ?= run(Server, <<"show-buffer">>, Args, ReadOptions),
        {ok, Bytes}
    end.

-doc """
Capture metadata in tmux's newest-first insertion order. Renaming preserves
position; replacing data through `load/3` inserts a new buffer. Length frames
preserve names containing delimiters, newlines or invalid UTF-8 on releases
that permit them. Returns an ordinary list, bounded to 4096 rows and 1 MiB of
encoded output. No payloads, hidden refresh or atomic snapshot is provided.
""".
-spec list(tmux_server:t()) -> {ok, [info()]} | {error, map()}.
list(Server) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Version} ?= tmux_server:version(Server),
        {ok, #{stdout := Bytes}} ?= run(Server, <<"list-buffers">>, [<<"-F">>,
            <<"#{n:buffer_name}:#{buffer_size}:#{buffer_created}:#{q:buffer_name}">>], #{}),
        tmux_buffer_codec:list(Bytes, Version)
    end.

-doc """
Delete a named buffer or latest. Missing buffers return buffer_not_found.
This performs I/O and affects the server-wide buffer store.

On 3.3/3.3a, named deletion first checks existence with a zero-output `show/3`
read because native deletion falls back to the newest buffer when a name is
absent. This check does not collect a payload or depend on the list bounds.
It is not atomic: concurrent removal after the check can trigger that fallback.
Use external serialization or tmux 3.4+ when that race is unacceptable.
""".
-spec delete(tmux_server:t(), target()) ->
    {ok, tmux_operation:completed()} | {error, map()}.
delete(Server, Buffer) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Args} ?= target(Buffer),
        ok ?= preflight(Server, Buffer),
        run(Server, <<"delete-buffer">>, Args, #{})
    end.

-doc """
Rename one explicit name. tmux 3.3 refuses an occupied destination; 3.4+ replaces
it. This is native collision behavior, not an atomic absence check. Identical
input names return same_buffer_name before I/O, avoiding unsafe legacy tmux
paths. New names retain native cleaning rules; see `list/1` for stored names.
The same observed 3.3/3.3a missing-name preflight and race as `delete/2` apply.
""".
-spec rename(tmux_server:t(), binary(), binary()) ->
    {ok, tmux_operation:completed()} | {error, map()}.
rename(Server, Old, New) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Args} ?= named(Old),
        {ok, _} ?= named(New),
        ok ?= case Old =:= New of
            true -> {error, #{code => same_buffer_name}};
            false -> ok
        end,
        ok ?= preflight(Server, Old),
        run(Server, <<"set-buffer">>, Args ++ [<<"-n">>, New], #{})
    end.

-doc """
Send a named buffer or latest to a registered pane. Defaults preserve payload
bytes: LF separators and unsanitized input. On tmux 3.7+, raw paste uses -S;
sanitize=true selects its safe print encoding. Earlier releases reject that
request with unsupported_capability before dispatch.

separator is NUL-free; delete removes the buffer after the native paste call.
bracketed adds markers only if the target has enabled that terminal mode.
Native input-off/dead-pane behavior still applies. Completion establishes the
tmux command result, not consumption by the child. No automatic retry occurs.
""".
-spec paste(tmux_model:pane(), target(), paste_options()) ->
    {ok, tmux_operation:completed()} | {error, map()}.
paste(Pane, Buffer, Options) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Flags} ?= tmux_args:options(Options,
            [{separator, bytes, <<"-s">>}, {delete, flag, <<"-d">>},
             {bracketed, flag, <<"-p">>}, {sanitize, boolean, <<>>}]),
        {ok, BufferArgs} ?= target(Buffer),
        {ok, Server, PaneTarget} ?= tmux_target:resolve(pane, Pane),
        {ok, Version} ?= tmux_server:version(Server),
        {ok, Safety} ?= safety(maps:get(sanitize, Options, false), capabilities(Version)),
        Separator = case maps:is_key(separator, Options) of
            true -> [];
            false -> [<<"-s">>, <<"\n">>]
        end,
        run(Server, <<"paste-buffer">>, BufferArgs ++ [<<"-t">>, PaneTarget] ++
            Safety ++ Separator ++ Flags, #{})
    end.

safety(true, #{paste_sanitize := false}) ->
    {error, #{code => unsupported_capability, capability => paste_sanitize}};
safety(false, #{paste_sanitize := true}) -> {ok, [<<"-S">>]};
safety(_, _) -> {ok, []}.

preflight(_, latest) -> ok;
preflight(Server, Name) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Version} ?= tmux_server:version(Server),
        case capabilities(Version) of
            #{strict_named_target := true} -> ok;
            _ ->
                %% Strict native show has no missing-name fallback. A zero
                %% allowance admits one detection byte and retires the client
                %% before returning overflow. Both outcomes prove existence.
                case show(Server, Name, #{max_bytes => 0}) of
                    {ok, <<>>} -> ok;
                    {error, #{code := output_limit, stream := stdout,
                              stdout := <<>>, cleanup := complete}} -> ok;
                    Error -> Error
                end
        end
    end.

target(latest) -> {ok, []};
target(Name) -> named(Name).

named(Name) when is_binary(Name), byte_size(Name) > 0 ->
    case binary:match(Name, <<0>>) of
        nomatch -> {ok, [<<"-b">>, Name]};
        _ -> {error, #{code => invalid_buffer_name}}
    end;
named(_) -> {error, #{code => invalid_buffer_name}}.

payload(Bytes) when is_binary(Bytes), byte_size(Bytes) =< 262144 -> ok;
payload(Bytes) when is_binary(Bytes) -> {error, #{code => command_limit}};
payload(_) -> {error, #{code => invalid_buffer_data}}.

read_options(Options) when is_map(Options) ->
    Unknown = lists:sort(maps:keys(maps:without([max_bytes, deadline_ms], Options))),
    case Unknown of
        [Key | _] -> {error, #{code => unknown_option, path => [Key]}};
        [] ->
            Bytes = maps:get(max_bytes, Options, 1048576),
            Deadline = maps:get(deadline_ms, Options, 2500),
            if
                not is_integer(Bytes, 0, 1048576) ->
                    {error, #{code => invalid_option, path => [max_bytes]}};
                not is_integer(Deadline, 1, 600000) ->
                    {error, #{code => invalid_option, path => [deadline_ms]}};
                true -> {ok, #{max_stdout => Bytes, deadline_ms => Deadline}}
            end
    end;
read_options(_) -> {error, #{code => invalid_options, path => []}}.

run(Server, Name, Args, Options) ->
    case tmux_target:run(Server, Name, Args, Options) of
        {error, #{code := command_error, stderr := Stderr} = Detail} ->
            Missing = case Stderr of
                <<"no buffer", _/binary>> -> true;
                <<"unknown buffer: ", _/binary>> -> true;
                _ -> false
            end,
            {error, case Missing of true -> Detail#{code => buffer_not_found}; false -> Detail end};
        Result -> Result
    end.

-module(tmux_capability).
-moduledoc """
Look up source-derived native command declarations and feature minimums.

`commands/1` and `command/2` describe the exact source profiles in `profiles/0`.
Profiles cover every release in the supported tmux 3.3a–3.8 range. They do not
contact tmux, interpret its arguments or qualify another build.
Canonical command names are lookup keys; aliases remain metadata. A native
declaration does not mean this library provides a typed facade for it. Use
`tmux_command:raw/2` for an explicit trusted command.

`describe/1` reports selected native feature minimums. `require/2` compares a
parsed version with one of those minimums; it does not perform I/O or dispatch
the command. Numeric minimum checks also accept uncatalogued and tracking
versions, preserving the distinction from exact parser discovery. They do not
establish runtime or CI qualification. Use `tmux_server:version/1` to obtain the
version captured by a registered endpoint.

The [generated reference](commands-reference.md) records source profiles and
parser declarations. Maintaining the catalogue needs a tmux source checkout;
installed consumers use compiled data and OTP only.
""".
-export([profiles/0, commands/1, command/2, describe/1, require/2]).
-export_type([feature/0, feature_info/0, command_info/0]).

-doc "Selected native capabilities; these do not introduce new typed command options.".
-type feature() :: native_list_filter | send_client_keys | key_list_format | layout_json.
-doc "Source-sampled profiles, native commands, description and numeric minimum.".
-type feature_info() :: #{minimum := {non_neg_integer(), non_neg_integer()},
    commands := [binary()], description := binary(), versions := [binary()]}.
-doc """
Native alias, flag declaration and positional bounds, with the exact source
file, commit and SHA-256. none means no alias or an unbounded positional upper
limit. Additional argument callbacks and runtime checks remain tmux's concern.
""".
-type command_info() :: #{alias := binary() | none, argument_spec := binary(),
    min_args := non_neg_integer(), max_args := non_neg_integer() | none,
    source := #{file := binary(), commit := binary(), sha256 := binary()}}.

-doc "List the exact source profile names in catalogue order. Performs no I/O.".
-spec profiles() -> [binary()].
profiles() -> maps:get(versions, tmux_capability_data:all()).

-doc """
Return sorted canonical command names for an exact catalogued stable version.
Tracking and uncatalogued versions return unsupported_command_catalogue.
This is pure source discovery; it does not execute list-commands.
""".
-spec commands(tmux_version:t()) -> {ok, [binary()]} | {error, map()}.
commands(Version) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Profile} ?= profile(Version),
        Data = maps:get(commands, tmux_capability_data:all()),
        {ok, lists:sort([Name || {Name, Variants} <- maps:to_list(Data),
            variant(Profile, Variants) =/= none])}
    end.

-doc """
Look up one canonical native command in an exact source profile. Returns
unknown_command for aliases or unknown names, unsupported_command when a
known command is absent from that profile, and unsupported_command_catalogue
for uncatalogued or tracking versions. Performs no I/O.

```erlang
1> {ok, V} = tmux_version:parse(<<"tmux 3.3a">>), ok.
ok
2> {ok, C} = tmux_capability:command(V, <<"send-keys">>), ok.
ok
3> maps:get(file, maps:get(source, C)).
<<"cmd-send-keys.c">>
```
""".
-spec command(tmux_version:t(), binary()) -> {ok, command_info()} | {error, map()}.
command(Version, Name) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Profile} ?= profile(Version),
        Data = tmux_capability_data:all(),
        case maps:find(Name, maps:get(commands, Data)) of
            error -> {error, #{code => unknown_command, command => Name}};
            {ok, Variants} -> case variant(Profile, Variants) of
                none -> {error, #{code => unsupported_command,
                    command => Name, version => Profile}};
                {ok, Metadata} ->
                    File = maps:get(file, Metadata),
                    Source = maps:get(Profile, maps:get(sources, Data)),
                    {ok, (maps:remove(file, Metadata))#{source => #{file => File,
                        commit => maps:get(commit, Source),
                        sha256 => maps:get(File, maps:get(files, Source))}}}
            end
        end
    end.

-doc """
Return a selected native feature's source-derived minimum and sampled
profiles. Unknown features return unknown_capability. Performs no I/O;
`require/2` applies the minimum to a parsed version.
""".
-spec describe(feature()) -> {ok, feature_info()} | {error, map()}.
describe(Feature) when is_atom(Feature) ->
    Features = maps:get(features, tmux_capability_data:all()),
    case maps:find(atom_to_binary(Feature, utf8), Features) of
        {ok, #{minimum := [Major, Minor]} = Info} ->
            {ok, Info#{minimum => {Major, Minor}}};
        error -> {error, #{code => unknown_capability, capability => Feature}}
    end;
describe(Feature) -> {error, #{code => unknown_capability, capability => Feature}}.

-doc """
Require a native feature's numeric major/minor floor without dispatching I/O.
An older version returns unsupported_capability with capability and minimum.
Patch letters and tracking markers do not promote an older minor version.
Unknown features and malformed parsed versions return distinct errors.

```erlang
1> {ok, V} = tmux_version:parse(<<"tmux 3.4">>), ok.
ok
2> tmux_capability:require(V, send_client_keys).
ok
```
""".
-spec require(tmux_version:t(), feature()) -> ok | {error, map()}.
require(Version, Feature) ->
    maybe
        ok ?= valid_version(Version),
        {ok, #{minimum := Minimum}} ?= describe(Feature),
        case tmux_version:at_least(Version, Minimum) of
            true -> ok;
            false -> {error, #{code => unsupported_capability,
                capability => Feature, minimum => Minimum}}
        end
    end.

variant(_, []) -> none;
variant(Profile, [#{versions := Versions, metadata := Metadata} | Rest]) ->
    case lists:member(Profile, Versions) of
        true -> {ok, Metadata};
        false -> variant(Profile, Rest)
    end.

profile(Version) ->
    maybe
        ok ?= valid_version(Version),
        #{major := Major, minor := Minor, patch := Patch, tracking := Tracking} = Version,
        Prefix = case Tracking of true -> <<"next-">>; false -> <<>> end,
        Profile = <<Prefix/binary, (integer_to_binary(Major))/binary, $.,
            (integer_to_binary(Minor))/binary, Patch/binary>>,
        case lists:member(Profile, profiles()) of
            true -> {ok, Profile};
            false -> {error, #{code => unsupported_command_catalogue, version => Profile}}
        end
    end.

valid_version(#{major := Major, minor := Minor, patch := Patch, tracking := Tracking})
  when is_integer(Major), Major >= 0, is_integer(Minor), Minor >= 0,
       is_boolean(Tracking) ->
    case Patch of
        <<>> -> ok;
        <<C>> when C >= $a, C =< $z -> ok;
        _ -> {error, #{code => invalid_version}}
    end;
valid_version(_) -> {error, #{code => invalid_version}}.

-module(tmux_command).
-moduledoc """
Build tmux commands and bounded sequences without performing I/O.

Arguments remain binary values. Rendering protects trailing semicolons from
tmux's command separator parser. This is distinct from shell quoting and from
format expansion. A raw command is trusted application code; external services
must apply their own command allowlist and write policy.

```erlang
1> {ok, C} = tmux_command:raw(<<"list-panes">>, [<<"-a">>]), ok.
ok
2> tmux_command:argv(C).
[<<"list-panes">>,<<"-a">>]
3> tmux_command:literal_format(<<"api-#{pane_id}">>).
{ok,<<"api-##{pane_id}">>}
4> tmux_command:launch(#{argv => [<<"/bin/printf">>, <<"hello">>]}).
{ok,[<<"/bin/printf">>,<<"hello">>]}
```

Use `literal_format/1` only for a whole argument that tmux
expands as a format, such as a new name or cwd. It does not encode a value
nested in a format expression. tmux's stored-name escaping and session-name
substitutions still apply. Use `literal_format/2` with mode time
for commands such as display-message that also expand strftime percent
directives. This protects one format-expansion pass, not later visual style
rendering or recursive/nested expansion. No renderer reverses stored-name
semantics.

`launch/1` distinguishes executable argv from an explicitly
requested shell command. A singleton argv uses the installed helper's
exec-only mode because tmux otherwise passes one argument to its default
shell. Empty argv is invalid; default_shell explicitly requests tmux's
configured default command/shell. The internal helper uses an absolute path so
a child's cwd does not change helper resolution. Relative executable arguments
retain their native meaning.

Empty shell commands have command-specific lifetime. split-window creates a
process-free pane. new-session executes an empty shell command and can remove
the new object immediately. new-window does likewise before tmux 3.8; tmux 3.8
creates a process-free pane. Use a persistent job for parent sessions/windows
that must remain available across supported versions.

Submit commands through `tmux_server:command/3` or `tmux_operation:start/3`.
`sequence/1` combines flat command values for one-shot execution with combined
output and a possible completed prefix on error.
The [job guide](jobs.md) shows submission, completion and cancellation.
`tmux_session:rename_command/2` and `tmux_pane:resize_command/2` build values
bound to their row's captured origin. Execution through another endpoint
returns different_owner before native work. Construction does not validate
endpoint liveness or authorize an automatic mutation retry.

`wait_for/2` builds native channel signals, waits and advisory locks.
`source_file/2` builds configuration loading from stdin or a literal absolute
path. Both return command values without opening an endpoint or doing I/O.
`to_config/1` renders a command or bounded command list for native
configuration input, preserving argument bytes through tmux's lexer.
""".
-export([raw/2, sequence/1, validate/1, argv/1, literal_format/1, literal_format/2, launch/1,
         wait_for/2, source_file/2, to_config/1]).
-export([generated/3, provenance/1]).
-export_type([t/0]).
-export_type([wait_action/0, source/0, source_options/0]).

-doc "Native wait channel action. lock/unlock are explicit advisory operations, not owned leases.".
-type wait_action() :: wait | signal | lock | unlock.
-doc "Standard input, or one literal absolute POSIX byte path with no NUL.".
-type source() :: stdin | binary().
-doc "Native parse-only and quiet-missing-file flags; both default to false.".
-type source_options() :: #{parse_only => boolean(), quiet => boolean()}.

-export_type([launch_spec/0]).
-doc "Explicit executable argv, an explicitly requested shell command, or tmux's configured default shell.".
-type launch_spec() :: default_shell | #{argv := nonempty_list(binary())} | #{shell := binary()}.

-export_type([respawn_spec/0]).
-doc """
Reuse tmux's saved command/shell, or replace it with argv or a shell command.
Used by `tmux_pane:respawn/2` and `tmux_window:respawn/2`.
""".
-type respawn_spec() :: previous | #{argv := nonempty_list(binary())} | #{shell := binary()}.

-doc """
A validated command or flat sequence. Rendering and execution remain separate.
Domain builders retain a captured endpoint origin; raw values are unbound.
""".
-opaque t() :: {tmux_command, binary(), [binary()]}
             | {tmux_command, binary(), [binary()],
                #{origin := reference(), kind := session_rename | pane_resize}}
             | {tmux_sequence, nonempty_list(t())}.

-doc """
Validate one trusted command name and binary argv, without I/O. The renderer
protects tmux separators; it does not provide shell or nested-format quoting.
External services still need their own allowlists and write policy. Names are
at most 128 bytes. NUL bytes are rejected, and at most 2,040 arguments fit
within a 32 KiB command reservation including framing overhead.
""".
-spec raw(binary(), [binary()]) -> {ok, t()} | {error, map()}.
raw(Name, Arguments) ->
    case valid_name(Name) of
        false -> {error, #{code => invalid_command}};
        true ->
            maybe
                ok ?= words(Arguments, 2040, byte_size(Name) + 2),
                {ok, {tmux_command, compact(Name), [compact(A) || A <- Arguments]}}
            end
    end.

-doc """
Build one bounded native command sequence without I/O. Members must be a
nonempty flat list of at most 256 command values. Their combined executable
argv is limited to 2041 words and 32 KiB including separator overhead.
Arguments keep the literal separator protection of `raw/2`; only boundaries
between members become native command separators in `argv/1`.

Captured members must share an endpoint origin. That origin also binds the
sequence; raw members use the caller's explicitly selected endpoint. Submit
through `tmux_server:command/3` or `tmux_operation:start/3`.

Execution is not atomic. A failed member can leave a completed prefix, and
commands can wait or interleave with other work. The one-shot result contains
combined bounded stdout/stderr and native exit status, without per-member
completion attribution or rollback. Control-mode eligibility is separate.
`to_config/1` can serialize a sequence with the same origin-loss policy as
other configuration text.
""".
-spec sequence(nonempty_list(t())) -> {ok, t()} | {error, map()}.
sequence([_ | _] = Commands) -> sequence(Commands, 256, 0, 0, none, []);
sequence(_) -> {error, #{code => invalid_command, reason => invalid_command_list}}.

sequence([], _, _, _, _, Acc) -> {ok, {tmux_sequence, lists:reverse(Acc)}};
sequence([_ | _], 0, _, _, _, _) -> {error, #{code => command_limit}};
sequence([Command | Rest], Left, Words, Bytes, Origin, Acc) ->
    case Command of
        {tmux_sequence, _} -> {error, #{code => invalid_command, reason => nested_sequence}};
        _ ->
            maybe
                {ok, Valid} ?= validate(Command),
                Args = argv(Valid),
                Separator = case Acc of [] -> 0; _ -> 1 end,
                Count = Words + length(Args) + Separator,
                Size = Bytes + lists:sum([byte_size(A) + 3 || A <- Args]) + Separator * 4,
                ok ?= case Count =< 2041 andalso Size =< 32768 of
                    true -> ok;
                    false -> {error, #{code => command_limit}}
                end,
                Next = case provenance(Valid) of none -> none; #{origin := O} -> O end,
                {ok, Bound} ?= sequence_origin(Origin, Next),
                sequence(Rest, Left - 1, Count, Size, Bound, [Valid | Acc])
            end
    end;
sequence(_, _, _, _, _, _) ->
    {error, #{code => invalid_command, reason => invalid_command_list}}.

sequence_origin(none, Origin) -> {ok, Origin};
sequence_origin(Origin, none) -> {ok, Origin};
sequence_origin(Origin, Origin) -> {ok, Origin};
sequence_origin(_, _) -> {error, #{code => different_owner}}.

-doc """
Build a native `wait-for` command without I/O. Channels are nonempty NUL-free
binary names, subject to the command reservation in `raw/2`; neither shell nor
format expansion occurs. Submit through `tmux_operation:start/3` for a wait
that leaves the caller free, or through `tmux_server:command/3` to await it.

`signal` wakes current waiters. On an unlocked channel with no waiters or
pending wakeup, it retains one wakeup for a later wait. Signaling that channel
again before a wait can clear the pending state. Signals are neither counted
nor reliably coalesced events; send once per expected wait. Channel names are
shared by all clients of the server. Use separate names for signaling and
locking. `lock` acquires an advisory channel lock or waits
for an explicit `unlock`; a completed command client's exit does not release
its acquired lock. Unlocking an unlocked channel is a native command error.

Cancellation retires the library client. It does not undo a signal or release
a lock that may already have been acquired; an uncertain lock outcome needs
application coordination before another unlock. This is not an owned mutex.

```erlang
1> {ok, Signal} = tmux_command:wait_for(<<"build-ready">>, signal), ok.
ok
2> tmux_command:argv(Signal).
[<<"wait-for">>,<<"-S">>,<<"--">>,<<"build-ready">>]
```
""".
-spec wait_for(binary(), wait_action()) -> {ok, t()} | {error, map()}.
wait_for(Channel, Action) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Flags} ?= case Action of
            wait -> {ok, []};
            signal -> {ok, [<<"-S">>]};
            lock -> {ok, [<<"-L">>]};
            unlock -> {ok, [<<"-U">>]};
            _ -> {error, #{code => invalid_wait_action}}
        end,
        ok ?= case Channel of <<>> -> {error, #{code => invalid_channel}}; _ -> word(Channel) end,
        raw(<<"wait-for">>, Flags ++ [<<"--">>, Channel])
    end.

-doc """
Build configuration loading from stdin or one literal absolute path, without
I/O. `stdin` renders `source-file -`; supply configuration bytes in the
`stdin` option of `tmux_server:command/3` or `tmux_operation:start/3`. Those
APIs bound input to 256 KiB including their argument reservation.

Paths are NUL-free POSIX byte binaries. Glob metacharacters and backslashes
are escaped so only that filename is selected; format expansion is disabled.
The combined encoded path and flags must fit `raw/2` limits. The file is read
by tmux at execution time; this builder does not open it or bound its size.

`parse_only` requests native `-n` parsing without executing the configuration's
command list. `quiet` requests native `-q` missing-file suppression; it does
not suppress syntax or execution errors. Both default to false. Configuration
is trusted tmux code, with its own variable, directive and command semantics.
Parse-only is not a sandbox. Execution can partially change server state before
an error; cancellation cannot undo those effects. Completion does not prove
that background jobs launched by the configuration have finished.

```erlang
1> {ok, Source} = tmux_command:source_file(stdin, #{parse_only => true}), ok.
ok
2> tmux_command:argv(Source).
[<<"source-file">>,<<"-n">>,<<"--">>,<<"-">>]
```
""".
-spec source_file(source(), source_options()) -> {ok, t()} | {error, map()}.
source_file(Source, Options) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Flags} ?= tmux_args:options(Options,
            [{parse_only, flag, <<"-n">>}, {quiet, flag, <<"-q">>}]),
        {ok, Path} ?= source_path(Source),
        raw(<<"source-file">>, Flags ++ [<<"--">>, Path])
    end.

source_path(stdin) -> {ok, <<"-">>};
source_path(<<$/, _/binary>> = Path) ->
    maybe
        ok ?= word(Path),
        {ok, << <<(glob_byte(C))/binary>> || <<C>> <= Path >>}
    end;
source_path(_) -> {error, #{code => invalid_source_path}}.

glob_byte(C) when C =:= $*; C =:= $?; C =:= $[; C =:= $]; C =:= $\\ -> <<$\\, C>>;
glob_byte(C) -> <<C>>.

-doc """
Revalidate a command value at a submission boundary. Returns a compact
validated command or a tagged shape/argument/resource error, without I/O.
""".
-spec validate(term()) -> {ok, t()} | {error, map()}.
validate({tmux_command, Name, Arguments}) -> raw(Name, Arguments);
validate({tmux_sequence, Commands}) -> sequence(Commands);
validate({tmux_command, Name, Arguments, #{origin := Origin, kind := Kind} = Metadata})
  when map_size(Metadata) =:= 2 ->
    case generated(Kind, Origin, Arguments) of
        {ok, {tmux_command, Name, _, _}} = Valid -> Valid;
        {ok, _} -> {error, #{code => invalid_command}};
        Error -> Error
    end;
validate(_) -> {error, #{code => invalid_command}}.

-doc false.
-spec generated(session_rename | pane_resize, reference(), [binary()]) ->
    {ok, t()} | {error, map()}.
generated(Kind, Origin, Arguments) when is_reference(Origin) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Name} ?= case Kind of
            session_rename -> {ok, <<"rename-session">>};
            pane_resize -> {ok, <<"resize-pane">>};
            _ -> {error, #{code => invalid_command}}
        end,
        {ok, {tmux_command, Name, Words}} ?= raw(Name, Arguments),
        {ok, {tmux_command, Name, Words, #{origin => Origin, kind => Kind}}}
    end;
generated(_, _, _) -> {error, #{code => invalid_command}}.

%% Intent does not establish control eligibility; reply success and error
%% shapes require separate qualification before a control dispatcher admits it.
-doc false.
-spec provenance(t()) -> none |
    #{origin := reference(), kind := session_rename | pane_resize | sequence}.
provenance({tmux_command, _, _}) -> none;
provenance({tmux_command, _, _, Metadata}) -> Metadata;
provenance({tmux_sequence, Commands}) ->
    case [O || Command <- Commands, #{origin := O} <- [provenance(Command)]] of
        [] -> none;
        [Origin | _] -> #{origin => Origin, kind => sequence}
    end.

parts({tmux_command, Name, Arguments}) -> {Name, Arguments};
parts({tmux_command, Name, Arguments, _}) -> {Name, Arguments}.

-doc """
Render a validated command into executable argv, protecting trailing tmux
separators. Performs no I/O and raises for an invalid command value.
""".
-spec argv(t()) -> [binary()].
argv(Command) ->
    case validate(Command) of
        {ok, {tmux_sequence, Commands}} ->
            lists:append(lists:join([<<";">>], [argv(C) || C <- Commands]));
        {ok, Validated} ->
            {Name, Arguments} = parts(Validated),
            [Name | [escape_separator(Word) || Word <- Arguments]];
        {error, Detail} -> erlang:error({invalid_command, Detail}, none,
            [{error_info, #{module => tmux_error}}])
    end.

-doc """
Render validated commands as native configuration text, without I/O. Accepts
one command, a `sequence/1` value, or a nonempty flat list of at most 256
commands. Returns an ASCII
binary of at most 32 KiB, without a final newline. Validation uses `validate/1`;
escaping growth, command count and aggregate size can return `command_limit`.
Lists use native command separators between independently quoted commands.
Rendering does not execute them or provide atomic execution or rollback.
The text carries no origin token; executing serialized configuration requires
the caller to choose and validate its destination explicitly.

Each argument is doublequoted. Quote, backslash, dollar, tilde, control and
non-ASCII bytes use three-digit octal escapes. Empty arguments, semicolons,
newlines and non-UTF-8 byte values remain argument data. The lexer does not
expand their variables or tilde prefixes, strip newline indentation, or
interpret them as directives, comments or additional commands.

Protection covers one lexer pass. Native command-string arguments, including
`bind-key` and `set-hook` values, can be parsed again by the receiving command.
Render each inner command string separately for its own parse boundary.

This is tmux configuration syntax, separate from `argv/1` executable arguments
and shell quoting. Native commands still interpret their values and expand
formats as usual; `literal_format/2` handles that separate boundary when
literal format values are required. Load the text explicitly with
`source_file/2`, or store it through a native command that accepts configuration
text. The [configuration guide](configuration.md) uses this renderer with
explicit execution and completion signals.
""".
-spec to_config(t() | [t(), ...]) -> {ok, binary()} | {error, map()}.
to_config({tmux_sequence, Commands}) ->
    maybe
        {ok, {tmux_sequence, Valid}} ?= sequence(Commands),
        config_commands(Valid, 256, 0, [])
    end;
to_config([_ | _] = Commands) -> config_commands(Commands, 256, 0, []);
to_config(Command) -> config_command(Command).

config_command({tmux_sequence, _}) -> {error, #{code => invalid_command}};
config_command(Command) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Validated} ?= validate(Command),
        {Name, Arguments} = parts(Validated),
        Words = [Name | [config_word(Word) || Word <- Arguments]],
        Text = iolist_to_binary(lists:join(<<" ">>, Words)),
        case byte_size(Text) =< 32768 of
            true -> {ok, Text};
            false -> {error, #{code => command_limit}}
        end
    end.


config_commands([], _, _, Acc) ->
    {ok, iolist_to_binary(lists:join(<<" ; ">>, lists:reverse(Acc)))};
config_commands([_ | _], 0, _, _) -> {error, #{code => command_limit}};
config_commands([Command | Rest], Remaining, Bytes, Acc) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Text} ?= config_command(Command),
        Size = Bytes + byte_size(Text) + case Acc of [] -> 0; _ -> 3 end,
        case Size =< 32768 of
            true -> config_commands(Rest, Remaining - 1, Size, [Text | Acc]);
            false -> {error, #{code => command_limit}}
        end
    end;
config_commands(_, _, _, _) ->
    {error, #{code => invalid_command, reason => invalid_command_list}}.

config_word(Word) -> [<<$">>, [config_byte(Byte) || <<Byte>> <= Word], <<$">>].

config_byte(Byte) when Byte >= 32, Byte =< 126, Byte =/= $", Byte =/= $\\,
                       Byte =/= $$, Byte =/= $~ -> <<Byte>>;
config_byte(Byte) ->
    <<$\\, ($0 + (Byte bsr 6)), ($0 + ((Byte bsr 3) band 7)), ($0 + (Byte band 7))>>.

-doc """
Quote a complete literal argument for tmux format expansion. This does not
encode operands nested inside another format expression. Performs no I/O.
""".
-spec literal_format(binary()) -> {ok, binary()} | {error, map()}.
literal_format(Value) ->
    literal_format(Value, tmux).

-doc """
Quote a complete literal format argument. Mode tmux protects hash expansion;
mode time also protects strftime percent directives. Stored-name semantics
remain tmux's own. This handles one expansion pass, not a nested operand,
recursive expansion or later visual style rendering. Performs no I/O.

Hash runs before `[` stay unchanged because tmux preserves style-looking
prefixes for a separate drawing step. Other hashes are doubled. In time mode,
an argument containing percent bytes must fit tmux's 8191-byte strftime result
limit after hash encoding and before percent doubling; larger values return
`format_limit` with `time_bytes` and `max_bytes`. Arguments without percent
bytes skip that native time-expansion limit. The encoded 32 KiB command limit
still applies in either mode.
""".
-spec literal_format(binary(), tmux | time) -> {ok, binary()} | {error, map()}.
literal_format(Value, Mode) when Mode =:= tmux; Mode =:= time ->
    maybe
        ok ?= word(Value),
        Hashes = literal_hashes(Value),
        Encoded = case Mode of
            tmux -> Hashes;
            time -> binary:replace(Hashes, <<"%">>, <<"%%">>, [global])
        end,
        Time = Mode =:= time andalso binary:match(Value, <<"%">>) =/= nomatch,
        case {byte_size(Encoded) =< 32768, Time andalso byte_size(Hashes) > 8191} of
            {false, _} -> {error, #{code => command_limit}};
            {_, true} -> {error, #{code => format_limit, max_bytes => 8191,
                                  time_bytes => byte_size(Hashes)}};
            _ -> {ok, Encoded}
        end
    end;
literal_format(_, _) -> {error, #{code => invalid_format_mode}}.

literal_hashes(Value) ->
    case binary:match(Value, <<"#">>) of
        nomatch -> Value;
        _ -> iolist_to_binary(lists:reverse(literal_hashes(Value, [])))
    end.

literal_hashes(<<>>, Acc) -> Acc;
literal_hashes(<<$#, Rest/binary>>, Acc) ->
    {Count, Tail} = hash_run(Rest, 1),
    Size = case Tail of <<$[, _/binary>> -> Count; _ -> Count * 2 end,
    literal_hashes(Tail, [binary:copy(<<$#>>, Size) | Acc]);
literal_hashes(<<Byte, Rest/binary>>, Acc) -> literal_hashes(Rest, [Byte | Acc]).

hash_run(<<$#, Rest/binary>>, Count) -> hash_run(Rest, Count + 1);
hash_run(Tail, Count) -> {Count, Tail}.

-doc """
Render explicit executable argv, an explicitly requested shell command, or
default_shell. Singleton argv uses the installed helper's exec-only mode to
avoid tmux interpreting it as shell syntax. Performs no I/O.
""".
-spec launch(launch_spec()) ->
    {ok, [binary()]} | {error, map()}.
launch(default_shell) -> {ok, []};
launch(#{argv := [Executable]} = Spec) when map_size(Spec) =:= 1 ->
    maybe
        ok ?= executable(Executable),
        case code:priv_dir(libtmux_erlang) of
            {error, _} -> {error, #{code => application_unavailable}};
            Priv ->
                Path = filename:absname(filename:join(Priv, "tmux_owned_io")),
                Helper = unicode:characters_to_binary(Path),
                {ok, [Helper, <<"--exec-one">>, Executable]}
        end
    end;
launch(#{argv := [Executable, _ | _] = Arguments} = Spec) when map_size(Spec) =:= 1 ->
    maybe
        ok ?= executable(Executable),
        ok ?= words(Arguments, 2040, 0),
        {ok, Arguments}
    end;
launch(#{shell := Shell} = Spec) when map_size(Spec) =:= 1 ->
    maybe
        ok ?= word(Shell),
        {ok, [Shell]}
    end;
launch(_) -> {error, #{code => invalid_launch}}.

valid_name(<<First, Rest/binary>> = Name)
  when First >= $a, First =< $z, byte_size(Name) =< 128 ->
    valid_name_bytes(Rest);
valid_name(_) -> false.

valid_name_bytes(<<>>) -> true;
valid_name_bytes(<<C, Rest/binary>>) when (C >= $a andalso C =< $z) orelse C =:= $- ->
    valid_name_bytes(Rest);
valid_name_bytes(_) -> false.

word(Value) when is_binary(Value), byte_size(Value) =< 32768 ->
    case binary:match(Value, <<0>>) of
        nomatch -> ok;
        _ -> {error, #{code => invalid_argument}}
    end;
word(Value) when is_binary(Value) -> {error, #{code => command_limit}};
word(_) -> {error, #{code => invalid_argument}}.

words([], _, _) -> ok;
words([_ | _], 0, _) -> {error, #{code => command_limit}};
words([Value | Rest], Remaining, Size) ->
    maybe
        ok ?= word(Value),
        NewSize = Size + byte_size(Value) + 3,
        case NewSize =< 32768 of
            true -> words(Rest, Remaining - 1, NewSize);
            false -> {error, #{code => command_limit}}
        end
    end;
words(_, _, _) -> {error, #{code => invalid_argument}}.

executable(<<>>) -> {error, #{code => invalid_executable}};
executable(Value) -> word(Value).

compact(Bytes) ->
    case binary:referenced_byte_size(Bytes) =:= byte_size(Bytes) of
        true -> Bytes;
        false -> binary:copy(Bytes)
    end.

escape_separator(<<>>) -> <<>>;
escape_separator(Word) ->
    case binary:last(Word) of
        $; ->
            Prefix = binary:part(Word, 0, byte_size(Word) - 1),
            <<Prefix/binary, $\\, $;>>;
        _ -> Word
    end.

-module(tmux_control).
-moduledoc """
Own an explicit persistent tmux control attachment.

`attach/3` attaches to an existing session from `m:tmux_server` and verifies
the daemon identity on that connection. The caller owns its lifetime.
Attachment changes the session's attached-client count. The command client
uses no-output and ignore-size; -E skips attachment's environment update.
The library issues no session-option writes or session-creation commands.
Configured hooks and native lifetime policies can still change state,
including on failed attach or detachment. Those effects are not rolled back.
Command submission and terminal streaming are not yet exposed.

Use `close/1` before closing the parent endpoint. Parent closing, invalidation
or caller death requests retirement, but parent close alone does not prove
this client's exit. Control close and `status/1` report its native cleanup.
Neither detachment nor cancellation reverses remote effects. Application
shutdown alone is not a verified cleanup result.
""".
-behaviour(gen_server).
-export([attach/3, close/1, status/1]).
-export([start_link/4, init/1, handle_continue/2, handle_call/3, handle_cast/2,
         handle_info/2, terminate/2, format_status/1, send_request/2]).
-export_type([t/0, attach_options/0, state/0]).

-doc "A generation-bound connection handle. Passing it does not transfer lifetime ownership.".
-opaque t() :: {control, pid(), reference()}.
-doc "Finite attachment budget, including parent registration, exec and identity. Defaults to 2500 ms.".
-type attach_options() :: #{startup_timeout_ms => 1..600000}.
-doc """
Connection state, separate from command completion. complete proves native
client/helper retirement; pending and incomplete do not. Retained PIDs are
diagnostic observations, never permission to signal a process.
""".
-type state() :: #{phase := attaching | open | closing | closed,
    generation := reference(), owner := pid(), identity := unverified | same_connection,
    cleanup := pending | incomplete | complete, child_pid := none | pos_integer(),
    helper_pid := none | pos_integer(), cause := none | atom()}.

-doc """
Attach to an existing captured session from this exact endpoint origin.
Performs I/O and waits for a same-connection identity probe. Uses attach-session
with -E rather than creating a session or writing options. Configured hooks
may change state; failure does not reverse their effects. The control client
affects attached_count.
Unexpected hook-generated reply blocks fail attachment and retire the client.

An attachment timeout requests cleanup. If cleanup cannot be proved within
its finite deadline, the error includes a control handle for `close/1` recovery.
The supervised owner remains until native retirement. Close explicitly to
observe cleanup, including when the parent endpoint is already closed.
""".
-spec attach(tmux_server:t(), tmux_model:session(), attach_options()) ->
    {ok, t()} | {error, map()}.
attach(Server, Session, Options) ->
    Started = now_ms(),
    maybe
        {ok, Timeout} ?= options(Options),
        {ok, Origin, Target} ?= tmux_target:captured_target(session, Session),
        Generation = make_ref(),
        Config = #{origin => Origin, target => Target, deadline => Started + Timeout},
        Child = #{id => Generation, start => {?MODULE, start_link,
            [self(), Generation, Server, Config]}, restart => temporary, shutdown => 1000},
        try supervisor:start_child(tmux_sup, Child) of
            {ok, Pid} ->
                Control = {control, Pid, Generation},
                case request(Control, ready, max(0, Started + Timeout + 1000 - now_ms())) of
                    ok -> {ok, Control};
                    {error, Error} ->
                        gen_server:cast(Pid, {Generation, close}),
                        {error, Error#{control => Control}}
                end;
            {error, _} -> {error, #{code => control_unavailable, cleanup => complete}}
        catch
            exit:{noproc, _} -> {error, #{code => control_unavailable, cleanup => complete}};
            exit:_ -> {error, #{code => control_unavailable, cleanup => unverified}}
        end
    end.

-doc """
Retire this control client and its helper without issuing session or daemon
destruction commands. Native lifetime policies and detachment hooks may still
change state; cleanup does not reverse their effects. Returns ok only after
actual retirement. A finite cleanup failure leaves a supervised owner for
retry and observation.
Successful close is idempotent during the 60-second handle retention period.
""".
-spec close(t()) -> ok | {error, map()}.
close(Control) -> request(Control, close, 1000).

-doc """
Read retained connection state without a tmux command. Inspect cleanup rather
than inferring native exit from the Erlang owner's lifecycle. Closed handles
expire after 60 seconds and then return control_expired.
""".
-spec status(t()) -> {ok, state()} | {error, map()}.
status(Control) -> request(Control, status, 900).

request({control, Pid, Generation}, Kind, Timeout)
  when is_pid(Pid), is_reference(Generation) ->
    Tag = make_ref(),
    Request = gen_server:send_request(Pid, {Generation, Kind, Tag}),
    case gen_server:receive_response(Request, Timeout) of
        {reply, Reply} -> Reply;
        timeout ->
            gen_server:cast(Pid, {Generation, unwait, Tag}),
            Code = case Kind of close -> cleanup_incomplete; _ -> await_timeout end,
            {error, #{code => Code, cleanup => unverified}};
        {error, _} -> {error, #{code => control_expired, cleanup => unverified}}
    end;
request(_, _, _) -> {error, #{code => invalid_control}}.

-doc false.
-spec send_request(t(), retired) -> gen_server:request_id().
send_request({control, Pid, Generation}, retired) ->
    gen_server:send_request(Pid, {Generation, retired, make_ref()}).

-doc false.
-spec start_link(pid(), reference(), tmux_server:t(), map()) -> gen_server:start_ret().
start_link(Owner, Generation, Server, Config) ->
    gen_server:start_link(?MODULE, {Owner, Generation, Server, Config}, []).

-doc false.
-spec init({pid(), reference(), tmux_server:t(), map()}) ->
    {ok, map(), {continue, launch}}.
init({Owner, Generation, Server, Config}) ->
    {ok, #{owner => Owner, owner_monitor => monitor(process, Owner),
        generation => Generation, server => Server, config => Config, context => none,
        parent_monitor => none, watch => none, channel => none,
        requests => gen_server:reqids_new(), phase => attaching, startup => attachment,
        codec => tmux_control_codec:new(Generation), block => none, probe => none,
        write => none, child_pid => none, helper_pid => none,
        identity => unverified, cleanup => pending, cause => none,
        failure => none, diagnostics => <<>>, startup_bytes => 0,
        timer => none, close_timer => none, retention_timer => none, waiters => #{}},
        {continue, launch}}.

-doc false.
-spec handle_continue(launch, map()) -> {noreply, map()}.
handle_continue(launch, State) -> {noreply, launch(State)}.

-doc false.
-spec handle_call(term(), gen_server:from(), map()) -> {reply, term(), map()} | {noreply, map()}.
handle_call({Generation, status, _}, _, #{generation := Generation} = State) ->
    {reply, {ok, public_status(State)}, State};
handle_call({Generation, Kind, Tag}, From, #{generation := Generation} = State)
  when Kind =:= ready; Kind =:= close; Kind =:= retired ->
    Next = case Kind of close -> retire(closed, State); _ -> State end,
    case answer(Kind, Next) of
        pending -> add_waiter(Kind, Tag, From, Next);
        Reply -> {reply, Reply, Next}
    end;
handle_call(_, _, State) -> {reply, {error, #{code => invalid_control}}, State}.

-doc false.
-spec handle_cast(term(), map()) -> {noreply, map()}.
handle_cast({Generation, close}, #{generation := Generation} = State) ->
    {noreply, retire(closed, State)};
handle_cast({Generation, unwait, Tag}, #{generation := Generation} = State) ->
    {noreply, remove_waiter(Tag, State)};
handle_cast(_, State) -> {noreply, State}.

-doc false.
-spec handle_info(term(), map()) -> {noreply, map()} | {stop, normal, map()}.
handle_info({tmux_transport, Channel, {data, stdout, Sequence, Bytes}},
            #{channel := Channel} = State) ->
    Next = stdout(Bytes, State),
    case maps:get(phase, Next) of
        closing -> {noreply, Next};
        closed -> {noreply, Next};
        _ ->
            case tmux_transport:ack(Channel, stdout, Sequence) of
                ok -> {noreply, Next};
                {error, Error} -> {noreply, fail(Error, Next)}
            end
    end;
handle_info({tmux_transport, Channel, {data, stderr, Sequence, Bytes}},
            #{channel := Channel, diagnostics := Previous} = State) ->
    case byte_size(Previous) + byte_size(Bytes) =< 65536 of
        true ->
            Next = State#{diagnostics => <<Previous/binary, Bytes/binary>>},
            case tmux_transport:ack(Channel, stderr, Sequence) of
                ok -> {noreply, Next};
                {error, Error} -> {noreply, fail(Error, Next)}
            end;
        false -> {noreply, fail(#{code => control_diagnostic_limit}, State)}
    end;
handle_info({tmux_transport, Channel, {write_ack, Id, Size}},
            #{channel := Channel, write := {Id, Size}} = State) ->
    case tmux_transport:ack_write(Channel, Id) of
        ok -> {noreply, maybe_ready(State#{write => none})};
        {error, Error} -> {noreply, fail(Error, State)}
    end;
handle_info({tmux_transport, Channel, {eof, stdout}}, #{channel := Channel} = State) ->
    {noreply, fail(#{code => control_eof}, State)};
handle_info({tmux_server_closing, Parent, ParentGeneration, Watch, _},
            #{context := #{owner := Parent, generation := ParentGeneration}, watch := Watch} = State) ->
    {noreply, retire(parent_closed, State)};
handle_info({timeout, Timer, startup}, #{timer := Timer} = State) ->
    {noreply, fail(#{code => startup_timeout}, State#{timer => none})};
handle_info({timeout, Timer, cleanup}, #{close_timer := Timer} = State) ->
    {noreply, reply_waiters(State#{cleanup => incomplete, close_timer => none})};
handle_info({timeout, Timer, expire}, #{retention_timer := Timer, phase := closed} = State) ->
    {stop, normal, State};
handle_info({'DOWN', Ref, process, _, _}, #{owner_monitor := Ref} = State) ->
    {noreply, retire(owner_down, State)};
handle_info({'DOWN', Ref, process, _, _}, #{parent_monitor := Ref} = State) when is_reference(Ref) ->
    {noreply, retire(parent_down, State)};
handle_info(Message, State) ->
    case gen_server:check_response(Message, maps:get(requests, State), true) of
        {{reply, Reply}, Label, Requests} ->
            {noreply, native_reply(Label, Reply, State#{requests => Requests})};
        {{error, _}, _, Requests} ->
            {noreply, fail(#{code => channel_unavailable}, State#{requests => Requests})};
        _ -> {noreply, subscriber_down(Message, State)}
    end.

-doc false.
-spec terminate(term(), map()) -> ok.
terminate(_, #{channel := none}) -> ok;
terminate(_, #{channel := Channel}) -> tmux_transport:cancel_async(Channel).

-doc false.
-spec format_status(map()) -> map().
format_status(Status) ->
    maps:map(fun
        (state, State) -> public_status(State);
        (message, _) -> redacted;
        (reason, _) -> redacted;
        (_, Value) -> Value
    end, maps:without([log], Status)).

options(Options) when is_map(Options) ->
    Timeout = maps:get(startup_timeout_ms, Options, 2500),
    case maps:without([startup_timeout_ms], Options) =:= #{} andalso is_integer(Timeout, 1, 600000) of
        true -> {ok, Timeout};
        false -> {error, #{code => invalid_control_options}}
    end;
options(_) -> {error, #{code => invalid_control_options}}.

launch(#{server := Server, config := Config} = State) ->
    Remaining = maps:get(deadline, Config) - now_ms(),
    case Remaining > 0 andalso is_process_alive(maps:get(owner, State)) of
        false -> fail(#{code => startup_timeout}, State);
        true ->
            case tmux_server:watch_closing(Server, min(900, Remaining)) of
                {ok, Watch, Context} ->
                    Next = State#{watch => Watch, context => Context,
                        parent_monitor => monitor(process, maps:get(owner, Context))},
                    case maps:get(origin, Context) =:= maps:get(origin, Config) of
                        false -> fail(#{code => different_owner}, Next);
                        true -> launch_channel(Next)
                    end;
                {error, Error} -> fail(Error, State)
            end
    end.

launch_channel(#{context := #{config := Native}, config := Config} = State) ->
    Remaining = maps:get(deadline, Config) - now_ms(),
    case authorized(State) andalso Remaining > 0 of
        false -> fail(#{code => parent_closed}, State);
        true ->
            Flags = case tmux_version:at_least(maps:get(version, Native), {3, 6}) of
                true -> <<"no-output,ignore-size,no-detach-on-destroy">>;
                false -> <<"no-output,ignore-size">>
            end,
            Args = [<<"-u">>, <<"-C">>, <<"-N">>, <<"-S">>, maps:get(socket_path, Native),
                <<"attach-session">>, <<"-E">>, <<"-f">>, Flags, <<"-t">>, maps:get(target, Config)],
            case tmux_transport:start_channel(maps:get(executable, Native), Args,
                                              #{startup_timeout_ms => min(600000, Remaining)}) of
                {ok, Channel} ->
                    Requests = lists:foldl(fun(Kind, Acc) ->
                        gen_server:reqids_add(tmux_transport:send_request(Channel, Kind), Kind, Acc)
                    end, maps:get(requests, State), [started, await, retired]),
                    State#{channel => Channel,
                        requests => Requests, timer => erlang:start_timer(Remaining, self(), startup)};
                {error, Error} -> fail(Error, State)
            end
    end.

authorized(#{context := #{admission := Admission}, owner := Owner}) ->
    is_process_alive(Owner) andalso
        case tmux_admission:stats(Admission) of {ok, #{open := true}} -> true; _ -> false end;
authorized(_) -> false.

stdout(_, #{phase := Phase} = State) when Phase =:= closing; Phase =:= closed -> State;
stdout(Bytes, State) ->
    Used = maps:get(startup_bytes, State) + byte_size(Bytes),
    case maps:get(phase, State) =:= attaching andalso Used > 1048576 of
        true -> fail(#{code => control_startup_limit}, State);
        false ->
            Next = case maps:get(phase, State) of attaching -> State#{startup_bytes => Used}; _ -> State end,
            case tmux_control_codec:feed(maps:get(codec, State), Bytes) of
                {ok, Events, Codec} -> events(Events, Next#{codec => Codec});
                {error, Error, _} -> fail(Error, Next)
            end
    end.

events([], State) -> maybe_ready(State);
events(_, #{phase := Phase} = State) when Phase =:= closing; Phase =:= closed -> State;
events([Event | Rest], State) -> events(Rest, event(Event, State)).

event({notification, _, _}, State) -> State;
event({exit, _, _}, State) -> fail(#{code => control_exit}, State);
event({block_begin, #{flags := 0} = Guard}, #{startup := attachment, block := none} = State) ->
    State#{block => {Guard, <<>>}, startup => attachment_block};
event({block_begin, #{flags := 1} = Guard}, #{startup := probe, block := none} = State) ->
    State#{block => {Guard, <<>>}};
event({block_begin, _}, State) -> fail(#{code => unexpected_control_block}, State);
event({block_data, Guard, Bytes}, #{block := {Guard, Acc}} = State)
  when byte_size(Acc) + byte_size(Bytes) =< 128 ->
    State#{block => {Guard, <<Acc/binary, Bytes/binary>>}};
event({block_end, Guard, ok}, #{startup := attachment_block, block := {Guard, <<>>}} = State) ->
    probe(State#{block => none});
event({block_end, Guard, ok}, #{startup := probe, block := {Guard, Bytes}} = State) ->
    verify_probe(Bytes, State#{block => none});
event({block_end, _, error}, State) -> fail(#{code => control_attach_error}, State);
event(_, State) -> fail(#{code => unqualified_control_reply}, State).

probe(State) ->
    case {within_deadline(State), authorized(State)} of
        {false, _} -> fail(#{code => startup_timeout}, State);
        {_, false} -> fail(#{code => parent_closed}, State);
        {true, true} ->
            Nonce = binary:encode_hex(crypto:strong_rand_bytes(16), lowercase),
            Bytes = <<"display-message -p \"", Nonce/binary, ":#{pid}:#{version}\"\n">>,
            case tmux_transport:write(maps:get(channel, State), Bytes) of
                {ok, Id} -> State#{startup => probe, probe => Nonce, write => {Id, byte_size(Bytes)}};
                {error, Error} -> fail(Error, State)
            end
    end.

verify_probe(Bytes, #{context := #{config := Native}, probe := Nonce} = State) ->
    Prefix = <<Nonce/binary, $:>>, Size = byte_size(Prefix),
    case Bytes of
        <<Prefix:Size/binary, Rest/binary>> ->
            ExpectedPid = integer_to_binary(maps:get(server_pid, Native)),
            case binary:split(Rest, <<":">>, [global]) of
                [ExpectedPid, Version] ->
                    case {tmux_version:require(<<"tmux ", Version/binary>>),
                          tmux_identity:check(maps:get(identity, Native), maps:get(server_pid, Native))} of
                        {{ok, Parsed}, ok} ->
                            Known = maps:get(version, Native),
                            case maps:without([raw], Parsed) =:= maps:without([raw], Known) of
                                true -> State#{startup => verified, identity => same_connection};
                                false -> fail(#{code => stale_server}, State)
                            end;
                        _ -> fail(#{code => stale_server}, State)
                    end;
                _ -> fail(#{code => stale_server}, State)
            end;
        _ -> fail(#{code => invalid_control_identity}, State)
    end.

maybe_ready(#{phase := attaching, startup := verified, write := none,
              child_pid := Child} = State) when is_integer(Child) ->
    case {within_deadline(State), authorized(State)} of
        {true, true} ->
            cancel_timer(maps:get(timer, State)),
            reply_waiters(State#{phase => open, timer => none, probe => none, startup_bytes => 0});
        {false, _} -> fail(#{code => startup_timeout}, State);
        _ -> fail(#{code => parent_closed}, State)
    end;
maybe_ready(State) -> State.

within_deadline(#{config := #{deadline := Deadline}}) -> now_ms() < Deadline.

native_reply(started, {ok, Native}, State) ->
    maybe_ready(State#{child_pid => maps:get(child_pid, Native), helper_pid => maps:get(helper_pid, Native)});
native_reply(retired, {_, #{cleanup := complete}}, State) -> closed(State);
native_reply(await, {error, Error}, State) -> fail(Error, State);
native_reply(await, {ok, _}, State) -> retire(control_exit, State);
native_reply(_, {error, Error}, State) -> fail(Error, State);
native_reply(_, _, State) -> fail(#{code => invalid_channel_response}, State).

fail(_, #{phase := closed} = State) -> State;
fail(Error, State) ->
    Next = case maps:get(failure, State) of none -> State#{failure => maps:with([code], Error)}; _ -> State end,
    retire(maps:get(code, Error), Next).

retire(_, #{phase := Phase} = State) when Phase =:= closing; Phase =:= closed -> State;
retire(Cause, State) ->
    cancel_timer(maps:get(timer, State)),
    unwatch(State),
    Next = State#{phase => closing, cause => Cause, timer => none, watch => none,
        block => none, codec => none, probe => none, write => none},
    case maps:get(channel, Next) of
        none -> closed(Next);
        Channel ->
            ok = tmux_transport:cancel_async(Channel),
            Next#{close_timer => erlang:start_timer(900, self(), cleanup)}
    end.

unwatch(#{watch := Watch, context := #{owner := Pid, generation := Generation}})
  when is_reference(Watch) ->
    gen_server:cast(Pid, {Generation, unwatch_closing, Watch, self()});
unwatch(_) -> ok.

closed(#{phase := closed} = State) -> State;
closed(State) ->
    Next = retire(control_exit, State),
    cancel_timer(maps:get(close_timer, Next)),
    reply_waiters(Next#{phase => closed, cleanup => complete, close_timer => none,
        retention_timer => erlang:start_timer(60000, self(), expire)}).

answer(status, State) -> {ok, public_status(State)};
answer(ready, #{phase := open}) -> ok;
answer(ready, #{cleanup := Cleanup, failure := Failure, cause := Cause}) when Cleanup =/= pending ->
    Error = case Failure of none -> #{code => Cause}; _ -> Failure end,
    {error, Error#{cleanup => Cleanup}};
answer(close, #{cleanup := complete}) -> ok;
answer(close, #{cleanup := incomplete}) -> {error, #{code => cleanup_incomplete}};
answer(retired, #{cleanup := complete}) -> ok;
answer(_, _) -> pending.

add_waiter(Kind, Tag, {Pid, _} = From, #{waiters := Waiters} = State) when map_size(Waiters) < 16 ->
    {noreply, State#{waiters => Waiters#{Tag => {Kind, From, monitor(process, Pid)}}}};
add_waiter(_, _, _, State) -> {reply, {error, #{code => too_many_waiters}}, State}.

remove_waiter(Tag, #{waiters := Waiters} = State) ->
    case maps:take(Tag, Waiters) of
        {{_, _, Monitor}, Rest} -> demonitor(Monitor, [flush]), State#{waiters => Rest};
        error -> State
    end.

reply_waiters(State) ->
    maps:fold(fun(Tag, {Kind, From, _}, Acc) ->
        case answer(Kind, Acc) of
            pending -> Acc;
            Reply -> gen_server:reply(From, Reply), remove_waiter(Tag, Acc)
        end
    end, State, maps:get(waiters, State)).

subscriber_down({'DOWN', Ref, process, _, _}, State) ->
    maps:fold(fun(Tag, {_, _, Monitor}, Acc) ->
        case Ref =:= Monitor of true -> remove_waiter(Tag, Acc); false -> Acc end
    end, State, maps:get(waiters, State));
subscriber_down(_, State) -> State.

public_status(State) -> maps:with([phase, generation, owner, identity, cleanup,
                                 child_pid, helper_pid, cause], State).

cancel_timer(none) -> ok;
cancel_timer(Timer) -> _ = erlang:cancel_timer(Timer), ok.
now_ms() -> erlang:monotonic_time(millisecond).
