-module(tmux_filter).
-moduledoc """
Construct portable conditions and prepare them against captured values.

Local criteria use atom keys, binary text and schema-typed values. Fields and
operators conjoin. Boolean branches use 'and', 'or' and 'not'; relationships
use some/every/none/count or is/is_not. Validation examines the entire input
before evaluation. No function here performs tmux I/O. Use portable filters
with `tmux_select:where/2` or `tmux_query:where/2`; the [query
guide](querying.md) explains their different execution boundaries.

```erlang
1> Fields = #{id => <<"%1">>, current_command => <<"vim">>}, ok.
ok
2> {ok, P} = tmux_model:pane(Fields), S = tmux_select:from_list(pane, [P]), ok.
ok
3> R = #{pattern => <<"^(vim|nvim)$">>, dialect => portable_v1}, ok.
ok
4> tmux_select:size(tmux_select:where(#{current_command => #{regex => R}}, S)).
1
```

Wire version 1 uses generated camelCase field names, snake_case operators,
JSON null for known absence and {"base64": "..."} for byte operands. Byte
values never become text implicitly. Regex uses the restricted ASCII
portable_v1 dialect, absolute anchors and no flags. Preparation compiles each
pattern once. Non-ASCII subjects and exhausted match limits return errors.

Both input criteria and their normalized wire document must fit the grammar,
depth and byte limits. Resource errors can refer to the canonical wire path.
""".
-export([new/2, new_or_error/2, from_wire/2, to_wire/1, decode_json/1,
         entity/1, expression/1, requirements/1, prepare/2, predicate/1, matches/2,
         prepare_rows/3, conjoin/2]).
-export_type([t/0, prepared/0, expr/0, wire_document/0]).
-doc """
Portable normalized predicate data for one schema entity; contains no
executable state.
""".
-opaque t() :: {tmux_filter, 1, tmux_schema:entity(), expr()}.
-doc "Normalized data expressions with stable field IDs, used by internal planners; not the wire grammar.".
-type expr() :: {all | any, [expr()]} | {negate, expr()} |
    {field, binary(), atom(), term()} |
    {relation, binary(), atom(), expr()} |
    {count, binary(), [{atom(), term()}]}.
-doc """
A cached evaluator bound to one captured observation and schema context.
""".
-opaque prepared() :: tmux_filter_eval:t().
-doc """
Version-one JSON-compatible filter envelope with binary keys version, entity
and where. entity is the generated wire entity name; where contains Boolean,
field and relationship conditions. Version is the integer 1. Keys and
operators still require `from_wire/2` validation; the typespec alone does not
authorize arbitrary fields or unbounded external input.
""".
-type wire_document() :: #{binary() => json:encode_value()}.
-define(MAX_NODES, 1024).
-define(MAX_DEPTH, 32).
-define(MAX_MEMBERS, 256).

-doc """
Validate criteria or reuse an already normalized filter for the same entity.

```erlang
1> {ok, F} = tmux_filter:new(pane, #{width => #{gte => 120.0}}), ok.
ok
2> tmux_filter:new(pane, F) =:= {ok, F}.
true
3> tmux_filter:new(pane, #{active => #{contains => <<"yes">>}}).
{error,#{code => unsupported_operator,path => [active,contains],allowed => [equals,'not',in,not_in]}}
```
""".
-spec new(tmux_schema:entity(), map() | t()) -> {ok, t()} | {error, map()}.
new(Entity, {tmux_filter, 1, Entity, _} = Filter) -> {ok, Filter};
new(_Entity, {tmux_filter, _, _, _}) ->
    {error, #{code => wrong_filter_entity, path => []}};
new(Entity, Criteria) -> construct(Entity, Criteria, local, []).

-doc """
Construct a normalized portable filter, raising bad_filter on malformed
trusted criteria. Performs no tmux I/O. External input should use `new/2` or
`from_wire/2` for tagged validation errors.
""".
-spec new_or_error(tmux_schema:entity(), map() | t()) -> t().
new_or_error(Entity, Criteria) ->
    case new(Entity, Criteria) of
        {ok, Filter} -> Filter;
        {error, Detail} -> erlang:error({bad_filter, Detail}, none,
            [{error_info, #{module => tmux_error}}])
    end.

-doc """
Validate a versioned filter document using generated wire-name allowlists.
Rejects unknown fields, operators, wrong entity/version and resource limits.
No payload key becomes an atom; this does not execute a query.
""".
-spec from_wire(tmux_schema:entity(), term()) -> {ok, t()} | {error, map()}.
from_wire(Entity, Document) ->
    validated(fun() ->
        schema(Entity),
        object(Document, []),
        only_keys(Document, [<<"version">>, <<"entity">>, <<"where">>], []),
        case maps:get(<<"version">>, Document, missing) of
            1 -> ok;
            _ -> fail(unsupported_version, [<<"version">>])
        end,
        EntityName = tmux_schema_data:wire_entity(Entity),
        case maps:get(<<"entity">>, Document, missing) of
            EntityName -> ok;
            _ -> fail(wrong_filter_entity, [<<"entity">>])
        end,
        case maps:find(<<"where">>, Document) of
            {ok, Criteria} -> build(Entity, Criteria, wire, [<<"where">>]);
            error -> fail(required_field, [<<"where">>])
        end
    end).

-doc """
Export versioned JSON-compatible predicate data with generated wire names.
Byte operands use base64 objects and known absence uses JSON null. Functions,
compiled regexes and native record internals never enter this representation.
""".
-spec to_wire(t()) -> wire_document().
to_wire({tmux_filter, 1, Entity, Tree}) ->
    #{<<"version">> => 1, <<"entity">> => tmux_schema_data:wire_entity(Entity),
      <<"where">> => wire_node(Entity, Tree)}.

-doc """
Decode bounded external JSON with duplicate-key, trailing-input and depth
checks. Returns tagged errors with input paths. Parsing does not execute tmux
or choose application modules.
""".
-spec decode_json(binary()) -> {ok, json:decode_value()} | {error, map()}.
decode_json(Binary) -> tmux_json:decode(Binary).

-doc """
Return the schema entity this portable filter accepts, without I/O.
""".
-spec entity(t()) -> tmux_schema:entity().
entity({tmux_filter, 1, Entity, _}) -> Entity.

%% Internal planner boundary. The expression contains data and stable IDs only.
-doc false.
-spec expression(t()) -> expr().
expression({tmux_filter, 1, _, Tree}) -> Tree.

%% Internal composition of already validated data. Recheck canonical limits,
%% while preserving each relationship node's separate quantifier scope.
-doc false.
-spec conjoin(t(), t()) -> {ok, t()} | {error, map()}.
conjoin({tmux_filter, 1, Entity, Left}, {tmux_filter, 1, Entity, Right}) ->
    validated(fun() -> checked(Entity, conjunction([Left, Right])) end);
conjoin(_, _) -> {error, #{code => wrong_filter_entity, path => []}}.

-doc """
Derive every field and complete relationship needed for faithful evaluation.
The complete requirement set is checked before short-circuiting any row.
""".
-spec requirements(t()) -> [tmux_snapshot:requirement()].
requirements({tmux_filter, 1, Entity, Tree}) ->
    lists:usort([{collection, Entity} | needed(Entity, Tree)]).

-doc """
Bind a filter to one snapshot and check all required coverage first.

The prepared value can match only unmodified rows captured in that snapshot.
It remains usable after the endpoint closes. It cannot refresh observations.

```erlang
1> {ok, F} = tmux_filter:new(pane, #{width => #{gte => 80}}), ok.
ok
2> tmux_filter:requirements(F).
[{collection,pane},{field,pane,width}]
```
""".
-spec prepare(t(), tmux_snapshot:t()) -> {ok, prepared()} | {error, map()}.
prepare({tmux_filter, 1, Entity, Tree} = Filter, Snapshot) ->
    maybe
        ok ?= tmux_snapshot:require(requirements(Filter), Snapshot),
        tmux_filter_eval:prepare(Entity, Tree, {snapshot, Snapshot})
    end.

%% Selection construction validates rows and retains its original coverage.
%% Preparing a subset must not turn an unloaded field into a known value.
-doc false.
-spec prepare_rows(t(), [tmux_model:row()], map()) -> {ok, prepared()} | {error, map()}.
prepare_rows({tmux_filter, 1, Entity, Tree} = Filter, Rows, Coverage) ->
    Missing = [#{requirement => R, state => coverage_state(R, Entity, Coverage)}
               || R <- requirements(Filter),
                  not lists:member(coverage_state(R, Entity, Coverage), [complete, loaded])],
    case Missing of
        [] -> tmux_filter_eval:prepare(Entity, Tree, {rows, maps:from_keys(Rows, true)});
        _ -> {error, #{code => incomplete_snapshot, requirements => Missing}}
    end.

-doc """
Return a Boolean function bound to the prepared observation context.

Rows outside that context raise {prepared_context_mismatch, Detail}. Regex
evaluation errors raise {filter_evaluation_failed, Detail}. Use `matches/2`
for tagged errors. This does not run callbacks.
""".
-spec predicate(prepared()) -> fun((tmux_model:row()) -> boolean()).
predicate(Prepared) ->
    fun(Row) ->
        case matches(Prepared, Row) of
            {ok, Boolean} -> Boolean;
            {error, #{code := prepared_context_mismatch} = Detail} ->
                erlang:error({prepared_context_mismatch, Detail}, none,
                    [{error_info, #{module => tmux_error}}]);
            {error, Detail} -> erlang:error({filter_evaluation_failed, Detail}, none,
                [{error_info, #{module => tmux_error}}])
        end
    end.

-doc """
Evaluate an unmodified captured row against a prepared filter. Returns a
Boolean result or tagged context/regex resource error. It performs no tmux I/O
and never converts evaluation failure into a nonmatch.
""".
-spec matches(prepared(), tmux_model:row()) -> {ok, boolean()} | {error, map()}.
matches(Prepared, Row) -> tmux_filter_eval:matches(Prepared, Row).

construct(Entity, Criteria, Mode, Path) ->
    validated(fun() -> schema(Entity), build(Entity, Criteria, Mode, Path) end).

build(Entity, Criteria, Mode, Path) ->
    {Tree, _} = expression(Entity, Criteria, Mode, Path, 1, 0),
    checked(Entity, Tree).

checked(Entity, Tree) ->
    Filter = {tmux_filter, 1, Entity, Tree},
    %% Count the canonical expression/operand nodes without revalidating scalar
    %% values or importing the growing predicate through the wire grammar.
    _ = canonical_budget(Entity, Tree, [<<"where">>], 1, 0),
    Encoded = iolist_to_binary(json:encode(to_wire(Filter))),
    case tmux_json:decode(Encoded) of
        {ok, _} -> Filter;
        {error, Detail} -> fail(Detail)
    end.

validated(Function) ->
    try {ok, Function()}
    catch throw:{invalid_filter, Detail} -> {error, Detail}
    end.

schema(Entity) ->
    case tmux_schema:fields(Entity) of
        {ok, _} -> ok;
        {error, Detail} -> throw({invalid_filter, Detail})
    end.

expression(Entity, Input, Mode, Path, Depth, Count) ->
    Next = budget(Depth, Count, Path),
    object(Input, Path),
    {Nodes, Final} = entries(lists:sort(maps:to_list(Input)), Entity, Mode,
                           Path, Depth, Next, []),
    {conjunction(Nodes), Final}.

entries([], _, _, _, _, Count, Acc) -> {lists:reverse(Acc), Count};
entries([{Key, Value} | Rest], Entity, Mode, Path, Depth, Count, Acc) ->
    Here = Path ++ [Key],
    {Node, Next} = case resolve(Key, Mode, boolean_names()) of
        {ok, 'not'} ->
            {Child, N} = expression(Entity, Value, Mode, Here, Depth + 1, Count),
            {{negate, Child}, N};
        {ok, Boolean} ->
            {Children, N} = branches(Value, Entity, Mode, Here, Depth + 1, Count, 0, []),
            {case Boolean of 'and' -> conjunction(Children); 'or' -> {any, Children} end, N};
        error -> member(Entity, Key, Value, Mode, Here, Depth, Count)
    end,
    entries(Rest, Entity, Mode, Path, Depth, Next, [Node | Acc]).

branches([], _, _, _, _, Count, _, Acc) -> {lists:reverse(Acc), Count};
branches([Value | Rest], Entity, Mode, Path, Depth, Count, Index, Acc) ->
    {Node, Next} = expression(Entity, Value, Mode, Path ++ [Index], Depth, Count),
    branches(Rest, Entity, Mode, Path, Depth, Next, Index + 1, [Node | Acc]);
branches(_, _, _, Path, _, _, _, _) -> fail(expected_array, Path).

member(Entity, Key, Value, Mode, Path, Depth, Count) ->
    Fields = tmux_schema_data:fields(Entity),
    Relations = tmux_schema_data:relations(Entity),
    case {resolve_meta(Key, Mode, Fields), resolve_meta(Key, Mode, Relations)} of
        {{ok, _, Meta}, _} ->
            {Ops, Next} = operators(Value, Meta, Mode, Path, Depth, Count),
            {conjunction([{field, maps:get(stable, Meta), Op, V} || {Op, V} <- Ops]), Next};
        {error, {ok, _, Meta}} -> relation(Value, Meta, Mode, Path, Depth, Count);
        _ -> fail(#{code => unknown_field, path => Path,
                    allowed => names(Mode, maps:merge(Fields, Relations))})
    end.

operators(Input, Meta, Mode, Path, Depth, Count) ->
    IsBytes = Mode =:= wire andalso maps:get(type, Meta) =:= bytes andalso
              is_map(Input) andalso is_map_key(<<"base64">>, Input),
    case is_map(Input) andalso not IsBytes of
        true when map_size(Input) =:= 0 -> fail(empty_operators, Path);
        true -> scalar_ops(lists:sort(maps:to_list(Input)), Meta, Mode, Path, Depth, Count, []);
        false -> {[{equals, scalar(Meta, Input, Mode, Path)}], budget(Depth, Count, Path)}
    end.

scalar_ops([], _, _, _, _, Count, Acc) -> {lists:reverse(Acc), Count};
scalar_ops([{Key, Value} | Rest], Meta, Mode, Path, Depth, Count, Acc) ->
    Here = Path ++ [Key],
    Next = budget(Depth, Count, Here),
    Allowed = tmux_schema:operators(Meta),
    Op = operator(Key, Mode, Allowed, Here),
    Normalized = case Op of
        present when is_boolean(Value) -> Value;
        present -> fail(expected_boolean, Here);
        in -> members(Value, Meta, Mode, Here, 0, []);
        not_in -> members(Value, Meta, Mode, Here, 0, []);
        regex -> regex(Value, Mode, Here);
        equals -> scalar(Meta, Value, Mode, Here);
        'not' -> scalar(Meta, Value, Mode, Here);
        _ -> scalar(Meta#{nullable => false}, Value, Mode, Here)
    end,
    scalar_ops(Rest, Meta, Mode, Path, Depth, Next, [{Op, Normalized} | Acc]).

regex(Input, Mode, Path) ->
    object(Input, Path),
    Key = fun(Name) -> case Mode of local -> Name; wire -> atom_to_binary(Name) end end,
    PatternKey = Key(pattern),
    DialectKey = Key(dialect),
    FlagsKey = Key(flags),
    only_keys(Input, [PatternKey, DialectKey, FlagsKey], Path),
    Dialect = case Mode of local -> portable_v1; wire -> <<"portable_v1">> end,
    case maps:get(DialectKey, Input, missing) of
        Dialect -> ok;
        _ -> fail(unsupported_dialect, Path ++ [DialectKey])
    end,
    case maps:get(FlagsKey, Input, []) of
        [] -> ok;
        _ -> fail(unsupported_regex_flags, Path ++ [FlagsKey])
    end,
    Pattern = case maps:find(PatternKey, Input) of
        {ok, Value} -> Value;
        error -> fail(required_field, Path ++ [PatternKey])
    end,
    case tmux_regex:validate(Pattern) of
        {ok, _} -> #{pattern => Pattern, dialect => portable_v1, flags => []};
        {error, Detail} -> fail(Detail#{path => Path ++ [PatternKey]})
    end.

members([], _, _, _, _, Acc) -> lists:usort(Acc);
members([_ | _], _, _, Path, ?MAX_MEMBERS, _) -> fail(membership_limit, Path);
members([Value | Rest], Meta, Mode, Path, Index, Acc) ->
    Normalized = scalar(Meta, Value, Mode, Path ++ [Index]),
    members(Rest, Meta, Mode, Path, Index + 1, [Normalized | Acc]);
members(_, _, _, Path, _, _) -> fail(expected_array, Path).

scalar(Meta, Input, Mode, Path) ->
    Value = case {Mode, maps:get(type, Meta), Input} of
        {wire, _, null} -> none;
        {wire, bytes, #{<<"base64">> := Encoded} = Object} when map_size(Object) =:= 1,
                                                                     is_binary(Encoded) ->
            try
                Bytes = base64:decode(Encoded),
                case base64:encode(Bytes) of
                    Encoded -> Bytes;
                    _ -> fail(invalid_bytes, Path)
                end
            catch error:_ -> fail(invalid_bytes, Path)
            end;
        {wire, bytes, _} -> fail(invalid_bytes, Path);
        _ -> Input
    end,
    case tmux_schema:value(Meta, Value) of
        {ok, Normalized} -> Normalized;
        {error, Detail} -> fail(Detail#{path => Path})
    end.

relation(Input, #{kind := Kind, target := Target, stable := Stable}, Mode, Path, Depth, Count) ->
    object(Input, Path),
    case map_size(Input) of 0 -> fail(empty_operators, Path); _ -> ok end,
    Allowed = case Kind of many -> [some, every, none, count]; one -> [is, is_not] end,
    {Nodes, Final} = lists:mapfoldl(fun({Key, Value}, N) ->
        Here = Path ++ [Key],
        Next = budget(Depth, N, Here),
        Op = operator(Key, Mode, Allowed, Here),
        case Op of
            count ->
                {Ops, Last} = operators(Value, #{type => uint, nullable => false},
                                        Mode, Here, Depth + 1, Next),
                {{count, Stable, Ops}, Last};
            _ ->
                {Child, Last} = expression(Target, Value, Mode, Here, Depth + 1, Next),
                {{relation, Stable, Op, Child}, Last}
        end
    end, Count, lists:sort(maps:to_list(Input))),
    {conjunction(Nodes), Final}.

operator(Key, Mode, Allowed, Path) ->
    case resolve(Key, Mode, [{Op, atom_to_binary(Op)} || Op <- Allowed]) of
        {ok, Op} -> Op;
        error -> fail(#{code => unsupported_operator, path => Path,
                        allowed => case Mode of local -> Allowed;
                            wire -> [atom_to_binary(Op) || Op <- Allowed] end})
    end.

boolean_names() -> [{'and', <<"and">>}, {'or', <<"or">>}, {'not', <<"not">>}].
resolve(Key, local, Choices) ->
    case lists:keyfind(Key, 1, Choices) of {Key, _} -> {ok, Key}; false -> error end;
resolve(Key, wire, Choices) ->
    case lists:keyfind(Key, 2, Choices) of {Name, Key} -> {ok, Name}; false -> error end.
resolve_meta(Key, Mode, Items) ->
    case resolve(Key, Mode, [{Name, maps:get(wire, M)} || {Name, M} <- maps:to_list(Items)]) of
        {ok, Name} -> {ok, Name, maps:get(Name, Items)};
        error -> error
    end.
names(local, Items) -> lists:sort(maps:keys(Items));
names(wire, Items) -> lists:sort([maps:get(wire, M) || M <- maps:values(Items)]).

object(Value, _) when is_map(Value) -> ok;
object(_, Path) -> fail(expected_object, Path).
only_keys(Map, Allowed, Path) ->
    case lists:sort(maps:keys(maps:without(Allowed, Map))) of
        [] -> ok;
        [Key | _] -> fail(#{code => unknown_field, path => Path ++ [Key], allowed => Allowed})
    end.
budget(Depth, _, Path) when Depth > ?MAX_DEPTH -> fail(depth_limit, Path);
budget(_, Count, Path) when Count >= ?MAX_NODES -> fail(expression_limit, Path);
budget(_, Count, _) -> Count + 1.
conjunction(Nodes) ->
    Flat = lists:append([case Node of {all, Children} -> Children; _ -> [Node] end
                         || Node <- Nodes]),
    case Flat of [Only] -> Only; _ -> {all, Flat} end.

canonical_budget(Entity, Tree, Path, Depth, Count) ->
    Next = budget(Depth, Count, Path),
    case Tree of
        {Kind, Children} when Kind =:= all; Kind =:= any ->
            Key = case Kind of all -> <<"and">>; any -> <<"or">> end,
            lists:foldl(fun({Index, Child}, N) ->
                canonical_budget(Entity, Child, Path ++ [Key, Index], Depth + 1, N)
            end, Next, lists:enumerate(0, Children));
        {negate, Child} ->
            canonical_budget(Entity, Child, Path ++ [<<"not">>], Depth + 1, Next);
        {field, Stable, Op, _Value} ->
            {_, #{wire := Wire}} = metadata(Stable, tmux_schema_data:fields(Entity)),
            budget(Depth, Next, Path ++ [Wire, atom_to_binary(Op)]);
        {relation, Stable, Op, Child} ->
            {_, #{wire := Wire, target := Target}} =
                metadata(Stable, tmux_schema_data:relations(Entity)),
            Here = Path ++ [Wire, atom_to_binary(Op)],
            canonical_budget(Target, Child, Here, Depth + 1, budget(Depth, Next, Here));
        {count, Stable, Ops} ->
            {_, #{wire := Wire}} = metadata(Stable, tmux_schema_data:relations(Entity)),
            Here = Path ++ [Wire, <<"count">>],
            lists:foldl(fun({Op, _}, N) ->
                budget(Depth + 1, N, Here ++ [atom_to_binary(Op)])
            end, budget(Depth, Next, Here), Ops)
    end.
-spec fail(atom(), [term()]) -> no_return().
fail(Code, Path) -> fail(#{code => Code, path => Path}).
-spec fail(map()) -> no_return().
fail(Detail) -> throw({invalid_filter, Detail}).

metadata(Stable, Items) ->
    [{Name, Meta}] = [{N, M} || {N, M = #{stable := S}} <- maps:to_list(Items), S =:= Stable],
    {Name, Meta}.

needed(Entity, {Kind, Nodes}) when Kind =:= all; Kind =:= any ->
    lists:append([needed(Entity, Node) || Node <- Nodes]);
needed(Entity, {negate, Node}) -> needed(Entity, Node);
needed(Entity, {field, Stable, _, _}) ->
    {Name, _} = metadata(Stable, tmux_schema_data:fields(Entity)),
    [{field, Entity, Name}];
needed(Entity, {relation, Stable, _, Child}) ->
    {Name, #{target := Target}} = metadata(Stable, tmux_schema_data:relations(Entity)),
    [{relation, Entity, Name}, {collection, Target} | needed(Target, Child)];
needed(Entity, {count, Stable, _}) ->
    {Name, #{target := Target}} = metadata(Stable, tmux_schema_data:relations(Entity)),
    [{relation, Entity, Name}, {collection, Target}].

coverage_state({collection, Entity}, Entity, _) -> complete;
coverage_state({field, Entity, Field}, Entity, Coverage) -> maps:get(Field, Coverage);
coverage_state(_, _, _) -> not_loaded.

wire_node(Entity, {Kind, Children}) when Kind =:= all; Kind =:= any ->
    Key = case Kind of all -> <<"and">>; any -> <<"or">> end,
    #{Key => [wire_node(Entity, Child) || Child <- Children]};
wire_node(Entity, {negate, Child}) -> #{<<"not">> => wire_node(Entity, Child)};
wire_node(Entity, {field, Stable, Op, Value}) ->
    {_, Meta} = metadata(Stable, tmux_schema_data:fields(Entity)),
    #{maps:get(wire, Meta) => #{atom_to_binary(Op) => wire_value(Op, Value, Meta)}};
wire_node(Entity, {relation, Stable, Op, Child}) ->
    {_, #{target := Target, wire := Wire}} = metadata(Stable, tmux_schema_data:relations(Entity)),
    #{Wire => #{atom_to_binary(Op) => wire_node(Target, Child)}};
wire_node(Entity, {count, Stable, Ops}) ->
    {_, #{wire := Wire}} = metadata(Stable, tmux_schema_data:relations(Entity)),
    #{Wire => #{<<"count">> => maps:from_list([{atom_to_binary(Op), Value} || {Op, Value} <- Ops])}}.

wire_value(Op, Values, Meta) when Op =:= in; Op =:= not_in ->
    [wire_scalar(Value, Meta) || Value <- Values];
wire_value(present, Value, _) -> Value;
wire_value(regex, #{pattern := Pattern, dialect := portable_v1, flags := []}, _) ->
    #{<<"pattern">> => Pattern, <<"dialect">> => <<"portable_v1">>, <<"flags">> => []};
wire_value(_, Value, Meta) -> wire_scalar(Value, Meta).
wire_scalar(none, _) -> null;
wire_scalar(Value, #{type := bytes}) -> #{<<"base64">> => base64:encode(Value)};
wire_scalar(Value, _) -> Value.

-module(tmux_hook).
-moduledoc """
Store builtin hook commands and run them in an explicit observed context.

`set/3` replaces one indexed entry. `append/3` uses tmux's first vacant index;
`clear/2` leaves an empty local array and `unset/2` restores inheritance.
`get/3` reads local values unless inheritance is requested. Commands are
`t:tmux_command:t/0` values, rendered by `tmux_command:to_config/1` before tmux
parses and stores them. A successful write confirms registration, while later
hook effects need their own completion evidence.

Table scope and execution context are separate. `run/2` selects a session,
checked window link or checked pane/link pair. Physical windows can belong to
several sessions; a link preserves the chosen session and index. Preflight and
dispatch are separate observations, with no atomic compare-and-act guarantee.
Known restarts and closed owners invalidate references. Captured rows never
refresh during these actions.

Names and table scopes use the exact source-derived version catalogue from
`tmux_option:catalogue/1`. User options, prefixes and aliases are rejected.
The native custom-event and monitor interfaces are outside this API. Deliberate
raw integration remains available through `tmux_command:raw/2`. Calls perform
I/O after validation and never retry uncertain mutations. The
[hook guide](hooks.md) demonstrates registration and an effect acknowledgement.
""".
-export([get/3, set/3, append/3, clear/2, unset/2, run/2]).
-export_type([scope/0, context/0, commands/0, value/0]).

-doc """
A registered local table or explicit global session/window defaults; see
`t:tmux_option:scope/0`.
""".
-type scope() :: tmux_model:session() | tmux_model:window() | tmux_model:pane() |
    {session_defaults | window_defaults, tmux_server:t()}.
-doc """
A session's current context, one observed membership, or a pane in that
membership.
""".
-type context() :: tmux_model:session() | tmux_model:window_link() |
    {pane, tmux_model:pane(), tmux_model:window_link()}.
-doc """
One validated command or a nonempty list; at most 256 commands and 32 KiB
rendered text.
""".
-type commands() :: tmux_command:t() | [tmux_command:t(), ...].
-doc """
Canonical native command-list text, or a sparse map of indexes to that text.
""".
-type value() :: binary() | #{non_neg_integer() => binary()}.

-doc """
Read a builtin hook array or indexed entry. Options follow
`t:tmux_option:read_options/0`: local-only by default, inherit = true follows
its parent tables. Missing local arrays or entries return none; an empty local
array returns {ok, #{}} and masks inheritance.

Values are tmux's command-list serialization, including its quoting and escape
sequences. They are neither the original input text nor individual decoded
arguments. Reading does not execute them. Use `set/3` for validated command
values and `unset/2` to restore inheritance. Performs I/O and preserves backend
errors; a vanished target is not an absent hook.
""".
-spec get(scope(), tmux_option:key(), tmux_option:read_options()) ->
    {ok, value()} | none | {error, map()}.
get(Scope, Key, Options) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Flags} ?= tmux_args:options(Options, [{inherit, flag, <<"-A">>}]),
        {ok, Server, ScopeArgs, Name, Index, Meta} ?=
            tmux_option_scope:prepare(Scope, Key, read, hook),
        {ok, Version} ?= tmux_server:version(Server),
        {ok, Literal} ?= tmux_command:literal_format(Name),
        {ok, #{stdout := Output}} ?= tmux_target:run(Server, <<"show-options">>,
            ScopeArgs ++ Flags ++ [<<"-H">>, <<"--">>, Literal]),
        case tmux_option_codec:decode(Name, Output, Meta, Version) of
            {ok, Entries} when is_map(Entries), Index =/= none ->
                case maps:find(Index, Entries) of
                    {ok, Value} -> {ok, Value};
                    error -> none
                end;
            Result -> Result
        end
    end.

-doc """
Replace one {Name, Index} entry with validated command values. An explicit
index is required; other entries remain. Indexes range from zero to
2147483647. The rendered command text is bounded before dispatch. Native
commands still interpret their arguments and formats when the hook later runs.
Use `append/3` for native vacant-index selection and `clear/2` to mask inherited
hooks with an empty local array.

Performs I/O. tmux parses commands before replacing an existing entry, but a
failed first write can already create an empty local override. Registration
and later execution are separate; this call promises no transaction, rollback
or completion of future effects.
""".
-spec set(scope(), {binary(), non_neg_integer()}, commands()) ->
    {ok, tmux_operation:completed()} | {error, tmux_operation:failure()}.
set(Scope, Key, Commands) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Text} ?= body(Commands),
        {ok, Server, Flags, Name, Index, _} ?=
            tmux_option_scope:prepare(Scope, Key, write, hook),
        store(Server, Flags, tmux_option_scope:indexed(Name, Index), Text)
    end.

-doc """
Store commands at tmux's first vacant local index for the unindexed name.
A new local array starts independently of inherited entries; this does not
copy the parent's array. The command result does not report the chosen index;
`get/3` observes current entries separately. Performs I/O with the parsing and
unknown-outcome semantics of `set/3`.
""".
-spec append(scope(), binary(), commands()) ->
    {ok, tmux_operation:completed()} | {error, tmux_operation:failure()}.
append(Scope, Name0, Commands) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Name} ?= name(Name0),
        {ok, Text} ?= body(Commands),
        {ok, Server, Flags, Name, none, _} ?=
            tmux_option_scope:prepare(Scope, Name, append, hook),
        store(Server, Flags ++ [<<"-a">>], Name, Text)
    end.

-doc """
Leave an empty local hook array, masking inherited entries. This differs
from `unset/2`, which restores inheritance. Global clear empties that defaults
table. Performs I/O; existing effects already queued by tmux are not cancelled.
""".
-spec clear(scope(), binary()) ->
    {ok, tmux_operation:completed()} | {error, tmux_operation:failure()}.
clear(Scope, Name0) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Name} ?= name(Name0),
        {ok, Server, Flags, Name, none, _} ?=
            tmux_option_scope:prepare(Scope, Name, clear, hook),
        store(Server, Flags, Name, <<>>)
    end.

-doc """
Remove one indexed entry or the whole local array. Removing an entry leaves
its local array, possibly empty. Removing the whole array restores inheritance;
unsetting a global builtin resets its native default. Missing local values are
a successful native no-op. Performs I/O; queued hook effects are unaffected.
""".
-spec unset(scope(), tmux_option:key()) ->
    {ok, tmux_operation:completed()} | {error, tmux_operation:failure()}.
unset(Scope, Key) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Server, Flags, Name, Index, _} ?=
            tmux_option_scope:prepare(Scope, Key, unset, hook),
        {ok, Literal} ?= tmux_command:literal_format(tmux_option_scope:indexed(Name, Index)),
        tmux_target:run(Server, <<"set-hook">>, Flags ++ [<<"-u">>, <<"--">>, Literal])
    end.

-doc """
Request native set-hook -R in the explicit `t:context/0`. tmux resolves the
hook through that context's effective tables; global table flags do not select
a separate execution scope. A session uses its current window and pane. A
window link fixes the observed session/index and expected physical window;
a pane context additionally checks that pane's observed parent.

Performs I/O. The result is the native command outcome, not an acknowledgement
of background work launched by its commands. A missing or empty effective hook
can succeed without effects. Wait on an application completion condition when
effects matter. Existence and membership checks precede dispatch. If the
target disappears after preflight, tmux can still fall back to another
context. This is not atomic compare-and-act. Use fresh links after known
topology changes.
""".
-spec run(context(), binary()) ->
    {ok, tmux_operation:completed()} | {error, tmux_operation:failure()}.
run(Context, Name0) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Name} ?= name(Name0),
        {ok, Server, Target} ?= context(Context),
        {ok, Version} ?= tmux_server:version(Server),
        {ok, _} ?= tmux_option:describe(Version, Name),
        tmux_target:run(Server, <<"set-hook">>,
            [<<"-R">>, <<"-t">>, Target, <<"--">>, Name])
    end.

store(Server, Flags, Name, Text) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Literal} ?= tmux_command:literal_format(Name),
        tmux_target:run(Server, <<"set-hook">>, Flags ++ [<<"--">>, Literal, Text])
    end.

name(Name) when is_binary(Name) ->
    case tmux_option_scope:key(Name) of
        {ok, Name, none} ->
            case tmux_option_data:variants(Name) of
                [] -> {error, #{code => unknown_tmux_option, name => Name}};
                Variants ->
                    case lists:any(fun({_, Meta}) -> maps:get(hook, Meta) end, Variants) of
                        true -> {ok, Name};
                        false -> {error, #{code => not_a_hook}}
                    end
            end;
        _ -> {error, #{code => invalid_hook_name}}
    end;
name(_) -> {error, #{code => invalid_hook_name}}.

body([]) -> {error, #{code => invalid_hook_commands}};
body(Commands) ->
    case tmux_command:to_config(Commands) of
        {error, #{code := invalid_command, reason := invalid_command_list}} ->
            {error, #{code => invalid_hook_commands}};
        Result -> Result
    end.

context({pane, Pane, Link}) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Server} ?= tmux_target:same_owner(pane, Pane, window_link, Link),
        {ok, Target} ?= tmux_target:linked_pane(Server, Pane, Link),
        {ok, Server, Target}
    end;
context(Row) ->
    case tmux_model:validate(Row) of
        {ok, Valid} -> context_row(tmux_model:entity(Valid), Valid);
        _ -> {error, #{code => invalid_hook_context}}
    end.

context_row(session, Row) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Server, Target} ?= tmux_target:resolve(session, Row),
        {ok, _} ?= tmux_session:get(Server, tmux_model:get(id, Row)),
        {ok, Server, Target}
    end;
context_row(window_link, Link) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Server} ?= tmux_target:owner(window_link, Link),
        {ok, _, Target} ?= tmux_window_link:check(Server, Link),
        {ok, Server, Target}
    end;
context_row(_, _) -> {error, #{code => invalid_hook_context}}.

-module(tmux_identity).
-moduledoc """
Observe a Linux process incarnation using its PID, boot ID and start ticks.

```erlang
1> Pid = list_to_integer(os:getpid()), ok.
ok
2> {ok, Identity} = tmux_identity:observe(Pid), ok.
ok
3> tmux_identity:check(Identity, Pid).
ok
```

A successful check is an observation. It neither reserves a PID nor pins a
tmux connection, and it never authorizes signalling a process. Endpoint owners
in `m:tmux_server` compare the PID returned by the current connection as well.
A server can still change between this check and a later one-shot command.

Use `fingerprint/1` to compare captured incarnations across endpoint handles
or persist that comparison in a plan. It performs no process observation;
the key grants neither liveness nor permission to act.
""".
-export([observe/1, check/2, fingerprint/1]).
-export_type([t/0, fingerprint/0]).

-doc """
Observed Linux PID, boot identity and process-start token. It does not pin a
connection.
""".
-opaque t() :: {process_identity, pos_integer(), binary(), non_neg_integer()}.

-doc """
Versioned SHA-256 comparison key for a captured Linux process incarnation.
The linux-v1 prefix identifies the canonical encoding, independent of Erlang
term serialization. Keys compare identity observations, not endpoint ownership
or current liveness. They are identifiers, not authentication tokens.
""".
-type fingerprint() :: binary().

-doc """
Derive a portable `t:fingerprint/0` from a captured identity without I/O.

The key includes PID, boot ID and process-start ticks. Reconnecting to the same
process preserves it; changing any component changes it. The encoding is
versioned for persisted plans. Use `check/2` for a fresh process observation.
Malformed identity terms return invalid_identity before hashing.

```erlang
1> {ok, I} = tmux_identity:observe(list_to_integer(os:getpid())), ok.
ok
2> {ok, Key} = tmux_identity:fingerprint(I), ok.
ok
3> byte_size(Key).
73
```
""".
-spec fingerprint(t()) ->
    {ok, fingerprint()} | {error, #{code := invalid_identity}}.
fingerprint({process_identity, Pid, Boot, Started})
  when is_integer(Pid, 1, 2147483647), is_binary(Boot),
       is_integer(Started, 0, 18446744073709551615) ->
    case valid_boot_id(Boot) of
        true ->
            Digest = crypto:hash(sha256,
                [<<"libtmux-erlang-incarnation", 0, "1", 0>>,
                 integer_to_binary(Pid), <<0>>, Boot, <<0>>,
                 integer_to_binary(Started)]),
            {ok, <<"linux-v1:",
                (binary:encode_hex(Digest, lowercase))/binary>>};
        false -> {error, #{code => invalid_identity}}
    end;
fingerprint(_) -> {error, #{code => invalid_identity}}.

-doc """
Observe a Linux PID incarnation without signalling it. Returns a tagged error
if the process cannot be identified; this performs local operating-system I/O.
""".
-spec observe(pos_integer()) -> {ok, t()} | {error, map()}.
observe(Pid) when is_integer(Pid, 1, 2147483647) ->
    case os:type() of
        {unix, linux} -> observe_linux(Pid);
        _ -> {error, #{code => unsupported_platform}}
    end;
observe(_) -> {error, #{code => invalid_pid}}.

-doc """
Re-observe the PID and compare its incarnation token. A successful result is a
momentary observation, not ownership, permission to signal, or a
same-connection guarantee.
""".
-spec check(t(), pos_integer()) -> ok | {error, map()}.
check({process_identity, Pid, Boot, Started} = Identity, ObservedPid)
  when is_integer(Pid, 1, 2147483647), is_integer(ObservedPid, 1, 2147483647),
       is_binary(Boot), is_integer(Started, 0, 18446744073709551615) ->
    case valid_boot_id(Boot) of
        false -> {error, #{code => invalid_identity}};
        true when Pid =/= ObservedPid -> {error, #{code => stale_server}};
        true ->
            case observe(Pid) of
                {ok, Identity} -> ok;
                {ok, _} -> {error, #{code => stale_server}};
                {error, #{code := target_gone}} -> {error, #{code => stale_server}};
                Error -> Error
            end
    end;
check(_, _) -> {error, #{code => invalid_identity}}.

observe_linux(Pid) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Stat} ?= read_bounded("/proc/" ++ integer_to_list(Pid) ++ "/stat", 4096),
        {ok, Started} ?= start_ticks(Pid, Stat),
        {ok, RawBoot} ?= boot_file(),
        Boot = string:trim(RawBoot),
        case valid_boot_id(Boot) of
            true -> {ok, {process_identity, Pid, Boot, Started}};
            false -> {error, #{code => identity_unavailable, reason => malformed_boot_id}}
        end
    end.

boot_file() ->
    case read_bounded("/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id", 64) of
        {ok, Bytes} -> {ok, Bytes};
        {error, Detail} -> {error, Detail#{code => identity_unavailable, resource => boot_id}}
    end.

read_bounded(Path, Limit) ->
    case file:open(Path, [read, binary, raw]) of
        {ok, File} ->
            try
                case file:read(File, Limit + 1) of
                    {ok, Data} when byte_size(Data) =< Limit -> {ok, Data};
                    {ok, _} -> {error, #{code => identity_unavailable, reason => oversized_proc_file}};
                    eof -> {error, #{code => target_gone}};
                    {error, Reason} -> file_error(Reason)
                end
            after ok = file:close(File)
            end;
        {error, Reason} -> file_error(Reason)
    end.

file_error(enoent) -> {error, #{code => target_gone}};
file_error(esrch) -> {error, #{code => target_gone}};
file_error(Reason) -> {error, #{code => identity_unavailable, reason => Reason}}.

start_ticks(Pid, Stat) ->
    Prefix = <<(integer_to_binary(Pid))/binary, " (">>,
    Size = byte_size(Prefix),
    case Stat of
        <<Prefix:Size/binary, Rest/binary>> -> parse_stat_tail(Rest);
        _ -> {error, #{code => identity_unavailable, reason => malformed_proc_stat}}
    end.

parse_stat_tail(Rest) ->
    case binary:matches(Rest, <<") ">>) of
        [] -> {error, #{code => identity_unavailable, reason => malformed_proc_stat}};
        Matches ->
            %% comm may itself contain spaces, newlines and closing parentheses.
            {Position, 2} = lists:last(Matches),
            Tail = binary:part(Rest, Position + 2, byte_size(Rest) - Position - 2),
            Fields = binary:split(Tail, <<" ">>, [global]),
            parse_fields(Fields)
    end.

parse_fields([State | _]) when State =:= <<"Z">>; State =:= <<"X">>; State =:= <<"x">> ->
    {error, #{code => target_gone}};
parse_fields(Fields) when length(Fields) >= 20 ->
    Start = lists:nth(20, Fields),
    case decimal(Start) of
        true ->
            Ticks = binary_to_integer(Start),
            case Ticks =< 18446744073709551615 of
                true -> {ok, Ticks};
                false -> {error, #{code => identity_unavailable, reason => malformed_proc_stat}}
            end;
        false -> {error, #{code => identity_unavailable, reason => malformed_proc_stat}}
    end;
parse_fields(_) -> {error, #{code => identity_unavailable, reason => malformed_proc_stat}}.

decimal(<<>>) -> false;
decimal(Bytes) -> decimal_tail(Bytes).
decimal_tail(<<>>) -> true;
decimal_tail(<<C, Rest/binary>>) when C >= $0, C =< $9 -> decimal_tail(Rest);
decimal_tail(_) -> false.

valid_boot_id(<<A:8/binary, $-, B:4/binary, $-, C:4/binary, $-, D:4/binary, $-, E:12/binary>>) ->
    hex(<<A/binary, B/binary, C/binary, D/binary, E/binary>>);
valid_boot_id(_) -> false.

hex(<<>>) -> true;
hex(<<C, Rest/binary>>) when (C >= $0 andalso C =< $9) orelse (C >= $a andalso C =< $f) ->
    hex(Rest);
hex(_) -> false.

-module(tmux_json).
-moduledoc """
Decode bounded JSON using OTP's `m:json` parser and binary object keys.

Documents are limited to 256 KiB before parsing and 32 nested containers
during parsing. Duplicate keys are rejected before overwriting values, even
when different escapes spell the same key. Trailing input is rejected. Numbers
stay in the shared exact integer range. Integral decimal tokens are converted
exactly; fractional tokens that round to integers are rejected. Field
validation decides whether a remaining float is permitted. Syntax and resource
errors have a root path; duplicate-key errors retain their complete document
path. Use `tmux_filter:from_wire/2` to validate decoded filter data.
""".
-export([decode/1]).
-define(MAX_BYTES, 262144).
-define(MAX_DEPTH, 32).
-define(MAX_INTEGER, 9007199254740991).

-doc """
Return a decoded value or a structured error without creating payload atoms.

```erlang
1> tmux_json:decode(<<"{\"a\": [1, true, null]}">>).
{ok,#{<<"a">> => [1,true,null]}}
2> tmux_json:decode(<<"{\"a\": {\"x\": 1, \"x\": 2}}">>).
{error,#{code => duplicate_key,path => [<<"a">>,<<"x">>]}}
3> tmux_json:decode(<<"[] []">>).
{error,#{code => trailing_input,path => []}}
```
""".
-spec decode(binary()) -> {ok, json:decode_value()} | {error, map()}.
decode(Binary) when is_binary(Binary), byte_size(Binary) > ?MAX_BYTES ->
    {error, #{code => document_limit, path => [], limit => ?MAX_BYTES}};
decode(Binary) when is_binary(Binary) ->
    Decoders = #{object_start => fun object_start/1, object_push => fun object_push/3,
                 object_finish => fun object_finish/2, array_start => fun array_start/1,
                 array_push => fun array_push/2, array_finish => fun array_finish/2,
                 integer => fun integer/1, float => fun float_value/1},
    try json:decode(Binary, #{depth => 0}, Decoders) of
        {{invalid_json, Detail}, _, _} -> {error, Detail};
        {Value, _, Rest} ->
            case whitespace(Rest) of
                true -> {ok, Value};
                false -> {error, #{code => trailing_input, path => []}}
            end
    catch
        throw:{invalid_json, Detail} -> {error, Detail};
        error:unexpected_end -> syntax(unexpected_end);
        error:{invalid_byte, _} -> syntax(invalid_byte);
        error:{unexpected_sequence, _} -> syntax(unexpected_sequence)
    end;
decode(_) -> {error, #{code => expected_binary, path => []}}.

object_start(Parent) -> start(Parent, #{}).
array_start(Parent) -> start(Parent, []).
start(#{depth := Depth}, Items) when Depth < ?MAX_DEPTH ->
    #{depth => Depth + 1, items => Items, index => 0, error => none};
start(_, _) -> reject(depth_limit).

object_push(Key, Value, #{items := Items, error := none} = Acc) ->
    case maps:is_key(Key, Items) of
        true -> Acc#{error => #{code => duplicate_key, path => [Key]}};
        false ->
            case Value of
                {invalid_json, Detail} -> Acc#{error => prepend(Key, Detail)};
                _ -> Acc#{items => Items#{Key => Value}}
            end
    end;
object_push(_, _, Acc) -> Acc.

array_push(Value, #{items := Items, index := Index, error := none} = Acc) ->
    case Value of
        {invalid_json, Detail} -> Acc#{error => prepend(Index, Detail)};
        _ -> Acc#{items => [Value | Items], index => Index + 1}
    end;
array_push(_, Acc) -> Acc.

object_finish(#{error := none, items := Items}, Parent) -> {Items, Parent};
object_finish(#{error := Detail}, Parent) -> {{invalid_json, Detail}, Parent}.
array_finish(#{error := none, items := Items}, Parent) -> {lists:reverse(Items), Parent};
array_finish(#{error := Detail}, Parent) -> {{invalid_json, Detail}, Parent}.
prepend(Key, #{path := Path} = Detail) -> Detail#{path => [Key | Path]}.

integer(Binary) when byte_size(Binary) =< 17 ->
    integer_value(binary_to_integer(Binary));
integer(_) -> invalid(number_out_of_range).

integer_value(Value) ->
    case is_integer(Value, -?MAX_INTEGER, ?MAX_INTEGER) of
        true -> Value;
        false -> invalid(number_out_of_range)
    end.

float_value(Binary) when byte_size(Binary) =< 128 ->
    case decimal_integer(Binary) of
        {integer, Integer} -> integer_value(Integer);
        out_of_range -> invalid(number_out_of_range);
        fractional ->
            try binary_to_float(Binary) of
                Value when Value < -?MAX_INTEGER; Value > ?MAX_INTEGER -> invalid(number_out_of_range);
                Value ->
                    case Value == trunc(Value) of
                        true -> invalid(nonintegral_number);
                        false -> Value
                    end
            catch error:badarg -> invalid(invalid_number)
            end
    end;
float_value(_) -> invalid(number_limit).

%% JSON supplies a validated token (and inserts .0 for exponent-only forms).
%% Bound the exponent before constructing powers; a large negative exponent
%% cannot make a nonzero coefficient integral.
decimal_integer(Binary) ->
    {Mantissa, Exponent} = case binary:split(Binary, [<<"e">>, <<"E">>]) of
        [M] -> {M, 0};
        [M, E] -> {M, binary_to_integer(E)}
    end,
    [Whole, Fraction] = binary:split(Mantissa, <<".">>),
    Digits = <<Whole/binary, Fraction/binary>>,
    Coefficient = binary_to_integer(Digits),
    Scale = Exponent - byte_size(Fraction),
    case {Coefficient, Scale} of
        {0, _} -> {integer, 0};
        {_, N} when N > 16 -> out_of_range;
        {C, N} when N >= 0 -> {integer, C * power10(N)};
        {_, N} when -N > byte_size(Digits) -> fractional;
        {C, N} ->
            Divisor = power10(-N),
            case C rem Divisor of
                0 -> {integer, C div Divisor};
                _ -> fractional
            end
    end.
power10(0) -> 1;
power10(N) -> 10 * power10(N - 1).

whitespace(<<>>) -> true;
whitespace(<<C, Rest/binary>>) when C =:= 32; C =:= 9; C =:= 10; C =:= 13 -> whitespace(Rest);
whitespace(_) -> false.
syntax(Reason) -> {error, #{code => invalid_json, path => [], reason => Reason}}.
invalid(Code) -> {invalid_json, #{code => Code, path => []}}.
-spec reject(atom()) -> no_return().
reject(Code) -> throw({invalid_json, #{code => Code, path => []}}).

-module(tmux_key).
-moduledoc """
Register and remove bindings in explicit server key tables.

`bind/3` uses the native prefix table; `bind/4` chooses a table, repeat flag
and note. Command values use `tmux_command:to_config/1` for the stored parser
boundary. Replacing a binding resets its commands, repeat flag and note.
Registration does not prove that a client later executed the binding.

Tables belong to the server. A session's key-table option selects its default
table through `m:tmux_option`; tmux's prefix and client table-switching rules
still apply. Registering a custom table does not select it for any client.
`clear_table/2` requires an explicit name and can affect attached clients.

`listing/2` returns native presentation bytes. Field padding, quoting, note
coverage and formatting vary by daemon release. It does not decode bindings
or promise reusable configuration. Retain the original command values when
an application needs to install the same binding again.

Key names use tmux's own binary spellings, such as C-b, Enter and MouseDown1Pane.
The daemon validates actual names and modifiers. Library validation bounds
bytes and rejects NUL before dispatch. Calls use registered endpoint identity,
perform explicit I/O and never retry uncertain mutations. They do not attach
a client or refresh captured rows.

The [key-table guide](keys.md) installs and removes an application-owned table.
""".
-export([bind/3, bind/4, unbind/2, unbind/3, clear_table/2, listing/1, listing/2]).
-export_type([key/0, bind_options/0, listing_options/0]).

-doc "A nonempty NUL-free native key spelling, at most 128 bytes; tmux validates its meaning.".
-type key() :: binary().
-doc """
Default table is prefix and repeat is false. Tables contain 1..1024 NUL-free
bytes. note is at most 32 KiB of NUL-free bytes; omitting it removes an old
note when commands are replaced. Command-level aggregate bounds still apply.
""".
-type bind_options() :: #{table => binary(), repeat => boolean(), note => binary()}.
-doc """
No table filter lists all native tables. table restricts the listing to one
nonempty NUL-free name of at most 1024 bytes; key restricts it to a native key
spelling. Missing tables and invalid key spellings retain native errors.
Unmatched filters can return empty output or a backend error by release.
""".
-type listing_options() :: #{table => binary(), key => key()}.

-doc """
Register commands in the native prefix table with default options. Performs
I/O; see `bind/4` for replacement, command parsing and future execution.
""".
-spec bind(tmux_server:t(), key(), tmux_command:t() | [tmux_command:t(), ...]) ->
    {ok, tmux_operation:completed()} | {error, tmux_operation:failure()}.
bind(Server, Key, Commands) -> bind(Server, Key, Commands, #{}).

-doc """
Register or replace one binding with validated command values. Commands can
be one value or a flat nonempty list; `tmux_command:to_config/1` applies the
aggregate count and byte bounds. Options follow `t:bind_options/0`. Arguments,
table names and notes are literal bytes at registration; stored commands still
interpret their values and formats when a client executes them.

Performs I/O. tmux parses the commands before replacing an existing binding.
The result confirms registration, while effects of future key presses need
their own acknowledgement. Replacement resets the old repeat flag and note
using the supplied options. Errors preserve backend diagnostics and unknown
outcomes; there is no rollback or automatic retry.
""".
-spec bind(tmux_server:t(), key(), tmux_command:t() | [tmux_command:t(), ...],
    bind_options()) -> {ok, tmux_operation:completed()} | {error, tmux_operation:failure()}.
bind(Server, Key0, Commands, Options) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Key} ?= key(Key0),
        {ok, Text} ?= tmux_command:to_config(Commands),
        {ok, Flags} ?= tmux_args:options(Options,
            [{table, key_table, <<"-T">>}, {repeat, flag, <<"-r">>},
             {note, bytes, <<"-N">>}], #{table => <<"prefix">>}),
        tmux_target:run(Server, <<"bind-key">>, Flags ++ [<<"--">>, Key, Text])
    end.

-doc "Remove a binding from the native prefix table. Performs I/O; see `unbind/3`.".
-spec unbind(tmux_server:t(), key()) ->
    {ok, tmux_operation:completed()} | {error, tmux_operation:failure()}.
unbind(Server, Key) -> unbind(Server, Key, #{}).

-doc """
Remove one key from the explicit table, defaulting to prefix. Only table is
accepted in the options map. A missing key in an existing table is a native
no-op; a missing explicit table remains an error. Removing the final custom
binding can remove its table, so a repeated call can then report that missing
table. Invalid native key names are never quietly suppressed.

Performs I/O. Effects already queued by a client are unaffected. Use
`clear_table/2` to remove an entire explicitly named table.
""".
-spec unbind(tmux_server:t(), key(), #{table => binary()}) ->
    {ok, tmux_operation:completed()} | {error, tmux_operation:failure()}.
unbind(Server, Key0, Options) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Key} ?= key(Key0),
        {ok, Flags} ?= tmux_args:options(Options,
            [{table, key_table, <<"-T">>}], #{table => <<"prefix">>}),
        tmux_target:run(Server, <<"unbind-key">>, Flags ++ [<<"--">>, Key])
    end.

-doc """
Remove the entire explicitly named table through native unbind-key -a -T.
Names use the bounds in `t:bind_options/0`. This can remove default bindings
and affect attached clients. Missing tables remain native errors; this call
does not restore factory defaults or cancel commands already queued.
Performs I/O after endpoint and argument validation.
""".
-spec clear_table(tmux_server:t(), binary()) ->
    {ok, tmux_operation:completed()} | {error, tmux_operation:failure()}.
clear_table(Server, Table) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Flags} ?= tmux_args:options(#{table => Table}, [{table, key_table, <<"-T">>}]),
        tmux_target:run(Server, <<"unbind-key">>, [<<"-a">> | Flags] ++ [<<"--">>])
    end.

-doc "Read all tables as native listing bytes. Performs I/O; see `listing/2`.".
-spec listing(tmux_server:t()) -> {ok, binary()} | {error, map()}.
listing(Server) -> listing(Server, #{}).

-doc """
Read native list-keys presentation output, optionally filtering by table and
key through `t:listing_options/0`. Returns the command's stdout unchanged;
spacing, quoting and included metadata follow that daemon. This is a text
view, with no decoded-row, exact-note or configuration-round-trip guarantee.

tmux 3.4 can escape dollar signs in this output. tmux 3.7c can send a single
matching entry to its status-message path, producing empty stdout without an
attached target client. Empty presentation output does not prove absence.
The [key-table guide](keys.md) demonstrates a table with multiple bindings.

The baseline command has no custom format option on tmux 3.3. Deliberate
newer-server formatting is available through `tmux_command:raw/2`. Performs
I/O; missing tables, invalid key spellings and backend errors remain errors.
""".
-spec listing(tmux_server:t(), listing_options()) -> {ok, binary()} | {error, map()}.
listing(Server, Options) when is_map(Options) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Flags} ?= tmux_args:options(maps:remove(key, Options),
            [{table, key_table, <<"-T">>}]),
        {ok, Keys} ?= case maps:find(key, Options) of
            error -> {ok, []};
            {ok, Key0} -> maybe {ok, Key} ?= key(Key0), {ok, [Key]} end
        end,
        {ok, #{stdout := Output}} ?= tmux_target:run(Server, <<"list-keys">>,
            Flags ++ [<<"--">> | Keys]),
        {ok, Output}
    end;
listing(_, _) -> {error, #{code => invalid_options, path => []}}.

key(Key) when is_binary(Key), byte_size(Key) > 0, byte_size(Key) =< 128 ->
    case binary:match(Key, <<0>>) of
        nomatch -> {ok, Key};
        _ -> {error, #{code => invalid_key}}
    end;
key(_) -> {error, #{code => invalid_key}}.

-module(tmux_matcher).
-moduledoc """
Prepare a trusted local predicate once for a captured snapshot.

Use `tmux_select:matching/2` with `{Module, State}`. The application chooses
Module; external filter documents cannot select the `c:prepare/2`
callback. Preparation returns a unary Boolean function or a tagged error.
Callback exceptions propagate. The adapter does not make executable predicates
portable or push them to tmux.
""".
-doc """
Prepare a local Boolean predicate once for this captured snapshot. Return a
tagged preparation error when the matcher cannot operate. Callback exceptions
remain application failures; this does not make a matcher portable or suitable
for untrusted module selection.
""".
-callback prepare(State :: term(), Snapshot :: tmux_snapshot:t()) ->
    {ok, fun((tmux_model:row()) -> boolean())} | {error, term()}.

%% Generated from schema/entities.json by tools/generate_schema.escript.
-module(tmux_model).
-moduledoc """
Validated native domain records. Constructors perform no tmux I/O.

Missing optional observations remain not_loaded; required identity fields
must be supplied. Unavailable capabilities remain
unavailable. Neither state means an empty relation or known absence.
Rows created by `new/2` and the entity constructors are detached.
Entity constructors accept generated input-map types such as
`t:pane_input/0`. Use `new/2` to validate dynamic maps; Dialyzer checks
known constructor shapes but does not replace runtime validation.
Use `tmux_server:bind/2` to register a fresh observed row for actions;
use `m:tmux_snapshot` for captured graph relationships.

Observed rows carry a private `t:observation/0` value. Actions compare it
with the row's origin, snapshot identity and target fields, rejecting
mismatched observations before I/O. Valid-shaped binding mismatches return
observation_mismatch; detached and malformed rows keep their validation
errors. Retarget through
`tmux_server:bind/2`; it reads current values. This protects ordinary API
use, not authority against trusted code in the Erlang VM.

Native model version 2 adds this association. Discard version-1 rows and
snapshots on upgrade and freshly observe them. `to_map/1` extracts domain
fields for explicit schema validation; maps carry no actionable origin.
""".
-export_record([session, window, window_link, pane]).
-export([new/2, validate/1, entity/1, get/2, to_map/1, origin/1,
         snapshot_id/1, model_version/1, bind/3, verify_observation/1]).
-export([session/1, window/1, window_link/1, pane/1]).
-export_type([row/0, observation/0, pane_id/0, window_id/0, session_id/0,
              session/0, window/0, window_link/0, pane/0,
              session_input/0, window_input/0, window_link_input/0, pane_input/0]).

-doc "A canonical pane ID binary in the percent namespace; nominal checking is by Dialyzer.".
-nominal pane_id() :: binary().
-doc "A canonical physical-window ID binary in the at-sign namespace.".
-nominal window_id() :: binary().
-doc "A canonical session ID binary in the dollar namespace.".
-nominal session_id() :: binary().

-record #observation{entity :: atom(), origin :: reference(),
    snapshot_id :: reference(), identity :: tuple()}.
-doc "Private captured target association, created by observation. Retain with its row; construction and field access are internal. It is not an authorization or serialization format.".
-opaque observation() :: #observation{}.

-record #session{
    id :: session_id(),
    name = not_loaded :: binary() | not_loaded | unavailable,
    attached_count = not_loaded :: non_neg_integer() | not_loaded | unavailable,
    attached = not_loaded :: boolean() | not_loaded | unavailable,
    created = not_loaded :: non_neg_integer() | not_loaded | unavailable,
    origin = none :: none | reference(),
    snapshot_id = none :: none | reference(),
    model_version = 2 :: pos_integer(),
    observation = none :: none | observation()
}.

-record #window{
    id :: window_id(),
    name = not_loaded :: binary() | not_loaded | unavailable,
    width = not_loaded :: non_neg_integer() | not_loaded | unavailable,
    height = not_loaded :: non_neg_integer() | not_loaded | unavailable,
    pane_count = not_loaded :: non_neg_integer() | not_loaded | unavailable,
    layout = not_loaded :: binary() | not_loaded | unavailable,
    origin = none :: none | reference(),
    snapshot_id = none :: none | reference(),
    model_version = 2 :: pos_integer(),
    observation = none :: none | observation()
}.

-record #window_link{
    session_id :: session_id(),
    window_id :: window_id(),
    index :: non_neg_integer(),
    active = not_loaded :: boolean() | not_loaded | unavailable,
    origin = none :: none | reference(),
    snapshot_id = none :: none | reference(),
    model_version = 2 :: pos_integer(),
    observation = none :: none | observation()
}.

-record #pane{
    id :: pane_id(),
    window_id = not_loaded :: window_id() | not_loaded | unavailable,
    index = not_loaded :: non_neg_integer() | not_loaded | unavailable,
    active = not_loaded :: boolean() | not_loaded | unavailable,
    current_command = not_loaded :: binary() | not_loaded | unavailable,
    current_path = not_loaded :: binary() | not_loaded | unavailable,
    width = not_loaded :: non_neg_integer() | not_loaded | unavailable,
    height = not_loaded :: non_neg_integer() | not_loaded | unavailable,
    pid = not_loaded :: pos_integer() | none | not_loaded | unavailable,
    title = not_loaded :: binary() | not_loaded | unavailable,
    dead = not_loaded :: boolean() | not_loaded | unavailable,
    exit_status = not_loaded :: integer() | none | not_loaded | unavailable,
    origin = none :: none | reference(),
    snapshot_id = none :: none | reference(),
    model_version = 2 :: pos_integer(),
    observation = none :: none | observation()
}.

-doc "One schema-defined native domain record, with separate origin and capture metadata.".
-type row() :: #session{} | #window{} | #window_link{} | #pane{}.
-doc "A validated session observation. Native records are experimental in OTP 29.".
-type session() :: #session{}.
-doc "A validated window observation. Native records are experimental in OTP 29.".
-type window() :: #window{}.
-doc "A validated window_link observation. Native records are experimental in OTP 29.".
-type window_link() :: #window_link{}.
-doc "A validated pane observation. Native records are experimental in OTP 29.".
-type pane() :: #pane{}.

-doc """
Trusted constructor fields for `session/1`. Required keys use :=;
optional observations may be not_loaded or unavailable. Integral floats
are normalized to integers. Runtime validation still checks ranges, IDs,
UTF-8 and derived values. Use `new/2` for dynamically validated maps.
""".
-type session_input() :: #{
    id := session_id(),
    name => binary() | not_loaded | unavailable,
    attached_count => non_neg_integer() | float() | not_loaded | unavailable,
    attached => boolean() | not_loaded | unavailable,
    created => non_neg_integer() | float() | not_loaded | unavailable
}.

-doc """
Trusted constructor fields for `window/1`. Required keys use :=;
optional observations may be not_loaded or unavailable. Integral floats
are normalized to integers. Runtime validation still checks ranges, IDs,
UTF-8 and derived values. Use `new/2` for dynamically validated maps.
""".
-type window_input() :: #{
    id := window_id(),
    name => binary() | not_loaded | unavailable,
    width => non_neg_integer() | float() | not_loaded | unavailable,
    height => non_neg_integer() | float() | not_loaded | unavailable,
    pane_count => non_neg_integer() | float() | not_loaded | unavailable,
    layout => binary() | not_loaded | unavailable
}.

-doc """
Trusted constructor fields for `window_link/1`. Required keys use :=;
optional observations may be not_loaded or unavailable. Integral floats
are normalized to integers. Runtime validation still checks ranges, IDs,
UTF-8 and derived values. Use `new/2` for dynamically validated maps.
""".
-type window_link_input() :: #{
    session_id := session_id(),
    window_id := window_id(),
    index := non_neg_integer() | float(),
    active => boolean() | not_loaded | unavailable
}.

-doc """
Trusted constructor fields for `pane/1`. Required keys use :=;
optional observations may be not_loaded or unavailable. Integral floats
are normalized to integers. Runtime validation still checks ranges, IDs,
UTF-8 and derived values. Use `new/2` for dynamically validated maps.
""".
-type pane_input() :: #{
    id := pane_id(),
    window_id => window_id() | not_loaded | unavailable,
    index => non_neg_integer() | float() | not_loaded | unavailable,
    active => boolean() | not_loaded | unavailable,
    current_command => binary() | not_loaded | unavailable,
    current_path => binary() | not_loaded | unavailable,
    width => non_neg_integer() | float() | not_loaded | unavailable,
    height => non_neg_integer() | float() | not_loaded | unavailable,
    pid => pos_integer() | float() | none | not_loaded | unavailable,
    title => binary() | not_loaded | unavailable,
    dead => boolean() | not_loaded | unavailable,
    exit_status => integer() | float() | none | not_loaded | unavailable
}.

-doc """
Construct a detached row from validated observations.

Accepts dynamic maps, including malformed input that returns a tagged
`t:tmux_schema:error_detail/0`. For trusted typed code, prefer the entity
constructors such as `pane/1` and `t:pane_input/0`.

```erlang
1> {ok, Pane} = tmux_model:new(pane, #{id => <<"%1">>, width => 120}), ok.
ok
2> tmux_model:get(width, Pane).
120
```
""".
-spec new(atom(), map()) -> {ok, row()} | {error, tmux_schema:error_detail()}.
new(Entity, Fields) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Normalized} ?= tmux_schema:normalize(Entity, Fields),
        {ok, build(Entity, Normalized)}
    end.

-doc "Construct a detached session row, validating required fields and scalar bounds without tmux I/O.".
-spec session(session_input()) -> {ok, session()} | {error, tmux_schema:error_detail()}.
session(Fields) -> new(session, Fields).

-doc "Construct a detached window row, validating required fields and scalar bounds without tmux I/O.".
-spec window(window_input()) -> {ok, window()} | {error, tmux_schema:error_detail()}.
window(Fields) -> new(window, Fields).

-doc "Construct a detached window_link row, validating required fields and scalar bounds without tmux I/O.".
-spec window_link(window_link_input()) -> {ok, window_link()} | {error, tmux_schema:error_detail()}.
window_link(Fields) -> new(window_link, Fields).

-doc "Construct a detached pane row, validating required fields and scalar bounds without tmux I/O.".
-spec pane(pane_input()) -> {ok, pane()} | {error, tmux_schema:error_detail()}.
pane(Fields) -> new(pane, Fields).

-doc "Validate native row shape, model version and normalized observations. Exported records do not enforce these invariants at construction. Performs no I/O.".
-spec validate(term()) -> {ok, row()} | {error, map()}.
validate(Row) ->
    case row_metadata(Row) of
        {Entity, 2, Origin, Snapshot, Observation}
          when (Origin =:= none orelse is_reference(Origin)),
               (Snapshot =:= none orelse is_reference(Snapshot)),
               (Observation =:= none orelse is_record(Observation, observation)) ->
            Fields = to_map(Row),
            case tmux_schema:normalize(Entity, Fields) of
                {ok, Fields} -> {ok, Row};
                {ok, _} -> {error, #{code => unnormalized_row, path => []}};
                {error, _} = Error -> Error
            end;
        _ -> {error, #{code => invalid_row, path => []}}
    end.

-doc "Return the built-in entity kind of a native row without I/O.".
-spec entity(row()) -> tmux_schema:entity().
entity(#session{}) -> session;
entity(#window{}) -> window;
entity(#window_link{}) -> window_link;
entity(#pane{}) -> pane.

-doc "Read the opaque origin token, or none for a detached row. This does not revalidate endpoint lifetime.".
-spec origin(row()) -> none | reference().
origin(#session{origin = Value}) -> Value;
origin(#window{origin = Value}) -> Value;
origin(#window_link{origin = Value}) -> Value;
origin(#pane{origin = Value}) -> Value.

-doc "Read the capture identity, or none when not associated with a snapshot. Performs no I/O.".
-spec snapshot_id(row()) -> none | reference().
snapshot_id(#session{snapshot_id = Value}) -> Value;
snapshot_id(#window{snapshot_id = Value}) -> Value;
snapshot_id(#window_link{snapshot_id = Value}) -> Value;
snapshot_id(#pane{snapshot_id = Value}) -> Value.

-doc "Read the native model version. Unknown versions fail validation; record internals are not a persistence format.".
-spec model_version(row()) -> pos_integer().
model_version(#session{model_version = Value}) -> Value;
model_version(#window{model_version = Value}) -> Value;
model_version(#window_link{model_version = Value}) -> Value;
model_version(#pane{model_version = Value}) -> Value.

-doc "Return domain field values without origin or capture metadata. This is not the portable filter wire representation. Performs no I/O.".
-spec to_map(row()) -> map().
to_map(Row = #session{}) -> #{id => Row#session.id, name => Row#session.name, attached_count => Row#session.attached_count, attached => Row#session.attached, created => Row#session.created};
to_map(Row = #window{}) -> #{id => Row#window.id, name => Row#window.name, width => Row#window.width, height => Row#window.height, pane_count => Row#window.pane_count, layout => Row#window.layout};
to_map(Row = #window_link{}) -> #{session_id => Row#window_link.session_id, window_id => Row#window_link.window_id, index => Row#window_link.index, active => Row#window_link.active};
to_map(Row = #pane{}) -> #{id => Row#pane.id, window_id => Row#pane.window_id, index => Row#pane.index, active => Row#pane.active, current_command => Row#pane.current_command, current_path => Row#pane.current_path, width => Row#pane.width, height => Row#pane.height, pid => Row#pane.pid, title => Row#pane.title, dead => Row#pane.dead, exit_status => Row#pane.exit_status}.

-doc "Read a permitted domain field without I/O. Unknown fields raise unknown_field; unloaded and unavailable values remain distinct.".
-spec get(atom(), row()) -> term().
get(id, #session{id = Value}) -> Value;
get(name, #session{name = Value}) -> Value;
get(attached_count, #session{attached_count = Value}) -> Value;
get(attached, #session{attached = Value}) -> Value;
get(created, #session{created = Value}) -> Value;
get(id, #window{id = Value}) -> Value;
get(name, #window{name = Value}) -> Value;
get(width, #window{width = Value}) -> Value;
get(height, #window{height = Value}) -> Value;
get(pane_count, #window{pane_count = Value}) -> Value;
get(layout, #window{layout = Value}) -> Value;
get(session_id, #window_link{session_id = Value}) -> Value;
get(window_id, #window_link{window_id = Value}) -> Value;
get(index, #window_link{index = Value}) -> Value;
get(active, #window_link{active = Value}) -> Value;
get(id, #pane{id = Value}) -> Value;
get(window_id, #pane{window_id = Value}) -> Value;
get(index, #pane{index = Value}) -> Value;
get(active, #pane{active = Value}) -> Value;
get(current_command, #pane{current_command = Value}) -> Value;
get(current_path, #pane{current_path = Value}) -> Value;
get(width, #pane{width = Value}) -> Value;
get(height, #pane{height = Value}) -> Value;
get(pid, #pane{pid = Value}) -> Value;
get(title, #pane{title = Value}) -> Value;
get(dead, #pane{dead = Value}) -> Value;
get(exit_status, #pane{exit_status = Value}) -> Value;
get(Field, Row) ->
    erlang:error({unknown_field, entity(Row), Field}, none,
        [{error_info, #{module => tmux_error}}]).

-doc false.
-spec bind(row(), reference(), reference()) -> row().
bind(Row = #session{}, Origin, Snapshot)
  when is_reference(Origin), is_reference(Snapshot) ->
    {ok, Row} = validate(Row),
    Row#session{origin = Origin, snapshot_id = Snapshot,
        observation = observation(Row, Origin, Snapshot)};
bind(Row = #window{}, Origin, Snapshot)
  when is_reference(Origin), is_reference(Snapshot) ->
    {ok, Row} = validate(Row),
    Row#window{origin = Origin, snapshot_id = Snapshot,
        observation = observation(Row, Origin, Snapshot)};
bind(Row = #window_link{}, Origin, Snapshot)
  when is_reference(Origin), is_reference(Snapshot) ->
    {ok, Row} = validate(Row),
    Row#window_link{origin = Origin, snapshot_id = Snapshot,
        observation = observation(Row, Origin, Snapshot)};
bind(Row = #pane{}, Origin, Snapshot)
  when is_reference(Origin), is_reference(Snapshot) ->
    {ok, Row} = validate(Row),
    Row#pane{origin = Origin, snapshot_id = Snapshot,
        observation = observation(Row, Origin, Snapshot)}.

-doc false.
-spec verify_observation(row()) -> ok | {error, map()}.
verify_observation(Row) ->
    case row_metadata(Row) of
        {_, 2, Origin, Snapshot, Captured}
          when is_reference(Origin), is_reference(Snapshot) ->
            case Captured =:= observation(Row, Origin, Snapshot) of
                true -> ok;
                false -> {error, #{code => observation_mismatch}}
            end;
        _ -> {error, #{code => observation_mismatch}}
    end.

observation(Row = #session{}, Origin, Snapshot) ->
    #observation{entity = session, origin = Origin,
        snapshot_id = Snapshot, identity = {Row#session.id}};
observation(Row = #window{}, Origin, Snapshot) ->
    #observation{entity = window, origin = Origin,
        snapshot_id = Snapshot, identity = {Row#window.id}};
observation(Row = #window_link{}, Origin, Snapshot) ->
    #observation{entity = window_link, origin = Origin,
        snapshot_id = Snapshot, identity = {Row#window_link.session_id, Row#window_link.window_id, Row#window_link.index}};
observation(Row = #pane{}, Origin, Snapshot) ->
    #observation{entity = pane, origin = Origin,
        snapshot_id = Snapshot, identity = {Row#pane.id, Row#pane.window_id, Row#pane.index}}.

row_metadata(#session{model_version = V, origin = O, snapshot_id = S,
        observation = B}) ->
    {session, V, O, S, B};
row_metadata(#window{model_version = V, origin = O, snapshot_id = S,
        observation = B}) ->
    {window, V, O, S, B};
row_metadata(#window_link{model_version = V, origin = O, snapshot_id = S,
        observation = B}) ->
    {window_link, V, O, S, B};
row_metadata(#pane{model_version = V, origin = O, snapshot_id = S,
        observation = B}) ->
    {pane, V, O, S, B};
row_metadata(_) -> invalid.

build(session, Fields) -> #session{
    id = maps:get(id, Fields),
    name = maps:get(name, Fields),
    attached_count = maps:get(attached_count, Fields),
    attached = maps:get(attached, Fields),
    created = maps:get(created, Fields)
};
build(window, Fields) -> #window{
    id = maps:get(id, Fields),
    name = maps:get(name, Fields),
    width = maps:get(width, Fields),
    height = maps:get(height, Fields),
    pane_count = maps:get(pane_count, Fields),
    layout = maps:get(layout, Fields)
};
build(window_link, Fields) -> #window_link{
    session_id = maps:get(session_id, Fields),
    window_id = maps:get(window_id, Fields),
    index = maps:get(index, Fields),
    active = maps:get(active, Fields)
};
build(pane, Fields) -> #pane{
    id = maps:get(id, Fields),
    window_id = maps:get(window_id, Fields),
    index = maps:get(index, Fields),
    active = maps:get(active, Fields),
    current_command = maps:get(current_command, Fields),
    current_path = maps:get(current_path, Fields),
    width = maps:get(width, Fields),
    height = maps:get(height, Fields),
    pid = maps:get(pid, Fields),
    title = maps:get(title, Fields),
    dead = maps:get(dead, Fields),
    exit_status = maps:get(exit_status, Fields)
}.
