-module(tmux_operation).
-moduledoc """
Own a command independently of an individual wait.

`start/3` submits a validated command through the endpoint's
bounded admission. The initiating process owns it. `await/2`
timing out abandons only that wait; `cancel/1` or owner death
retires the client and may leave an unknown tmux outcome. The endpoint
acknowledges `transfer/2` after monitoring the new owner and
before replying to the old owner. The new process does not perform a
handshake. Retired results expire after 60 seconds or earlier when the
endpoint exceeds 64 retained results or 4 MiB of retained stdout/stderr
(oldest evicted first). Closing the endpoint clears its operation results
immediately. Each operation accepts at most 16 concurrent waiters; excess
waits return too_many_waiters. `await_started/2` returns
lifecycle status once the operation leaves queued; dispatch authorization does
not establish a tmux aftereffect.

See `t:completed/0` and `t:failure/0` for
command outcomes and `t:state/0` for lifecycle status. The [job
guide](jobs.md) shows the complete workflow. Bounded OTP Logger reports
correlate outcomes by operation and endpoint generation; see
[runtime diagnostics](diagnostics.md) for levels, fields and data boundaries.
""".
-export([start/3, await/2, await_started/2, status/1, cancel/1, transfer/2]).
-export_type([t/0, completed/0, failure/0, state/0, outcome/0, cleanup/0]).
-doc """
A generation-bound operation handle. Possessing a waiter handle does not
transfer ownership.
""".
-opaque t() :: {operation, pid(), reference(), reference()}.

-doc "Command certainty, separate from resource cleanup. unknown must not trigger an automatic mutation retry.".
-type outcome() :: success | error | not_started | cancelled_before_send | unknown.
-doc "complete proves owned client retirement; incomplete or unverified does not.".
-type cleanup() :: complete | incomplete | unverified.
-doc """
A successful command result. stdout and stderr are separate byte strings;
exit_status is zero. stdin_delivered counts bytes accepted by the client pipe,
not bytes consumed by tmux. success does not prove a background aftereffect.
""".
-type completed() :: #{stdout := binary(), stderr := binary(), exit_status := 0,
    stdin_delivered := non_neg_integer(), outcome := success, cleanup := complete}.
-doc """
A tagged error detail with a stable code and optional certainty/output data.
Validation, admission and wait errors may contain only code. Command failures
retain available stdout/stderr, stdin_delivered and exit_status. Other keys
provide code-specific context. Never infer missing certainty fields.

Common codes are busy, invalid_operation_options, command_error, deadline,
cancelled, stale_server, cleanup_incomplete, await_timeout and
operation_expired. command_error means a nonzero client exit; it does not roll
back a mutation. await_timeout abandons only this wait. operation_expired
cannot reconstruct a previous result or establish its remote outcome.
""".
-type failure() :: #{code := atom(), outcome => outcome(), cleanup => cleanup(),
    stdout => binary(), stderr => binary(), stdin_delivered => non_neg_integer(),
    exit_status => integer(), submitted => boolean(), atom() => term()}.
-doc """
Observed lifecycle state, without command output. queued includes admission
and identity preflight; sent means dispatch authorization, not a proven
aftereffect. responded can retain incomplete cleanup; retired releases
operation resources. pending certainty means no result yet. The owner is the
initiating or transferred process; holding a waiter handle does not change it.
""".
-type state() :: #{phase := queued | sent | responded | retired,
    stage := pending | waiting | preflight | command, owner := pid(),
    outcome := pending | outcome(), cleanup := pending | cleanup()}.

-doc """
Submit a validated command under the endpoint's admission limits and return an
operation handle. The initiating process owns it. Submission is non-blocking
with respect to command completion; the handle does not prove that tmux has
executed the command.
""".
-spec start(tmux_server:t(), tmux_command:t(), tmux_server:command_options()) -> {ok, t()} | {error, failure()}.
start(Server, Command, Options) ->
    case tmux_server:submit(Server, Command, Options) of
        {ok, {Pid, Generation, Lease}} -> {ok, {operation, Pid, Generation, Lease}};
        Error -> Error
    end.

-doc """
Wait for a retained result for at most Timeout. An await_timeout removes only
this waiter; the operation continues and its handle remains usable. Additional
waiters do not become owners. Results preserve outcome and cleanup certainty.
""".
-spec await(t(), timeout()) -> {ok, completed()} | {error, failure()}.
await(Operation, Timeout) -> request(Operation, await, Timeout).

-doc """
Wait until the operation leaves queued, returning its lifecycle state even if
it has already failed or retired. Inspect outcome and cleanup; call `await/2`
for final command data. Authorization is not proof of a tmux aftereffect. A
timeout abandons this wait without cancelling the operation.
""".
-spec await_started(t(), timeout()) -> {ok, state()} | {error, failure()}.
await_started(Operation, Timeout) -> request(Operation, started, Timeout).

-doc """
Read the retained lifecycle state without starting a tmux command. Expired
handles return operation_expired. Status is observation of the operation, not
evidence that a possibly sent mutation was cancelled.
""".
-spec status(t()) -> {ok, state()} | {error, failure()}.
status(Operation) -> request(Operation, status, 900).

-doc """
Request cancellation using this handle. Any holder can cancel; only the owner
can transfer ownership. Queued work can be cancelled before submission;
possibly sent work retires its client and can retain an unknown tmux outcome.
Use `await/2` for the result and cleanup proof. Never infer rollback or
automatically retry a mutation from cancellation alone. already_completed
means a response exists; it does not establish complete cleanup.
""".
-spec cancel(t()) -> {ok, cancelled_before_send | cancel_requested | already_completed} | {error, map()}.
cancel(Operation) -> request(Operation, cancel, 900).

-doc """
Transfer ownership to a live process on this Erlang node. The endpoint
installs its new owner monitor before releasing the previous monitor and
returns after the swap. The new process performs no handshake. Waiters and
ownership remain separate; endpoint ownership does not change.

An `await_timeout` abandons the reply, not the queued ownership change. The
transfer may complete later. Use `status/1` to read the current owner before
relying on ownership; a timeout does not prove that the old owner remains.
""".
-spec transfer(t(), pid()) -> ok | {error, map()}.
transfer(Operation, Owner) when is_pid(Owner), node(Owner) =:= node() ->
    request(Operation, {transfer, Owner}, 900);
transfer(_, _) -> {error, #{code => invalid_owner}}.

request({operation, Pid, Generation, Lease}, Kind, Timeout)
  when is_pid(Pid), is_reference(Generation), is_reference(Lease),
       (Timeout =:= infinity orelse is_integer(Timeout, 0, 4294967295)) ->
    Tag = make_ref(),
    Request = gen_server:send_request(Pid, {Generation, operation, Lease, Kind, Tag}),
    case gen_server:receive_response(Request, Timeout) of
        {reply, Reply} -> Reply;
        timeout ->
            gen_server:cast(Pid, {Generation, unwait, Lease, Tag}),
            {error, #{code => await_timeout}};
        {error, _} -> {error, #{code => operation_expired, cleanup => unverified}}
    end;
request(_, _, _) -> {error, #{code => invalid_operation}}.

-module(tmux_option).
-moduledoc """
Read and change explicit tmux option tables through registered references.

Session, physical window and pane records from `m:tmux_model` select their
local tables. Global tables use {server, Server}, {session_defaults, Server}
or {window_defaults, Server}. Built-in canonical names and scopes are checked
against pinned source metadata; tmux otherwise lets a name override the
supplied scope flags. `m:tmux_hook` owns hook registration and execution;
hooks are rejected here. Prefixes and aliases are rejected.

`get/3` requires an explicit options map. Local-only reads are the
default; inherit = true follows tmux's table parents (pane -> window -> window
defaults, or session -> session defaults). Server options have no parent. A
missing local value or array entry returns none; an empty binary or empty
array is a value. Arrays return maps of indexes to binary values, preserving
sparse indexes. There is no hidden capture refresh or cache of option values.
`get_many/3` reads the same scalar key from up to seven local rows through one
bounded native sequence, retaining local-only semantics by default.

Values are NUL-free binary tmux text bytes, including non-UTF-8 bytes. No
shell or format expansion is applied by this API. tmux still interprets a
built-in option according to its type: formats, shell commands and command
options may execute later when tmux uses them. This API is for trusted
application code. Numeric and flag values are canonical binary text on reads,
not Erlang numbers.

Built-in metadata covers every released version in the supported tmux
3.3a–3.8 range, including exact patch letters. Tracking and unknown versions
fail closed. User options beginning @ do not need a built-in
catalogue. The raw `tmux_command:raw/2` remains available for deliberate
newer-server integration. All mutations are one-shot I/O with observed
identity checks, not transactions. Timeouts can leave an unknown remote
outcome; mutations are never retried here. See the [scoped options
guide](options.md) for ownership and inheritance.
""".
-export([get/3, get_many/3, set/3, set/4, unset/2, describe/2, catalogue/1]).
-export_type([scope/0, key/0, metadata/0, read_options/0, write_options/0, value/0]).

-doc "A registered local entity or an explicitly selected global option table.".
-type scope() :: tmux_model:session() | tmux_model:window() | tmux_model:pane() |
    {server | session_defaults | window_defaults, tmux_server:t()}.
-doc "Canonical binary name; arrays use a structured non-negative index, never bracket syntax.".
-type key() :: binary() | {binary(), non_neg_integer()}.
-doc "Source-derived scope, parser type, array and executable-hook metadata.".
-type metadata() :: #{scopes := [server | session | window | pane],
    type := choice | colour | command | flag | key | number | string,
    array := boolean(), hook := boolean()}.
-doc "Local-only unless inherit is true. Unknown options and non-Booleans are errors.".
-type read_options() :: #{inherit => boolean()}.
-doc "append maps to -a; only_if_unset maps to -o and reports already-set errors. Both default false.".
-type write_options() :: #{append => boolean(), only_if_unset => boolean()}.
-doc "Canonical tmux text bytes for a scalar/entry, or a sparse map for a whole array.".
-type value() :: binary() | #{non_neg_integer() => binary()}.

-doc """
Return source metadata for a canonical built-in name and a parsed daemon
version, without I/O. Unknown names, unavailable names, tracking builds and
uncatalogued versions have distinct errors. The catalogue describes scopes and
parser types; it does not qualify runtime behavior or authorize hook
execution.

```erlang
1> {ok, V} = tmux_version:parse(<<"tmux 3.3a">>), ok.
ok
2> {ok, M} = tmux_option:describe(V, <<"exit-empty">>), ok.
ok
3> maps:get(scopes, M).
[server]
```
""".
-spec describe(tmux_version:t(), binary()) -> {ok, metadata()} | {error, map()}.
describe(Version, Name) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Profile} ?= profile(Version),
        case tmux_option_data:variants(Name) of
            [] -> {error, #{code => unknown_tmux_option, name => Name}};
            Variants -> find(Profile, Name, Variants)
        end
    end.

-doc """
Return all canonical built-in option and hook metadata for one exact parsed
version, without I/O. Catalogues cover every release from 3.3a through 3.8;
historical 3.3 metadata remains available for source discovery. The generated
reference records each release's source commit and file digests.
""".
-spec catalogue(tmux_version:t()) -> {ok, #{binary() => metadata()}} | {error, map()}.
catalogue(Version) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Profile} ?= profile(Version),
        {ok, maps:from_list([{Name, Meta} || Name <- tmux_option_data:names(),
            {ok, Meta} <- [find(Profile, Name, tmux_option_data:variants(Name))]])}
    end.

-doc """
Read one option or array, performing I/O after validation. Missing local
values and array entries return none; known empty strings and arrays return
{ok, Value}. inherit = true reads through tmux's parent tables. Unknown fields
are rejected. Errors retain backend diagnostics; a missing target never
becomes absence. Use `set/4` to write a value and `unset/2` to restore
inheritance.
""".
-spec get(scope(), key(), read_options()) -> {ok, value()} | none | {error, map()}.
get(Scope, Key, Options) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Flags} ?= tmux_args:options(Options, [{inherit, flag, <<"-A">>}]),
        {ok, Server, ScopeArgs, Name, Index, Meta} ?= tmux_option_scope:prepare(Scope, Key, read, option),
        {ok, Literal} ?= tmux_command:literal_format(Name),
        {ok, Version} ?= tmux_server:version(Server),
        Result = tmux_target:run(Server, <<"show-options">>,
            ScopeArgs ++ Flags ++ [<<"--">>, Literal]),
        read_result(Result, Name, Index, Meta, Version)
    end.

-doc """
Read one scalar option from one to seven local rows on the same registered
endpoint. Performs one bounded native sequence after validating every scope.
Results follow input order; each entry is binary text or none for a missing
local value. `t:read_options/0` controls inheritance as in `get/3`.

Names use ASCII letters, digits, dots, underscores and hyphens, with an
optional leading @ for user options. Global tables, arrays, indexed keys,
hooks and command options are unsupported. Use `get/3` for broader option
reads and `tmux_hook:get/3` for hooks.
Invalid scopes, unsupported keys and different owners fail before dispatch.

Each read is bracketed by matching native target-ID observations. Unresolved
or mismatched IDs reject the batch. The checks do not prove topology membership
or completed destruction: older tmux may retain an unlinked pane through
queued references. The sequence provides interval observations and the same
server-incarnation guarantee as `get/3`. Ambient command configuration applies
to both paths.

Stdout is bounded to 1 MiB and stderr to 64 KiB for the whole sequence, with
the endpoint's 2500 ms command deadline. Seven 32 KiB values fit even under
the qualified worst-case native quoting expansion. Larger external values
may exceed that aggregate output bound. Any command, framing or decoding
failure rejects the entire result, retaining native outcome and cleanup
evidence. There is no partial-success result, hidden refresh or value cache.
""".
-spec get_many(nonempty_list(tmux_model:session() | tmux_model:window() |
    tmux_model:pane()), binary(), read_options()) ->
    {ok, [binary() | none]} | {error, map()}.
get_many(Scopes, Name, Options) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Flags} ?= tmux_args:options(Options, [{inherit, flag, <<"-A">>}]),
        {ok, Server, Command, Rows} ?= tmux_option_batch:prepare(Scopes, Name, Flags),
        {ok, Version} ?= tmux_server:version(Server),
        {ok, Result} ?= tmux_server:command(Server, Command, #{}),
        case tmux_option_batch:decode(Name, maps:get(stdout, Result), Rows, Version) of
            {ok, _} = Success -> Success;
            {error, Error} -> {error, maps:merge(Result, Error)}
        end
    end.

-doc """
Set one scalar or indexed array entry with default write options. Performs
I/O; see `set/4` for append, only-if-unset, parsing and unknown-outcome
semantics.
""".
-spec set(scope(), key(), binary()) ->
    {ok, tmux_operation:completed()} | {error, tmux_operation:failure()}.
set(Scope, Key, Value) -> set(Scope, Key, Value, #{}).

-doc """
Set a literal binary value, after scope/version/owner validation. Array writes
require {Name, Index}; this avoids tmux's whole-array separator grammar.
append uses tmux's type-specific -a semantics. only_if_unset checks the local
table; already-set is a backend error, with no suppressed errors or
compare-and-swap guarantee. Values must be supplied explicitly; an empty flag
value retains tmux's native toggle behavior. A successful result proves
command completion, not later effects of a stored command or format. Performs
I/O; never retries.
""".
-spec set(scope(), key(), binary(), write_options()) ->
    {ok, tmux_operation:completed()} | {error, tmux_operation:failure()}.
set(Scope, Key, Value, Options) ->
    maybe
        ok ?= value(Value),
        {ok, Flags} ?= tmux_args:options(Options,
            [{append, flag, <<"-a">>}, {only_if_unset, flag, <<"-o">>}]),
        {ok, Server, ScopeArgs, Name, Index, _} ?= tmux_option_scope:prepare(Scope, Key, write, option),
        {ok, Literal} ?= tmux_command:literal_format(tmux_option_scope:indexed(Name, Index)),
        tmux_target:run(Server, <<"set-option">>,
            ScopeArgs ++ Flags ++ [<<"--">>, Literal, Value])
    end.

-doc """
Remove a local option or one indexed entry. Removing a local option restores
inheritance; removing an entry leaves a local array, possibly empty. Unsetting
a global built-in resets tmux's default; user options are removed. Missing
local values are a successful tmux no-op. No pane-wide -U action is implied.
Performs I/O and returns the command result without refreshing captured rows.
""".
-spec unset(scope(), key()) ->
    {ok, tmux_operation:completed()} | {error, tmux_operation:failure()}.
unset(Scope, Key) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Server, ScopeArgs, Name, Index, _} ?= tmux_option_scope:prepare(Scope, Key, unset, option),
        {ok, Literal} ?= tmux_command:literal_format(tmux_option_scope:indexed(Name, Index)),
        tmux_target:run(Server, <<"set-option">>, ScopeArgs ++ [<<"-u">>, <<"--">>, Literal])
    end.

value(Value) when is_binary(Value), byte_size(Value) =< 32768 ->
    case binary:match(Value, <<0>>) of
        nomatch -> ok;
        _ -> {error, #{code => invalid_option_value}}
    end;
value(_) -> {error, #{code => invalid_option_value}}.

profile(#{major := Major, minor := Minor, patch := Patch, tracking := false}) ->
    Profile = <<(integer_to_binary(Major))/binary, $., (integer_to_binary(Minor))/binary, Patch/binary>>,
    case lists:member(Profile, tmux_option_data:versions()) of
        true -> {ok, Profile};
        false -> {error, #{code => unsupported_option_catalogue, version => Profile}}
    end;
profile(_) -> {error, #{code => unsupported_option_catalogue}}.

find(_, Name, []) -> {error, #{code => unsupported_tmux_option, name => Name}};
find(Profile, Name, [{Versions, Meta} | Rest]) ->
    case lists:member(Profile, Versions) of
        true -> {ok, Meta};
        false -> find(Profile, Name, Rest)
    end.

read_result({ok, #{stdout := Output}}, Name, Index, Meta, Version) ->
    case tmux_option_codec:decode(Name, Output, Meta, Version) of
        {ok, Entries} when is_map(Entries), Index =/= none ->
            case maps:find(Index, Entries) of {ok, Value} -> {ok, Value}; error -> none end;
        Result -> Result
    end;
read_result({error, #{code := command_error, stderr := Stderr}} = Error, <<$@, _/binary>> = Name, _, _, _) ->
    case Stderr =:= <<"invalid option: ", Name/binary, $\n>> of true -> none; false -> Error end;
read_result(Result, _, _, _, _) -> Result.

-module(tmux_pane).
-moduledoc """
Create, observe and rearrange panes using registered physical IDs.

`split/2` accepts a pane or a window; a window means its active pane
at execution. Options (`t:split_options/0`) are direction
(horizontal or vertical), size ({cells, N} or {percent, N}), before,
full_size, zoom, cwd, env, launch and detach. It defaults to a detached
vertical split. `get/2` returns newly observed fields; existing rows
remain unchanged. Reads span several commands and do not claim atomicity.
Launch and environment options follow `tmux_session:create/2`. An absent or
zero tmux pane_pid is represented as none. A captured positive PID is an
observation, not a guarantee that the process remains alive.

A successful split followed by a failed observation retains the completed
mutation and command result in its error. `kill/1` returns the
command result. Detached or stale references cannot act. `resize_command/2`
builds a reusable value without tmux I/O; the other calls perform I/O after
validation.

`send_text/2` sends up to 2,000 literal bytes, including NUL, in one
command using tmux's hexadecimal key form. It adds no Enter key and never
splits a large input into partially applied commands. `send_keys/2`
accepts up to 256 named keys, single UTF-8 characters, {function, 1..12} and
{control, <<Letter>>}. Named keys are enter, tab, escape, backspace, space,
up, down, left, right, home, 'end', insert, delete, page_up, page_down and
back_tab. Terminal modes still govern how input is consumed; command
completion does not mean a program processed it.

`capture/2` returns stdout bytes unchanged, including final
newlines. Options (`t:capture_options/0`) are start and 'end' (line
integers or all), join_lines, escape_sequences, escape_control,
retain_trailing_spaces, alternate, pending and quiet. Defaults are tmux's
current-screen capture without escapes, joined wraps or padding. The
endpoint's output limit applies; an oversized capture returns an error.

Use `join/3`, `move/3` and `swap/3` to rearrange existing panes without
respawning their processes. `break/4` takes an explicit source window link:
breaking a window's only pane moves that membership, while breaking one of
several panes creates a new physical window. The [topology guide](panes.md)
shows the distinction. Use `get/2` or a new snapshot for updated parents and
indexes; actions leave captured values unchanged.

`pipe/3` connects a tmux-owned shell process to pane output, input or both.
It protects the shell text from tmux hash/strftime expansion; shell quoting
remains the caller's responsibility. `stop_pipe/1` closes that native pipe.
These actions do not create an Erlang output subscription or transfer process
ownership to the endpoint. Use an application acknowledgement for consumer
readiness, delivered bytes and job completion.
""".
-export([split/2, get/2, kill/1, resize/2, respawn/2, send_text/2, send_keys/2,
         capture/2, break/4, join/3, move/3, swap/3, pipe/3, stop_pipe/1]).
-export([resize_command/2]).

-export_type([split_options/0, capture_options/0, resize_options/0, respawn_options/0,
              coordinate/0, key/0, break_options/0, join_options/0, swap_options/0,
              pipe_command/0, pipe_options/0]).
-doc "Explicit shell code: a nonempty NUL-free binary, with no tmux format or strftime expansion.".
-type pipe_command() :: #{shell := binary()}.
-doc "Pipe direction defaults to output. toggle defaults false; true closes an existing pipe instead of replacing it.".
-type pipe_options() :: #{direction => output | input | both, toggle => boolean()}.
-doc """
Break placement: explicit destination index, optional literal window name.
detach defaults true.
""".
-type break_options() :: #{index := tmux_window_link:index(), name => binary(),
    detach => boolean()}.
-doc """
Join/move geometry: detach true, vertical split by default. before and
full_size follow tmux layout rules.
""".
-type join_options() :: #{direction => horizontal | vertical,
    size => {cells,1..2147483647} | {percent,1..100}, detach => boolean(),
    before => boolean(), full_size => boolean()}.
-doc """
Swap controls: detach defaults true; zoom maps to tmux -Z to retain zoom.
""".
-type swap_options() :: #{detach => boolean(), zoom => boolean()}.
-doc "Split geometry, placement and explicit launch options. Defaults to a detached vertical split.".
-type split_options() :: #{direction => horizontal | vertical,
    size => {cells,1..2147483647} | {percent,1..100}, before => boolean(),
    full_size => boolean(), zoom => boolean(), cwd => binary(),
    env => #{binary() => binary()}, launch => tmux_command:launch_spec(), detach => boolean()}.
-doc "Requested absolute pane dimensions in cells. Supply at least one dimension; tmux can clamp it to fit the layout.".
-type resize_options() :: #{width := 1..65535, height => 1..65535} |
                          #{width => 1..65535, height := 1..65535}.
-doc "Respawn options. Defaults: force false, launch previous, saved cwd. Environment augments tmux's resolved session environment for this spawn.".
-type respawn_options() :: #{force => boolean(), launch => tmux_command:respawn_spec(),
                             cwd => binary(), env => #{binary() => binary()}}.
-doc "A capture line coordinate, or all for tmux's full available range.".
-type coordinate() :: -2147483648..32767 | all.
-doc "Capture range and rendering flags. Byte output and its final newline are preserved.".
-type capture_options() :: #{start => coordinate(), 'end' => coordinate(),
    join_lines => boolean(), escape_sequences => boolean(), escape_control => boolean(),
    retain_trailing_spaces => boolean(), alternate => boolean(), pending => boolean(), quiet => boolean()}.
-doc "A validated named key, single UTF-8 character, function key or control-letter key.".
-type key() :: binary() | enter | tab | escape | backspace | space | up | down | left | right |
    home | 'end' | insert | delete | page_up | page_down | back_tab |
    {function,1..12} | {control,binary()}.

-doc """
Split a pane, or the supplied window's active pane, and observe the new pane.
Defaults to a detached vertical split. Options and launch semantics are
described in the module docs. Performs I/O; a post-creation read error retains
the completed mutation rather than pretending that no pane was created.
""".
-spec split(tmux_model:pane() | tmux_model:window(), split_options()) ->
    {ok, tmux_model:pane()} | {error, map()}.
split(Row, Options) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Flags, Launch} ?= tmux_args:launch_options(Options,
            [{direction, direction, <<>>}, {size, size, <<"-l">>},
             {before, flag, <<"-b">>}, {full_size, flag, <<"-f">>}, {zoom, flag, <<"-Z">>}]),
        {ok, Server, Target} ?= tmux_target:resolve([pane, window], Row),
        {ok, Result} ?= tmux_target:run(Server, <<"split-window">>,
            [<<"-P">>, <<"-F">>, <<"#{pane_id}">>, <<"-t">>, Target] ++
            Flags ++ [<<"--">> | Launch]),
        tmux_observe:created(Server, pane, Result)
    end.

-doc """
Read fresh fields for a physical pane ID. Performs I/O and returns target_gone
for a vanished pane. A captured PID remains an observation, not a live-process
guarantee.
""".
-spec get(tmux_server:t(), tmux_model:pane_id()) -> {ok, tmux_model:pane()} | {error, map()}.
get(Server, Id) -> tmux_observe:get(Server, pane, Id).

-doc """
Destroy this registered pane. Performs I/O after validating its origin and
stable ID; it never falls back to a positional target.
""".
-spec kill(tmux_model:pane()) -> {ok, map()} | {error, map()}.
kill(Pane) -> tmux_target:act(pane, Pane, <<"kill-pane">>, []).

-doc """
Connect a shell process to this registered physical pane, performing I/O.
An explicit nonempty `#{shell => Command}` is required (`t:pipe_command/0`).
tmux hash formats and strftime directives are escaped so the shell receives
the supplied text.
This does not quote values interpolated into shell code; the caller owns that
quoting. Executable argv is not accepted by this shell-only native command.
Encoding follows `tmux_command:literal_format/2` in time mode. A percent-bearing
command above its native 8191-byte intermediate limit returns `format_limit`
before dispatch, preserving any existing pipe.

`direction` (`t:pipe_options/0`) is `output` (default: pane output to child
stdin), `input` (child stdout to pane input) or `both`. `toggle` defaults false,
replacing any existing pipe. True maps to native `-o`: close an existing pipe without
starting another, or open one when none exists. A stopped pipe and replacement
can discard pending output. Await consumer acknowledgements before closing
if delivered bytes matter. This is a live PTY byte stream, not rendered
capture text or replay of terminal history; terminal modes affect its bytes.

The child is started by tmux through `/bin/sh -c`. Its stderr is discarded;
unused directions are routed to the native null device. No pane cwd or
environment copying is promised. A successful command result does not prove
exec success, readiness, delivery or child exit. The process is tmux-owned;
`tmux_server:close/1` preserves the borrowed pane and its pipe. This is not an
Erlang subscription with library flow control. Use `stop_pipe/1` to close the
pipe; stopping is not process cancellation or a wait for job completion.
""".
-spec pipe(tmux_model:pane(), pipe_command(), pipe_options()) ->
    {ok, map()} | {error, map()}.
pipe(Pane, #{shell := Shell} = Command, Options)
  when map_size(Command) =:= 1, is_binary(Shell), byte_size(Shell) > 0 ->
    maybe
        {ok, Flags} ?= tmux_args:options(Options,
            [{direction, pipe_direction, <<>>}, {toggle, flag, <<"-o">>}],
            #{direction => output}),
        {ok, Literal} ?= tmux_command:literal_format(Shell, time),
        {ok, Server, Target} ?= tmux_target:resolve(pane, Pane),
        tmux_target:run(Server, <<"pipe-pane">>,
            Flags ++ [<<"-t">>, Target, <<"--">>, Literal])
    end;
pipe(_, _, _) -> {error, #{code => invalid_pipe_command}}.

-doc """
Close this registered pane's native pipe, performing I/O. On a live pane,
closing an already closed pipe succeeds. An exited pane can produce a native
command error; a vanished ID returns `target_gone`.

Closing can discard pending bytes. It neither kills nor waits for an arbitrary
shell job started by `pipe/3`; applications must verify consumption and
process completion themselves. The endpoint does not own that shell process.
""".
-spec stop_pipe(tmux_model:pane()) -> {ok, map()} | {error, map()}.
stop_pipe(Pane) -> tmux_target:act(pane, Pane, <<"pipe-pane">>, []).

-doc """
Break a physical pane through its explicit source membership into a destination
session/index. Source, link and session must have the same registered owner.
The source link's expected window and the pane's observed parent are checked
before dispatch. The source selector also includes the stable pane ID, never
its positional index. Preflight and action are not atomic.

With multiple panes, tmux creates a new physical window. With only one pane,
it moves the selected source membership, preserving the existing window and
its other links. Moving the final membership out can remove the source session.
Pane IDs and processes remain; indexes and option inheritance can change.
name is a literal UTF-8 argument, subject to native name cleaning.
An occupied destination index is refused. detach defaults true; false selects
the destination membership. Session groups retain native synchronization.

Returns the command result consistently for both cases. Use `get/2` or
`tmux_window_link:get/3` for fresh observations. Even an eventual native error
can unzoom a window; this is not a transaction and is never retried.
""".
-spec break(tmux_model:pane(), tmux_model:window_link(), tmux_model:session(),
    break_options()) -> {ok, tmux_operation:completed()} | {error, map()}.
break(Pane, SourceLink, Session, Options) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Index, Flags} ?= break_options(Options),
        {ok, Server} ?= tmux_target:same_owner(pane, Pane, window_link, SourceLink),
        {ok, Server} ?= tmux_target:same_owner(pane, Pane, session, Session),
        {ok, Source} ?= tmux_target:linked_pane(Server, Pane, SourceLink),
        {ok, SessionTarget} ?= tmux_target:selector(session, tmux_model:get(id, Session)),
        Target = <<SessionTarget/binary, Index/binary>>,
        tmux_target:run(Server, <<"break-pane">>, Flags ++ [<<"-s">>, Source, <<"-t">>, Target])
    end.

-doc """
Move a source pane into a split beside the destination pane. Both physical IDs
must belong to the same registered owner and must differ. Geometry follows
`t:join_options/0`. Existing processes and pane IDs survive; dimensions,
indexes and inherited window options can change. Removing a window's last
pane destroys that physical window and its links, and can remove sessions.

Default detach true avoids selecting the resolved destination session; false
uses tmux's resolved session context for the destination pane. Shared physical
windows affect all their memberships. Returns the command result without
refreshing either row. Use `get/2` for current fields. No retry is performed.
""".
-spec join(tmux_model:pane(), tmux_model:pane(), join_options()) ->
    {ok, tmux_operation:completed()} | {error, map()}.
join(Source, Destination, Options) -> relocate(<<"join-pane">>, Source, Destination, Options).

-doc """
Rearrange a source pane beside the destination, including within one window.
Uses native move-pane, whose placement and lifetime behavior follow `join/3`.
Both calls use explicit physical IDs and leave captured rows unchanged.
""".
-spec move(tmux_model:pane(), tmux_model:pane(), join_options()) ->
    {ok, tmux_operation:completed()} | {error, map()}.
move(Source, Destination, Options) -> relocate(<<"move-pane">>, Source, Destination, Options).

-doc """
Exchange two panes' layout positions within or across physical windows.
Preserves their IDs and processes; parent windows, dimensions, indexes and
inherited options can change. Both rows require the same registered owner.
detach defaults true; active positions can still receive different panes.
zoom maps to native -Z. Identical IDs do not exchange panes, but native zoom
handling still runs; the default can unzoom even a same-pane swap.
Returns the command result; `get/2` observes the resulting values explicitly.
""".
-spec swap(tmux_model:pane(), tmux_model:pane(), swap_options()) ->
    {ok, tmux_operation:completed()} | {error, map()}.
swap(Source, Destination, Options) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Flags} ?= tmux_args:options(Options,
            [{detach, flag, <<"-d">>}, {zoom, flag, <<"-Z">>}], #{detach => true}),
        {ok, Server, From, To} ?= pane_targets(Source, Destination),
        tmux_target:run(Server, <<"swap-pane">>, Flags ++ [<<"-s">>, From, <<"-t">>, To])
    end.

relocate(Command, Source, Destination, Options) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Flags} ?= tmux_args:options(Options,
            [{detach, flag, <<"-d">>}, {direction, direction, <<>>},
             {size, size, <<"-l">>}, {before, flag, <<"-b">>},
             {full_size, flag, <<"-f">>}], #{detach => true}),
        {ok, Server, From, To} ?= pane_targets(Source, Destination),
        ok ?= case From =:= To of true -> {error, #{code => same_pane}}; false -> ok end,
        tmux_target:run(Server, Command, Flags ++ [<<"-s">>, From, <<"-t">>, To])
    end.

pane_targets(Source, Destination) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Server} ?= tmux_target:same_owner(pane, Source, pane, Destination),
        {ok, From} ?= tmux_target:selector(pane, tmux_model:get(id, Source)),
        {ok, To} ?= tmux_target:selector(pane, tmux_model:get(id, Destination)),
        {ok, Server, From, To}
    end.

break_options(Options) when is_map(Options) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Index} ?= case maps:find(index, Options) of
            {ok, Value} when is_integer(Value, 0, 2147483647) ->
                {ok, integer_to_binary(Value)};
            {ok, _} -> {error, #{code => invalid_option, path => [index]}};
            error -> {error, #{code => missing_option, path => [index]}}
        end,
        {ok, Flags} ?= tmux_args:options(maps:remove(index, Options),
            [{detach, flag, <<"-d">>}, {name, text, <<"-n">>}], #{detach => true}),
        {ok, Index, Flags}
    end;
break_options(_) -> {error, #{code => invalid_options, path => []}}.

-doc """
Request an absolute width, height or both for this registered physical pane.
Performs I/O after validating dimensions and origin. tmux can clamp the
request to its layout constraints and can resize neighboring panes. Resizing a
tiled pane unzooms its window. Use `get/2` for actual dimensions; the input
row is unchanged. The accepted library range is not a promise that every
server accepts every dimension: tmux versions can impose tighter limits and
return a command error.

An empty request is rejected before dispatch:

```erlang
1> tmux_pane:resize(invalid_row, #{}).
{error,#{code => empty_resize}}
```
""".
-spec resize(tmux_model:pane(), resize_options()) ->
    {ok, tmux_operation:completed()} | {error, tmux_operation:failure()}.
resize(Pane, Options) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Command} ?= resize_command(Pane, Options),
        tmux_target:execute(Command)
    end.

-doc """
Build a resize command without tmux I/O. Uses the dimensions and validation
rules of `resize/2`, preserving the row's captured origin and stable pane ID.
Endpoint liveness and native layout constraints are checked during execution.
Submit through `tmux_server:command/3` or `tmux_operation:start/3`.

```erlang
1> tmux_pane:resize_command(invalid_row, #{}).
{error,#{code => empty_resize}}
```
""".
-spec resize_command(tmux_model:pane(), resize_options()) -> {ok, tmux_command:t()} | {error, map()}.
resize_command(Pane, Options) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Flags} ?= tmux_args:options(Options,
            [{width, dimension, <<"-x">>}, {height, dimension, <<"-y">>}]),
        ok ?= case Flags of [] -> {error, #{code => empty_resize}}; _ -> ok end,
        {ok, Origin, Target} ?= tmux_target:captured_target(pane, Pane),
        tmux_command:generated(pane_resize, Origin, Flags ++ [<<"-t">>, Target])
    end.

-doc """
Respawn this registered physical pane, keeping its pane ID. force defaults
false and a running pane normally returns command_error. force = true lets
tmux close its existing PTY before spawning again. This acknowledges the tmux
command, not former-job termination or successful application initialization.
The old PTY can already be closed if a later spawn step fails.

launch defaults to previous, reusing tmux's saved argv or shell. An explicit
argv or shell map replaces that command. default_shell is invalid here because
absent respawn arguments mean saved-command reuse. Omitted cwd retains the
saved launch directory, rather than the program's current directory. env
augments the session environment tmux resolves for this physical pane; a
captured membership does not pin that context. Prior per-spawn overrides are
not automatically reapplied. Other launch rules follow
`tmux_session:create/2`.

Performs I/O after validation. Existing rows retain their observations; use
`get/2` and an application readiness condition to inspect the new process. An
uncertain result is not permission to replay this mutation automatically.

Unsupported launch modes fail before dispatch:

```erlang
1> tmux_pane:respawn(invalid_row, #{launch => default_shell}).
{error,#{code => invalid_launch}}
```
""".
-spec respawn(tmux_model:pane(), respawn_options()) ->
    {ok, tmux_operation:completed()} | {error, tmux_operation:failure()}.
respawn(Pane, Options) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Flags, Launch} ?= tmux_args:respawn_options(Options),
        {ok, Server, Target} ?= tmux_target:resolve(pane, Pane),
        tmux_target:run(Server, <<"respawn-pane">>,
            Flags ++ [<<"-t">>, Target, <<"--">> | Launch])
    end.

-doc """
Send at most 2,000 literal bytes as hexadecimal tmux keys. Adds no Enter key
and does not invoke a shell. Performs I/O in one command; oversized input is
rejected before partial submission. Completion does not prove that a terminal
program processed the input.
""".
-spec send_text(tmux_model:pane(), binary()) -> {ok, map()} | {error, map()}.
send_text(Pane, Bytes) when is_binary(Bytes), byte_size(Bytes) =< 2000 ->
    Hex = [integer_to_binary(Byte, 16) || <<Byte>> <= Bytes],
    send(Pane, [<<"-H">>], Hex);
send_text(_, Bytes) when is_binary(Bytes) -> {error, #{code => command_limit}};
send_text(_, _) -> {error, #{code => invalid_text}}.

-doc """
Send at most 256 validated key tokens. Named keys, single UTF-8 characters,
function keys and control-letter tuples are supported. Performs I/O; terminal
modes determine the resulting input bytes. Use `send_text/2` for arbitrary
bytes.
""".
-spec send_keys(tmux_model:pane(), [key()]) -> {ok, map()} | {error, map()}.
send_keys(Pane, Keys) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Arguments} ?= keys(Keys, 256, []),
        send(Pane, [], Arguments)
    end.

-doc """
Capture terminal bytes, preserving final newlines. Options select line range,
joined wraps, escapes, alternate screen and padding; defaults follow tmux
current-screen capture. Performs I/O and returns an explicit output-limit
error instead of silently truncating.
""".
-spec capture(tmux_model:pane(), capture_options()) -> {ok, binary()} | {error, map()}.
capture(Pane, Options) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Flags} ?= tmux_args:options(Options,
            [{start, coordinate, <<"-S">>}, {'end', coordinate, <<"-E">>},
             {join_lines, flag, <<"-J">>}, {escape_sequences, flag, <<"-e">>},
             {escape_control, flag, <<"-C">>}, {retain_trailing_spaces, flag, <<"-N">>},
             {alternate, flag, <<"-a">>}, {pending, flag, <<"-P">>}, {quiet, flag, <<"-q">>}]),
        {ok, Server, Target} ?= tmux_target:resolve(pane, Pane),
        {ok, #{stdout := Bytes}} ?= tmux_target:run(Server, <<"capture-pane">>,
            [<<"-p">>, <<"-t">>, Target | Flags]),
        {ok, Bytes}
    end.

send(Pane, Flags, Arguments) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Server, Target} ?= tmux_target:resolve(pane, Pane),
        tmux_target:run(Server, <<"send-keys">>,
            [<<"-t">>, Target] ++ Flags ++ [<<"--">> | Arguments])
    end.

keys([], _, Acc) -> {ok, lists:reverse(Acc)};
keys([_ | _], 0, _) -> {error, #{code => command_limit}};
keys([Key | Rest], Remaining, Acc) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Encoded} ?= key(Key),
        keys(Rest, Remaining - 1, [Encoded | Acc])
    end;
keys(_, _, _) -> {error, #{code => invalid_keys}}.

key({function, N}) when is_integer(N, 1, 12) -> {ok, <<$F, (integer_to_binary(N))/binary>>};
key({control, <<C>>}) when C >= $a, C =< $z -> {ok, <<"C-", C>>};
key(Bytes) when is_binary(Bytes), byte_size(Bytes) =< 4 ->
    case unicode:characters_to_list(Bytes) of
        [Codepoint] when Codepoint >= 32, Codepoint =/= 127 -> {ok, Bytes};
        _ -> {error, #{code => invalid_key}}
    end;
key(Name) ->
    Names = #{enter => <<"Enter">>, tab => <<"Tab">>, escape => <<"Escape">>,
        backspace => <<"BSpace">>, space => <<"Space">>, up => <<"Up">>, down => <<"Down">>,
        left => <<"Left">>, right => <<"Right">>, home => <<"Home">>, 'end' => <<"End">>,
        insert => <<"IC">>, delete => <<"DC">>, page_up => <<"PPage">>,
        page_down => <<"NPage">>, back_tab => <<"BTab">>},
    case maps:find(Name, Names) of
        {ok, Value} -> {ok, Value};
        error -> {error, #{code => invalid_key}}
    end.

-module(tmux_query).
-moduledoc """
Build and execute explicit queries over the tmux graph.

Use `fetch/1` to execute a query. Constructors,
`where/2`, `limit/2`, `pushdown/2` and
`explain/1` perform no tmux I/O. Criteria are validated when added,
and repeated conditions conjoin. Fetching returns an ordered `m:tmux_select`
selection backed by a complete `m:tmux_snapshot` graph. By default the full
captured view is filtered locally. Enable native candidate exclusion with
`pushdown/2`: it can add a scan without reducing complete-graph hydration. The
candidate is a necessary condition; the full filter still runs before the limit.

Captures span commands and are not atomic. Candidate IDs excluded at one
observation cannot be recovered by later local filtering. Disabling
`pushdown/2` evaluates the complete captured view without an
earlier candidate exclusion. Numeric candidate fields come from the restricted
scalar codec and must agree with the capture's scalar observations. Text and
relationships remain local.

Captures emit bounded OTP Logger reports with their snapshot ID and endpoint
generation. See [runtime diagnostics](diagnostics.md) for observation cost,
rejection reports and configuration.

```erlang
1> Q0 = tmux_query:panes(unopened), ok.
ok
2> Q = tmux_query:where(#{width => #{gte => 120}}, Q0), ok.
ok
3> maps:get(format, maps:get(candidate, tmux_query:explain(Q))).
<<"1">>
4> Pushed = tmux_query:pushdown(true, Q), ok.
ok
5> maps:get(format, maps:get(candidate, tmux_query:explain(Pushed))).
<<"#{e|>=|:#{pane_width},120}">>
```
""".
-export([panes/1, windows/1, window_links/1, sessions/1, where/2, limit/2,
         pushdown/2, explain/1, fetch/1, fetch/2]).
-export_type([t/0]).
-record(query, {server :: tmux_server:t(), entity :: tmux_schema:entity(),
                filter = none :: none | tmux_filter:t(),
                limit = infinity :: infinity | 0..65536,
                pushdown = false :: boolean()}).
-export_type([fetch_options/0, plan/0, candidate/0, local_reason/0,
              source_command/0, command_plan/0]).
-doc "Capture bounds plus an explicitly requested single inconsistent-capture retry; default retry is zero.".
-type fetch_options() :: #{deadline_ms => 1..600000, max_rows => 1..65536,
    max_bytes => 1..67108864, hydration => tmux_server:hydration(),
    consistency => observed | atomic, retry => 0 | 1}.
-doc """
Why part of a predicate stays local. field and relation contain stable schema
IDs, not Erlang names or tmux formats. An unsupported leaf may broaden the
native condition; it never removes the full local predicate.
""".
-type local_reason() :: #{reason := disabled | format_limit | inexact_negation |
        unqualified_scalar_codec | complete_relationship_required,
    field => binary(), relation => binary(), operator => tmux_schema:operator()}.
-doc """
Native necessary condition. format is a rendered tmux expression; exact means
the translation covers the whole predicate for one observed state. A true
fallback can admit every row. numeric_range describes qualified integer
conversion, and is omitted for disabled/oversized fallback plans.
""".
-type candidate() :: #{format := binary(), exact := boolean(),
    local_only := [local_reason()], numeric_range => {0, 9007199254740991}}.
-doc """
Diagnostic command template, not executable argv. Scan templates carry args;
text/byte hydration escapes each field once before column framing. Unqualified
schema fields use isolated target = observed_id templates, resolved only while
capturing. codec states how returned data is framed, including the
version-specific print layer. This value grants no atomicity or
persistent-connection guarantee.
""".
-type source_command() ::
    #{entity := tmux_schema:entity(), command := binary(), format := binary(),
      transport := one_shot, codec := scalar_spine,
      kind := tmux_schema:entity(), args := [binary()], filter => binary()} |
    #{entity := tmux_schema:entity(), fields := [atom()], command := binary(),
      format := binary(), transport := one_shot,
      codec := escaped_columns_v1, args := [binary()]} |
    #{entity := tmux_schema:entity(), field := atom(), command := binary(),
      format := binary(), transport := one_shot,
      codec := id_prefixed_quoted_field, target := observed_id}.
-doc """
Capture phases: initial identity/scalar scans, optional candidate scans,
complete text/byte hydration and final identity/scalar scans. hydration gives
the default batched templates; isolated_hydration describes the explicit
isolated option and unqualified-field fallback. An empty server skips
window/pane scans. Execution still validates capture bounds and can fail.
""".
-type command_plan() :: #{initial_spine := [source_command()],
    candidate := [source_command()], hydration := [source_command()],
    isolated_hydration := [source_command()],
    final_spine := [source_command()], empty_server := skip_window_and_pane_scans}.
-doc """
Pure explanation of a query. pushdown reports whether candidate exclusion is
enabled (disabled by default). residual is the full portable predicate, required
lists coverage requirements, and limit applies after residual evaluation.
ordering and deduplication name the identity policy, not arbitrary map order.
capabilities describes the planner baseline without probing a live endpoint.

Capture spans commands. Candidate scalar values are checked against the first
scan; text and relationships are later observations. Excluded rows cannot be
recovered after state changes. Even an exact candidate is not an atomic query.
""".
-type plan() :: #{entity := tmux_schema:entity(), pushdown := boolean(), candidate := candidate(),
    residual := tmux_filter:wire_document(), required := [tmux_snapshot:requirement()],
    limit := infinity | 0..65536, commands := command_plan(), hydration := complete_graph,
    ordering := session_index_window | numeric_id,
    deduplication := membership | physical_id,
    capabilities := #{minimum_tmux := binary(), transport := one_shot},
    consistency := observed, atomic := false,
    candidate_scalars := same_row_checked_against_spine,
    text_and_relations := later_observations,
    temporal_limit := excluded_rows_cannot_be_recovered}.

-doc """
An immutable description of future tmux reads. Only fetch executes it.
""".
-opaque t() :: #query{}.

-doc """
Describe a future server-wide physical pane query. Performs no I/O; `fetch/1`
is the execution boundary.
""".
-spec panes(tmux_server:t()) -> t().
panes(Server) -> #query{server = Server, entity = pane}.
-doc """
Describe a future query over unique physical windows. Performs no I/O.
""".
-spec windows(tmux_server:t()) -> t().
windows(Server) -> #query{server = Server, entity = window}.
-doc """
Describe a future query over session-relative window memberships. Repeated
physical windows retain distinct membership identity. Performs no I/O.
""".
-spec window_links(tmux_server:t()) -> t().
window_links(Server) -> #query{server = Server, entity = window_link}.
-doc """
Describe a future server-wide session query without executing tmux.
""".
-spec sessions(tmux_server:t()) -> t().
sessions(Server) -> #query{server = Server, entity = session}.

-doc """
Validate trusted criteria for this entity and conjoin them with prior
conditions. Successive calls share the same normalized resource limits as one
flat conjunction. Each relationship quantifier retains its own scope. Returns
a new immutable query; malformed criteria raise bad_filter. Performs no I/O.
""".
-spec where(map() | tmux_filter:t(), t()) -> t().
where(Criteria, #query{entity = Entity, filter = Previous} = Query) ->
    Filter = tmux_filter:new_or_error(Entity, Criteria),
    Combined = case Previous of
        none -> Filter;
        _ ->
            case tmux_filter:conjoin(Previous, Filter) of
                {ok, Result} -> Result;
                {error, Detail} -> erlang:error({bad_filter, Detail}, none,
                    [{error_info, #{module => tmux_error}}])
            end
    end,
    Query#query{filter = Combined}.

-doc """
Set a final result limit from 0 through 65536, applied after residual
filtering and identity handling. It is not a candidate-fetch limit. Performs
no I/O; invalid counts raise bad_query_limit.
""".
-spec limit(0..65536, t()) -> t().
limit(Count, Query) when is_integer(Count, 0, 65536) -> Query#query{limit = Count};
limit(Count, _) -> erlang:error({bad_query_limit, Count}, none,
    [{error_info, #{module => tmux_error}}]).

-doc """
Enable or disable native candidate exclusion, returning a new query. The
default is disabled: evaluate the complete captured view locally. Enabling it
can add a candidate scan without reducing hydration; neither mode promises an
atomic graph. Performs no I/O.
""".
-spec pushdown(boolean(), t()) -> t().
pushdown(Enabled, Query) when is_boolean(Enabled) -> Query#query{pushdown = Enabled}.

-doc """
Inspect command templates, necessary candidate conditions, full residual,
hydration, required fields, ordering and temporal assumptions. Performs no I/O
and does not contact the endpoint to claim dynamic capabilities.
""".
-spec explain(t()) -> plan().
explain(#query{entity = Entity, limit = Limit, pushdown = Enabled} = Query) ->
    Filter = filter(Query),
    Candidate = case Enabled of
        true -> tmux_query_plan:compile(Filter);
        false -> #{format => <<"1">>, exact => false, local_only => [#{reason => disabled}]}
    end,
    #{entity => Entity, pushdown => Enabled, candidate => Candidate, residual => tmux_filter:to_wire(Filter),
      required => tmux_filter:requirements(Filter), limit => Limit,
      commands => tmux_observe:plan(Entity, maps:get(format, Candidate)),
      hydration => complete_graph, ordering => case Entity of
          window_link -> session_index_window; _ -> numeric_id end,
      deduplication => case Entity of window_link -> membership; _ -> physical_id end,
      capabilities => #{minimum_tmux => <<"3.3a">>, transport => one_shot},
      consistency => observed, atomic => false,
      candidate_scalars => same_row_checked_against_spine,
      text_and_relations => later_observations,
      temporal_limit => excluded_rows_cannot_be_recovered}.

-doc """
Execute with default capture bounds and no retry. Returns an ordered selection
whose complete graph remains locally readable. See `fetch/2` for resource
limits, requested retries and operational errors.
""".
-spec fetch(t()) -> {ok, tmux_select:t()} | {error, map()}.
fetch(Query) -> fetch(Query, #{}).

-doc """
Execute the planned observation, full local predicate and final limit.

Capture options are those of `tmux_server:snapshot/2`. retry is 0 (default) or
1 and retries only inconsistent_capture, within the original capture deadline.
The retry is a new read-only capture. No mutations are retried. Invalid
capture requests return tagged errors, including unsupported consistency.

```erlang
1> tmux_query:fetch(tmux_query:panes(unopened), #{retry => 2}).
{error,#{code => invalid_query_options}}
```
""".
-spec fetch(t(), fetch_options()) -> {ok, tmux_select:t()} | {error, map()}.
fetch(Query, Options) when is_map(Options) ->
    Retry = maps:get(retry, Options, 0),
    Capture = maps:remove(retry, Options),
    case is_integer(Retry, 0, 1) of
        true -> fetch_attempt(Query, explain(Query), Capture, Retry, 1,
                              erlang:monotonic_time(millisecond));
        false -> {error, #{code => invalid_query_options}}
    end;
fetch(_, _) -> {error, #{code => invalid_query_options}}.

filter(#query{filter = none, entity = Entity}) -> tmux_filter:new_or_error(Entity, #{});
filter(#query{filter = Filter}) -> Filter.

fetch_attempt(#query{server = Server} = Query, Plan, Options, Retry, Attempt, Started) ->
    RunPlan = Plan#{attempt => Attempt, query_started => Started},
    case tmux_observe:query(Server, RunPlan, Options) of
        {ok, Snapshot, Keys} -> select(Query, Snapshot, Keys);
        {error, #{code := inconsistent_capture}} when Retry > 0 ->
            Deadline = maps:get(deadline_ms, Options, 2500),
            Remaining = Deadline - (erlang:monotonic_time(millisecond) - Started),
            case Remaining > 0 of
                true -> fetch_attempt(Query, Plan, Options#{deadline_ms => Remaining},
                                      Retry - 1, Attempt + 1, Started);
                false -> {error, #{code => capture_deadline}}
            end;
        {error, _} = Error -> Error
    end.

select(#query{entity = Entity, limit = Limit} = Query, Snapshot, Keys) ->
    Selection = case Entity of
        pane -> tmux_select:panes(Snapshot);
        window -> tmux_select:windows(Snapshot);
        window_link -> tmux_select:window_links(Snapshot);
        session -> tmux_select:sessions(Snapshot)
    end,
    Set = maps:from_keys(Keys, true),
    Candidates = tmux_select:filter(fun(Row) -> maps:is_key(identity(Row), Set) end, Selection),
    maybe
        {ok, Matched} ?= tmux_select:try_where(filter(Query), Candidates),
        {ok, case Limit of infinity -> Matched; _ -> tmux_select:take(Limit, Matched) end}
    end.

identity(Row) ->
    case tmux_model:entity(Row) of
        window_link -> {tmux_model:get(session_id, Row), tmux_model:get(index, Row),
                        tmux_model:get(window_id, Row)};
        _ -> tmux_model:get(id, Row)
    end.

-module(tmux_schema).
-moduledoc """
Validate schema-defined observations and normalize scalar values.

Field names come from the generated registry, never record reflection or
payload-created atoms. Text is validated UTF-8; byte fields preserve arbitrary
binaries. Integer normalization uses the shared exact JSON integer range.
`m:tmux_model` validates rows and `m:tmux_filter` validates criteria through
this schema. The [field reference](fields.md) lists fields and relationships.
""".
-export([fields/1, relations/1, field/2, normalize/2, value/2, operators/1]).
-export_type([entity/0, error_detail/0, value_type/0, field_metadata/0,
              relation_metadata/0, operator/0]).

-doc """
The built-in tmux graph entities; window_link represents a session membership.
""".
-type entity() :: session | window | window_link | pane.
-doc """
Structured boundary validation errors with a code and input path.
""".
-type error_detail() :: #{code := atom(), path := [term()], atom() => term()}.
-doc "Scalar categories used by normalization and operator validation; IDs remain binaries.".
-type value_type() :: session_id | window_id | pane_id | boolean | uint |
                      integer | text | bytes.
-doc """
Generated field contract. stable is a versioned portable identity; wire is the
JSON key. required controls construction and nullable permits known absence.
format is present only for directly observed tmux fields; derived fields omit
it. capture_codec identifies an admitted batched source encoding; its absence
selects isolated reads for that entity. minimum tightens an integer field's
lower bound. Field names themselves are the keys returned by `fields/1`, not
this map's wire or stable values.
""".
-type field_metadata() :: #{type := value_type(), wire := binary(),
    stable := binary(), required := boolean(), nullable := boolean(),
    format => binary(), capture_codec => escaped_columns_v1, minimum => integer()}.
-doc """
Generated relationship contract: kind is one or many; target names the related
entity. wire and stable have the same roles as in `t:field_metadata/0`.
Completeness belongs to snapshot coverage, not this static schema.
""".
-type relation_metadata() :: #{kind := one | many, target := entity(),
    wire := binary(), stable := binary()}.
-doc "Validated scalar operators. The field's type and nullability restrict this set.".
-type operator() :: equals | 'not' | in | not_in | lt | lte | gt | gte |
                    contains | starts_with | ends_with | regex | present.
-define(MAX_INTEGER, 9007199254740991).

-doc """
Return generated field metadata for a known entity, or a tagged unknown_entity
error. Field names, wire names and stable IDs are allowlisted; this is not
reflection over arbitrary record fields.
""".
-spec fields(entity()) -> {ok, #{atom() => field_metadata()}} | {error, error_detail()}.
fields(Entity) ->
    case lists:member(Entity, tmux_schema_data:entities()) of
        true -> {ok, tmux_schema_data:fields(Entity)};
        false -> {error, #{code => unknown_entity, path => []}}
    end.

-doc """
Return generated relationship metadata, including target entities and one/many
cardinality. Performs no I/O.
""".
-spec relations(entity()) -> {ok, #{atom() => relation_metadata()}} | {error, error_detail()}.
relations(Entity) ->
    maybe
        {ok, _} ?= fields(Entity),
        {ok, tmux_schema_data:relations(Entity)}
    end.

-doc """
Look up one permitted field by its Erlang atom name. Unknown names return a
tagged error; this does not turn input strings into atoms.
""".
-spec field(entity(), atom()) -> {ok, field_metadata()} | {error, error_detail()}.
field(Entity, Field) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Fields} ?= fields(Entity),
        case maps:find(Field, Fields) of
            {ok, Metadata} -> {ok, Metadata};
            error -> {error, #{code => unknown_field, path => [Field]}}
        end
    end.

-doc """
Validate a domain-field map and normalize its scalar observations, retaining
not_loaded/unavailable distinctly and deriving schema-defined values. Performs
no I/O; constructors and action boundaries still validate records.
""".
-spec normalize(entity(), map()) -> {ok, map()} | {error, error_detail()}.
normalize(Entity, Input) when is_map(Input) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Fields} ?= fields(Entity),
        ok ?= known_keys(maps:keys(Input), Fields),
        {ok, Normalized} ?= observations(lists:sort(maps:to_list(Fields)), Input, #{}),
        derived(Entity, Normalized)
    end;
normalize(_Entity, _Input) ->
    {error, #{code => invalid_object, path => []}}.

-doc """
Validate and normalize one value against generated field metadata. Integral
JSON numbers obey the exact shared integer range and field bounds; text is
validated UTF-8, while bytes remain arbitrary binaries. Performs no I/O.
""".
-spec value(map(), term()) -> {ok, term()} | {error, error_detail()}.
value(#{nullable := true}, none) ->
    {ok, none};
value(#{type := boolean}, Value) when is_boolean(Value) ->
    {ok, Value};
value(#{type := text} = Metadata, Value) when is_binary(Value) ->
    case unicode:characters_to_binary(Value, utf8, utf8) of
        Value -> {ok, Value};
        _ -> invalid(Metadata)
    end;
value(#{type := bytes}, Value) when is_binary(Value) ->
    {ok, Value};
value(#{type := Type} = Metadata, Value)
  when Type =:= integer; Type =:= uint ->
    DefaultMinimum = case Type of uint -> 0; integer -> -?MAX_INTEGER end,
    Minimum = maps:get(minimum, Metadata, DefaultMinimum),
    case Value of
        Integer when is_integer(Integer, Minimum, ?MAX_INTEGER) -> {ok, Integer};
        Float when is_float(Float), Float >= Minimum, Float =< ?MAX_INTEGER ->
            Integer = trunc(Float),
            case Integer == Float of
                true -> {ok, Integer};
                false -> invalid(Metadata)
            end;
        _ -> invalid(Metadata)
    end;
value(#{type := Type} = Metadata, Value)
  when Type =:= pane_id; Type =:= window_id; Type =:= session_id ->
    Prefix = case Type of pane_id -> $%; window_id -> $@; session_id -> $$ end,
    case valid_id(Prefix, Value) of
        true -> {ok, Value};
        false -> invalid(Metadata)
    end;
value(Metadata, _Value) ->
    invalid(Metadata).

-doc """
Return the permitted scalar operators for this field type and nullability. The
generated field reference uses this same validator. Performs no I/O.
""".
-spec operators(#{type := value_type(), nullable := boolean(), atom() => term()}) -> [operator()].
operators(#{type := Type, nullable := Nullable}) ->
    Base = [equals, 'not', in, not_in],
    Typed = case Type of
        uint -> [lt, lte, gt, gte];
        integer -> [lt, lte, gt, gte];
        text -> [contains, starts_with, ends_with, regex];
        bytes -> [contains, starts_with, ends_with];
        _ -> []
    end,
    Base ++ Typed ++ case Nullable of true -> [present]; false -> [] end.

known_keys([], _Fields) -> ok;
known_keys([Key | Rest], Fields) ->
    case maps:is_key(Key, Fields) of
        true -> known_keys(Rest, Fields);
        false -> {error, #{code => unknown_field, path => [Key]}}
    end.

observations([], _Input, Accumulator) -> {ok, Accumulator};
observations([{Name, Metadata} | Rest], Input, Accumulator) ->
    Raw = maps:get(Name, Input, not_loaded),
    case observation(Metadata, Raw) of
        {ok, Value} -> observations(Rest, Input, Accumulator#{Name => Value});
        {error, Detail} -> {error, Detail#{path => [Name]}}
    end.

observation(#{required := true}, Value)
  when Value =:= not_loaded; Value =:= unavailable ->
    {error, #{code => required_field, path => []}};
observation(_Metadata, Value) when Value =:= not_loaded; Value =:= unavailable ->
    {ok, Value};
observation(Metadata, Value) ->
    value(Metadata, Value).

derived(session, #{attached_count := Count, attached := Attached} = Fields)
  when is_integer(Count) ->
    Expected = Count > 0,
    case Attached of
        not_loaded -> {ok, Fields#{attached => Expected}};
        Expected -> {ok, Fields};
        _ -> {error, #{code => inconsistent_derived_value, path => [attached]}}
    end;
derived(_Entity, Fields) ->
    {ok, Fields}.

invalid(#{type := Type}) ->
    {error, #{code => invalid_value, path => [], expected => Type}}.

valid_id(Prefix, <<Prefix, Digits/binary>>) when byte_size(Digits) =< 32 ->
    case Digits of
        <<"0">> -> true;
        <<First, Rest/binary>> when First >= $1, First =< $9 -> digits(Rest);
        _ -> false
    end;
valid_id(_Prefix, _Value) -> false.

digits(<<>>) -> true;
digits(<<Digit, Rest/binary>>) when Digit >= $0, Digit =< $9 -> digits(Rest);
digits(_) -> false.

-module(tmux_scope).
-moduledoc """
Run synchronous work and cleanup while preserving both outcomes.

Use `run/2` around a resource whose handle remains in the caller's scope.
Use `run_or_error/2` for nested scopes or fail-fast programs that need the
callback's value directly and raise when cleanup fails.
`tmux_server:with_server/2` and `tmux_server:with_owned/2` also acquire their
resources and add recovery handles when cleanup fails. This module owns no
process, timeout or retry policy; the supplied functions own those contracts.
""".
-export([run/2, run_or_error/2]).
-export_type([exception/0, failure/0]).

-doc "The original exception class, reason and stack, retained as evidence.".
-type exception() :: {exception, error | exit | throw, term(), erlang:stacktrace()}.
-doc """
Both outcomes when cleanup failed. primary contains the callback's ordinary
return or exception; cleanup contains its separate error or exception.
Resource-specific wrappers may add recovery handles to this map.
""".
-type failure() :: #{code := scope_cleanup_failed,
    primary := {ok, term()} | exception(),
    cleanup := {error, term()} | exception(), atom() => term()}.

-doc """
Run a callback, then attempt cleanup once, synchronously in the calling process.
This function performs only the I/O supplied by those functions. The callback
has no library duration timer. Abrupt uncatchable caller death remains subject
to each resource's existing ownership policy.

Only ok proves cleanup success. Normalize resource-specific successful replies
inside the cleanup function. With successful cleanup, return {ok, Value} or
re-raise the original callback exception with its reason and stack. A callback
returning an error tuple is an ordinary value. Cleanup failure instead returns
{error, Failure} with `t:failure/0`, preserving both outcomes. An unexpected
cleanup return is recorded as invalid_cleanup_result.

Handle an inner scope's error explicitly when nesting scopes. Otherwise it is
an ordinary outer callback value. Keep resource handles for recovery; this
function does not infer ownership or retry cleanup.

```erlang
1> tmux_scope:run(fun() -> done end, fun() -> ok end).
{ok,done}
2> tmux_scope:run(fun() -> done end, fun() -> {error, enoent} end).
{error,#{code => scope_cleanup_failed,
         primary => {ok,done},cleanup => {error,enoent}}}
3> Work = fun() -> error(build_failed) end, ok.
ok
4> {error, F} = tmux_scope:run(Work, fun() -> {error, busy} end), ok.
ok
5> {exception, error, build_failed, [_ | _]} = maps:get(primary, F), ok.
ok
6> maps:get(cleanup, F).
{error,busy}
```
""".
-spec run(fun(() -> Value), fun(() -> ok | {error, term()})) ->
    {ok, Value} | {error, failure()}.
run(Function, Cleanup) when is_function(Function, 0), is_function(Cleanup, 0) ->
    Primary = outcome(Function),
    Retired = case outcome(Cleanup) of
        {ok, ok} -> ok;
        {ok, {error, _} = Error} -> Error;
        {ok, Other} -> {error, #{code => invalid_cleanup_result, value => Other}};
        {exception, _, _, _} = Exception -> Exception
    end,
    case {Primary, Retired} of
        {{ok, Value}, ok} -> {ok, Value};
        {{exception, Class, Reason, Stack}, ok} -> erlang:raise(Class, Reason, Stack);
        _ -> {error, #{code => scope_cleanup_failed,
                       primary => Primary, cleanup => Retired}}
    end.

-doc """
Run work and cleanup with `run/2`, returning the callback value directly.
Raises {scope_cleanup_failed, Failure} if cleanup fails, retaining both
outcomes in `t:failure/0`. With successful cleanup, callback exceptions retain
their original reason and stack. Nested raising scopes propagate an inner
failure through the outer scope while still attempting outer cleanup.
""".
-spec run_or_error(fun(() -> Value), fun(() -> ok | {error, term()})) -> Value.
run_or_error(Function, Cleanup) ->
    case run(Function, Cleanup) of
        {ok, Value} -> Value;
        {error, Failure} -> erlang:error({scope_cleanup_failed, Failure}, none,
            [{error_info, #{module => tmux_error}}])
    end.

outcome(Function) ->
    try {ok, Function()}
    catch Class:Reason:Stack -> {exception, Class, Reason, Stack}
    end.
