-module(tmux_snapshot).
-moduledoc """
Read an immutable captured graph without performing tmux I/O.

Server-wide lists use numeric ID order. Window links retain every membership,
including multiple indexes for the same window in one session. Session windows
are unique in first-link order; panes within a window use pane index order.
`related/3` accepts a row from this snapshot and returns a
tagged result. A row from another observation cannot silently select a
relationship in this one.

`metadata/1` records source calls, the capture interval,
endpoint generation and the observed server incarnation. Captures span
commands and are not atomic. Values remain readable after their endpoint
closes; actions still validate the row's registered origin. Coverage
distinguishes unloaded data from an empty collection and unavailable fields
from known absence. See the [graph guide](graph.md) for physical windows and
session memberships.
""".
-export([sessions/1, windows/1, window_links/1, panes/1, rows/2, get/3,
         related/3, metadata/1, coverage/1, require/2, build/2]).
-export_type([t/0, requirement/0, metadata/0, source_call/0,
              entity_coverage/0, coverage/0, query_metadata/0]).
-doc """
An immutable captured graph with identity, indexes, coverage and source
intervals.
""".
-opaque t() :: #{rows := map(), indexes := map(), edges := map(),
                 metadata := metadata(), coverage := coverage()}.
-doc """
A collection, field or complete relationship needed for faithful local
evaluation.
""".
-type requirement() :: {collection, tmux_schema:entity()} |
    {field | relation, tmux_schema:entity(), atom()}.
-doc """
One completed capture command and its stdout byte count. started and finished
are local monotonic microseconds, not wall-clock timestamps. The interval
includes identity preflight and command completion; it is not an atomic read.
""".
-type source_call() :: #{command := binary(), args := [binary()],
    started := integer(), finished := integer(), stdout_bytes := non_neg_integer()}.
-doc """
Collection completeness, field availability and relationship completeness. A
loaded field can hold a known value or known absence; inspect the row to
distinguish them. not_loaded never means empty, and unavailable never means
known absence. Completeness is relative to the captured source collection.
""".
-type entity_coverage() :: #{collection := complete | not_loaded,
    fields := #{atom() => loaded | not_loaded | unavailable},
    relations := #{atom() => complete | not_loaded}}.
-doc "Per-entity coverage. Use `require/2` to check requirements before evaluation.".
-type coverage() :: #{tmux_schema:entity() => entity_coverage()}.
-doc """
Source-query capture diagnostics. candidate_count is the deduplicated
candidate identity count before local residuals and limits. pushed_down
records a nontrivial native condition in the plan, not proof that its command
ran: empty collections can skip it. source_calls records actual capture
commands. The flag does not mean the full predicate was translated. attempt
starts at one and increases only for an explicitly requested retry.
""".
-type query_metadata() :: #{candidate_count := non_neg_integer(),
    pushed_down := boolean(), attempt := 1 | 2, consistency := observed}.
-doc """
Capture identity and provenance. id identifies this snapshot, origin its
registered endpoint and generation the endpoint lifetime. model_version names
the row representation. graph describes relationship coverage, not atomicity.

Live captures include endpoint, observed server_instance, tmux_version,
monotonic capture bounds in time_unit, source_calls, observed stdout bytes and
capabilities. Those fields can be absent in internally constructed partial
captures. Query captures also include `t:query_metadata/0`. Opaque references
and process identities are local values, not portable wire identifiers.
hydration records the requested `t:tmux_server:hydration/0` strategy; source_calls
shows which commands actually ran, including any schema-driven fallback.
""".
-type metadata() :: #{id := reference(), origin := reference(), model_version := 2,
    graph := complete | partial, generation => reference(),
    endpoint => #{socket_path := binary()}, server_instance => tmux_identity:t(),
    tmux_version => tmux_version:t(), capture_started => integer(),
    capture_finished => integer(), time_unit => microsecond,
    source_calls => [source_call()], observed_bytes => non_neg_integer(),
    consistency => observed, hydration => tmux_server:hydration(),
    capabilities => #{field_schema := 1, identity := observed, capture := observed},
    query => query_metadata(), atom() => term()}.

-doc """
Return captured sessions in numeric ID order. Performs no I/O and raises
incomplete_snapshot when that collection was not captured.
""".
-spec sessions(t()) -> [tmux_model:session()].
sessions(Snapshot) -> rows(session, Snapshot).
-doc """
Return unique captured physical windows in numeric ID order. Performs no I/O.
Use `window_links/1` for session-relative membership and indexes.
""".
-spec windows(t()) -> [tmux_model:window()].
windows(Snapshot) -> rows(window, Snapshot).
-doc """
Return every captured membership, ordered by numeric session ID, index and
window ID. Multiple links to the same physical window are preserved. Performs
no I/O; link identity belongs to this snapshot.
""".
-spec window_links(t()) -> [tmux_model:window_link()].
window_links(Snapshot) -> rows(window_link, Snapshot).
-doc """
Return unique captured physical panes in numeric ID order without I/O.
`related/3` orders panes within a window by pane index.
""".
-spec panes(t()) -> [tmux_model:pane()].
panes(Snapshot) -> rows(pane, Snapshot).

-doc """
Return a captured collection by schema entity. Performs no I/O. An unloaded
collection raises incomplete_snapshot rather than appearing empty.
""".
-spec rows(tmux_schema:entity(), t()) -> [tmux_model:row()].
rows(Entity, #{rows := Rows} = Snapshot) ->
    case require([{collection, Entity}], Snapshot) of
        ok -> maps:get(Entity, Rows);
        {error, Detail} -> erlang:error({incomplete_snapshot, Detail}, none,
            [{error_info, #{module => tmux_error}}])
    end.

-doc """
Look up a row in this capture by ID, or a session/index/window tuple for a
window link. Returns none for a known missing identity and a tagged coverage
error for an unloaded collection. Performs no I/O.
""".
-spec get(tmux_schema:entity(), term(), t()) ->
    {ok, tmux_model:row()} | none | {error, map()}.
get(Entity, Key, #{indexes := Indexes} = Snapshot) ->
    maybe
        ok ?= require([{collection, Entity}], Snapshot),
        case maps:find(Key, maps:get(Entity, Indexes)) of
            {ok, Row} -> {ok, Row};
            error -> none
        end
    end.

-doc """
Traverse a complete captured relationship without I/O. To-many relations
return lists; to-one relations return a row or known absence. The input row
must belong to this snapshot. Unloaded relations and mismatched rows return
tagged errors.
""".
-spec related(atom(), tmux_model:row(), t()) ->
    {ok, [tmux_model:row()] | tmux_model:row() | none} | {error, map()}.
related(Relation, Row, #{indexes := Indexes, edges := Edges} = Snapshot) ->
    maybe
        {ok, _} ?= tmux_model:validate(Row),
        Entity = tmux_model:entity(Row),
        ok ?= require([{relation, Entity, Relation}], Snapshot),
        ok ?= case get(Entity, key(Row), Snapshot) of
            {ok, Row} -> ok;
            _ -> {error, #{code => snapshot_row_mismatch}}
        end,
        {ok, Relations} = tmux_schema:relations(Entity),
        #{kind := Kind, target := Target} = maps:get(Relation, Relations),
        Keys = maps:get({Entity, key(Row), Relation}, Edges),
        Values = [maps:get(K, maps:get(Target, Indexes)) || K <- Keys],
        {ok, case {Kind, Values} of
            {many, _} -> Values;
            {one, []} -> none;
            {one, [Value]} -> Value
        end}
    end.

-doc """
Return capture identity, server generation, source calls, capabilities and
read interval metadata. Does not refresh the graph or imply atomic capture.
""".
-spec metadata(t()) -> metadata().
metadata(#{metadata := Metadata}) -> Metadata.
-doc """
Return per-collection, field and relationship coverage. Loaded values, known
absence, not_loaded and unavailable capabilities have distinct meanings.
Performs no I/O.
""".
-spec coverage(t()) -> coverage().
coverage(#{coverage := Coverage}) -> Coverage.

-doc """
Check every declared collection/field/relationship requirement before local
evaluation. Returns an incomplete_snapshot error with missing requirements
when the capture cannot answer faithfully. Performs no I/O, even on empty
data.
""".
-spec require([requirement()], t()) -> ok | {error, map()}.
require(Requirements, #{coverage := Coverage}) when is_list(Requirements) ->
    requirements(Requirements, Coverage, []);
require(_, _) -> {error, #{code => invalid_requirements}}.

%% Internal construction boundary for validated source observations. Partial
%% input never establishes relationship completeness, even when it is empty.
-doc false.
-spec build(map(), map()) -> {ok, t()} | {error, map()}.
build(Input, #{origin := Origin, id := Id, graph := Mode} = Metadata)
  when is_map(Input), is_reference(Origin), is_reference(Id),
       (Mode =:= complete orelse Mode =:= partial) ->
    Entities = tmux_schema_data:entities(),
    maybe
        ok ?= case maps:keys(maps:without(Entities, Input)) of
            [] -> ok;
            _ -> {error, #{code => unknown_entity}}
        end,
        {ok, Indexes} ?= index_entities(Entities, Input, Origin, Id, #{}),
        Rows = maps:map(fun(_, Index) -> sort_rows(maps:values(Index)) end, Indexes),
        ok ?= case Mode of
            complete -> validate_graph(Input, Rows, Indexes);
            partial -> ok
        end,
        Edges = case Mode of complete -> edges(Rows); partial -> #{} end,
        Coverage = maps:from_list([{Entity, entity_coverage(Entity, Input, Rows, Mode)}
                                   || Entity <- Entities]),
        {ok, #{rows => Rows, indexes => Indexes, edges => Edges,
               coverage => Coverage, metadata => Metadata#{model_version => 2}}}
    end;
build(_, _) -> {error, #{code => invalid_snapshot_metadata}}.

index_entities([], _, _, _, Acc) -> {ok, Acc};
index_entities([Entity | Rest], Input, Origin, Id, Acc) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Index} ?= index_rows(maps:get(Entity, Input, []), Entity, Origin, Id, #{}),
        index_entities(Rest, Input, Origin, Id, Acc#{Entity => Index})
    end.

index_rows([], _, _, _, Acc) -> {ok, Acc};
index_rows([Row | Rest], Entity, Origin, Id, Acc) ->
    maybe
        {ok, _} ?= tmux_model:validate(Row),
        ok ?= case {tmux_model:entity(Row), tmux_model:origin(Row)} of
            {Entity, O} when O =:= none; O =:= Origin -> ok;
            _ -> inconsistent(#{reason => wrong_row_context, entity => Entity})
        end,
        Bound = tmux_model:bind(Row, Origin, Id),
        Key = key(Bound),
        ok ?= case maps:find(Key, Acc) of
            error -> ok;
            {ok, Bound} -> ok;
            {ok, Previous} -> inconsistent(#{reason => conflicting_observations,
                entity => Entity, identity => Key,
                fields => [F || {F, V} <- maps:to_list(tmux_model:to_map(Bound)),
                                V =/= tmux_model:get(F, Previous)]})
        end,
        index_rows(Rest, Entity, Origin, Id, Acc#{Key => Bound})
    end;
index_rows(_, Entity, _, _, _) -> {error, #{code => invalid_rows, entity => Entity}}.

key(Row) ->
    case tmux_model:entity(Row) of
        window_link -> {tmux_model:get(session_id, Row), tmux_model:get(index, Row),
                        tmux_model:get(window_id, Row)};
        _ -> tmux_model:get(id, Row)
    end.

sort_rows(Rows) -> lists:sort(fun(A, B) -> order(A) =< order(B) end, Rows).
order(Row) ->
    case key(Row) of
        {Session, Index, Window} -> {number(Session), Index, number(Window)};
        Id -> number(Id)
    end.
number(<<_, Digits/binary>>) -> binary_to_integer(Digits).

validate_graph(Input, Rows, Indexes) ->
    maybe
        ok ?= case lists:all(fun(E) -> maps:is_key(E, Input) end,
                             tmux_schema_data:entities()) of
            true -> ok;
            false -> inconsistent(#{reason => missing_collection})
        end,
        Links = maps:get(window_link, Rows),
        Panes = maps:get(pane, Rows),
        ok ?= references(Links, [{session_id, session}, {window_id, window}], Indexes),
        ok ?= references(Panes, [{window_id, window}], Indexes),
        ok ?= unique_slots(Links, [session_id, index]),
        ok ?= unique_slots(Panes, [window_id, index]),
        counts(maps:get(window, Rows), group(window_id, Panes))
    end.

references([], _, _) -> ok;
references([Row | Rest], Fields, Indexes) ->
    Missing = [F || {F, E} <- Fields,
                    not maps:is_key(tmux_model:get(F, Row), maps:get(E, Indexes))],
    case Missing of
        [] -> references(Rest, Fields, Indexes);
        _ -> inconsistent(#{reason => missing_parent, entity => tmux_model:entity(Row),
                            identity => key(Row), fields => Missing})
    end.

unique_slots(Rows, Fields) ->
    Slots = [[tmux_model:get(F, R) || F <- Fields] || R <- Rows],
    case length(Slots) =:= length(lists:usort(Slots)) of
        true -> ok;
        false -> inconsistent(#{reason => conflicting_positions, fields => Fields})
    end.

counts([], _) -> ok;
counts([Window | Rest], Panes) ->
    Count = length(maps:get(key(Window), Panes, [])),
    case tmux_model:get(pane_count, Window) of
        Count -> counts(Rest, Panes);
        not_loaded -> counts(Rest, Panes);
        unavailable -> counts(Rest, Panes);
        _ -> inconsistent(#{reason => pane_count, identity => key(Window)})
    end.

group(Field, Rows) ->
    Reversed = lists:foldl(fun(Row, Acc) ->
        Key = tmux_model:get(Field, Row),
        Acc#{Key => [Row | maps:get(Key, Acc, [])]}
    end, #{}, Rows),
    maps:map(fun(_, Values) -> lists:reverse(Values) end, Reversed).

edges(Rows) ->
    Links = maps:get(window_link, Rows),
    BySession = group(session_id, Links),
    ByWindow = group(window_id, Links),
    Panes = group(window_id, maps:get(pane, Rows)),
    SessionEdges = lists:append([begin
        Memberships = maps:get(key(S), BySession, []),
        [{{session, key(S), window_links}, [key(L) || L <- Memberships]},
         {{session, key(S), windows}, unique([tmux_model:get(window_id, L) || L <- Memberships])}]
    end || S <- maps:get(session, Rows)]),
    WindowEdges = lists:append([begin
        Children = lists:sort(fun(A, B) ->
            {tmux_model:get(index, A), order(A)} =< {tmux_model:get(index, B), order(B)}
        end, maps:get(key(W), Panes, [])),
        [{{window, key(W), panes}, [key(P) || P <- Children]},
         {{window, key(W), window_links}, [key(L) || L <- maps:get(key(W), ByWindow, [])]}]
    end || W <- maps:get(window, Rows)]),
    LinkEdges = lists:append([[{{window_link, key(L), session}, [tmux_model:get(session_id, L)]},
                              {{window_link, key(L), window}, [tmux_model:get(window_id, L)]}]
                             || L <- Links]),
    PaneEdges = [{{pane, key(P), window}, [tmux_model:get(window_id, P)]}
                 || P <- maps:get(pane, Rows)],
    maps:from_list(SessionEdges ++ WindowEdges ++ LinkEdges ++ PaneEdges).

unique(Values) ->
    {_, Reversed} = lists:foldl(fun(Value, {Seen, Acc}) ->
        case is_map_key(Value, Seen) of
            true -> {Seen, Acc};
            false -> {Seen#{Value => true}, [Value | Acc]}
        end
    end, {#{}, []}, Values),
    lists:reverse(Reversed).

entity_coverage(Entity, Input, Rows, Mode) ->
    {ok, Fields} = tmux_schema:fields(Entity),
    {ok, Relations} = tmux_schema:relations(Entity),
    Present = maps:is_key(Entity, Input),
    FieldCoverage = maps:map(fun(Field, _) ->
        Values = [tmux_model:get(Field, Row) || Row <- maps:get(Entity, Rows)],
        Observed = Present andalso (Mode =:= complete orelse Values =/= []),
        case {Observed, lists:member(unavailable, Values), lists:member(not_loaded, Values)} of
            {_, true, _} -> unavailable;
            {false, _, _} -> not_loaded;
            {_, _, true} -> not_loaded;
            _ -> loaded
        end
    end, Fields),
    #{collection => case Present of true -> complete; false -> not_loaded end,
      fields => FieldCoverage,
      relations => maps:map(fun(_, _) ->
          case Mode of complete -> complete; partial -> not_loaded end
      end, Relations)}.

requirements([], _, []) -> ok;
requirements([], _, Missing) ->
    {error, #{code => incomplete_snapshot, requirements => lists:reverse(Missing)}};
requirements([Requirement | Rest], Coverage, Missing) ->
    case requirement(Requirement, Coverage) of
        {ok, loaded} -> requirements(Rest, Coverage, Missing);
        {ok, complete} -> requirements(Rest, Coverage, Missing);
        {ok, State} -> requirements(Rest, Coverage, [#{requirement => Requirement, state => State} | Missing]);
        error -> {error, #{code => invalid_requirement, requirement => Requirement}}
    end.

requirement({collection, Entity}, Coverage) ->
    case maps:find(Entity, Coverage) of
        {ok, Item} -> maps:find(collection, Item);
        error -> error
    end;
requirement({Kind, Entity, Name}, Coverage) when Kind =:= field; Kind =:= relation ->
    case maps:find(Entity, Coverage) of
        {ok, Item} ->
            Key = case Kind of field -> fields; relation -> relations end,
            maps:find(Name, maps:get(Key, Item));
        error -> error
    end;
requirement(_, _) -> error.

inconsistent(Details) -> {error, Details#{code => inconsistent_capture}}.

-module(tmux_version).
-moduledoc """
Parse the output of tmux -V without invoking tmux.

Support covers tmux 3.3a through 3.8, including intermediate releases. The
minimum-version check includes the patch letter; numeric feature comparisons
use major/minor components. CI tests the endpoints of the supported range. Use
`tmux_server:version/1` for the daemon version observed by an endpoint.
""".
-export([parse/1, require/1, at_least/2]).
-export_type([t/0]).

-doc """
Parsed numeric daemon version plus patch, tracking and original-output
metadata.
""".
-type t() :: #{major := non_neg_integer(), minor := non_neg_integer(),
               patch := binary(), tracking := boolean(), raw := binary()}.

-doc """
Parse bounded tmux -V output into numeric components and patch/tracking
metadata. This is pure parsing, not a probe or compatibility qualification.
""".
-spec parse(binary()) -> {ok, t()} | {error, {invalid_tmux_version, term()}}.
parse(<<"tmux ", Text/binary>> = Raw) when byte_size(Raw) =< 64 ->
    {Name, Tracking} = case trim_newline(Text) of
        <<"next-", Rest/binary>> -> {Rest, true};
        Rest -> {Rest, false}
    end,
    case binary:split(Name, <<".">>, [global]) of
        [Major, MinorPatch] when byte_size(Major) > 0,
                                byte_size(MinorPatch) > 0 ->
            {Minor, Patch} = split_patch(MinorPatch),
            case digits(Major) andalso digits(Minor) of
                true ->
                    {ok, #{major => binary_to_integer(Major),
                           minor => binary_to_integer(Minor),
                           patch => Patch, tracking => Tracking, raw => Raw}};
                false -> {error, {invalid_tmux_version, Raw}}
            end;
        _ -> {error, {invalid_tmux_version, Raw}}
    end;
parse(Raw) ->
    {error, {invalid_tmux_version, Raw}}.

-doc """
Reject a tmux release below the supported floor.

```erlang
1> {ok, Version} = tmux_version:require(<<"tmux 3.3a">>), ok.
ok
2> tmux_version:at_least(Version, {3, 4}).
false
```
""".
-spec require(binary()) ->
    {ok, t()} | {error, {invalid_tmux_version | unsupported_tmux_version, term()}}.
require(Raw) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Version} ?= parse(Raw),
        #{major := Major, minor := Minor, patch := Patch} = Version,
        case {Major, Minor, Patch} >= {3, 3, <<"a">>} of
            true -> {ok, Version};
            false -> {error, {unsupported_tmux_version, Version}}
        end
    end.

-doc """
Compare numeric major/minor components with a required floor. Patch letters do
not promote an older minor release. Performs no I/O.
""".
-spec at_least(t(), {non_neg_integer(), non_neg_integer()}) -> boolean().
at_least(#{major := Major, minor := Minor}, {RequiredMajor, RequiredMinor}) ->
    {Major, Minor} >= {RequiredMajor, RequiredMinor}.

trim_newline(<<>>) -> <<>>;
trim_newline(Text) ->
    case binary:last(Text) of
        10 -> binary:part(Text, 0, byte_size(Text) - 1);
        _ -> Text
    end.

split_patch(Text) ->
    Last = binary:last(Text),
    case Last >= $a andalso Last =< $z of
        true -> {binary:part(Text, 0, byte_size(Text) - 1), <<Last>>};
        false -> {Text, <<>>}
    end.

digits(<<>>) -> false;
digits(Text) -> digits_tail(Text).

digits_tail(<<>>) -> true;
digits_tail(<<C, Rest/binary>>) when C >= $0, C =< $9 -> digits_tail(Rest);
digits_tail(_) -> false.

-module(tmux_window_link).
-moduledoc """
Act on a physical window's observed membership in a particular session.

A window link is identified by session ID, window index and expected physical
window ID. It has no stable tmux link ID. These calls check that the observed
membership still names the expected window before dispatching an action.
Missing or replaced membership returns stale_link. A link that moves away and
back to the same coordinates and physical window cannot be distinguished.

The preflight and action use separate one-shot commands. Concurrent changes
after preflight can still affect the action; this is not atomic
compare-and-act. All input rows must belong to the same registered owner.
Re-read or explicitly bind rows when using another owner. Closed owners and
known restarts invalidate their rows. Every call performs explicit I/O after
validating its arguments.

Use `tmux_window:kill/1` to destroy a physical window across all memberships.
Use `unlink/2` to remove one membership. Existing rows and
snapshots are never refreshed by actions; use `get/3` or a
new snapshot for current memberships.
""".
-export([get/3, select/1, link/3, move/3, swap/3, unlink/2, check/2]).
-export_type([index/0, placement_options/0, swap_options/0, unlink_options/0]).

-doc "An explicit tmux window index; relative and next-free selectors are not accepted.".
-type index() :: 0..2147483647.
-doc "Destination index is required. Defaults: detach true, replace false. Replacement may destroy the destination window.".
-type placement_options() :: #{index := index(), detach => boolean(), replace => boolean()}.
-doc "Maps detach to tmux's -d flag, default true.".
-type swap_options() :: #{detach => boolean()}.
-doc "Force defaults false. Force permits unlinking the last membership and destroying its physical window.".
-type unlink_options() :: #{force => boolean()}.

-doc """
Read a current membership at the explicit session ID and index. The returned
native row carries its registered owner and a new observation identity.
Returns target_gone if the session or index is absent. This read does not make
later actions atomic and does not refresh previously captured links.

Invalid indexes are rejected before I/O:

```erlang
1> tmux_window_link:get(invalid_server, <<"$0">>, -1).
{error,#{code => invalid_option,path => [index]}}
```
""".
-spec get(tmux_server:t(), tmux_model:session_id(), index()) ->
    {ok, tmux_model:window_link()} | {error, map()}.
get(Server, SessionId, Index) ->
    maybe
        {ok, IndexBytes} ?= index(Index),
        {ok, SessionTarget} ?= tmux_target:selector(session, SessionId),
        {ok, Origin} ?= tmux_server:origin(Server),
        {ok, #{stdout := Output}} ?= tmux_target:run(Server, <<"list-windows">>,
            [<<"-t">>, SessionTarget,
             <<"-f">>, <<"#{==:#{window_index},", IndexBytes/binary, "}">>, <<"-F">>,
             <<"#{session_id}\t#{window_index}\t#{window_id}\t#{window_active}">>]),
        {ok, Row} ?= decode(Output, SessionId, Index),
        {ok, Server} ?= tmux_server:from_origin(Origin),
        {ok, tmux_model:bind(Row, Origin, make_ref())}
    end.

-doc """
Select this membership as its session's current window after checking the
expected physical window. Performs I/O and returns the command result.
""".
-spec select(tmux_model:window_link()) ->
    {ok, tmux_operation:completed()} | {error, tmux_operation:failure()}.
select(Link) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Server} ?= tmux_target:owner(window_link, Link),
        {ok, _, Target} ?= check(Server, Link),
        tmux_target:run(Server, <<"select-window">>, [<<"-t">>, Target])
    end.

-doc """
Add another membership of this link's physical window to the destination
session and explicit index. Defaults to detached and refuses an occupied
index. replace = true maps to tmux -k and can destroy the occupied window.
Returns the command result; use `get/3` to observe the new membership. The
source membership remains. Session groups and renumber-windows retain their
tmux semantics. Performs I/O after owner and membership checks.
""".
-spec link(tmux_model:window_link(), tmux_model:session(), placement_options()) ->
    {ok, tmux_operation:completed()} | {error, tmux_operation:failure()}.
link(Link, Session, Options) -> place(<<"link-window">>, Link, Session, Options).

-doc """
Move this membership to the destination session and explicit index, leaving
its physical window's other links intact. Placement options follow `link/3`.
Moving the final window out of a session can destroy that session; automatic
renumbering and session groups can change other memberships. Captured rows
remain unchanged. Returns the command result after observed preflight.
""".
-spec move(tmux_model:window_link(), tmux_model:session(), placement_options()) ->
    {ok, tmux_operation:completed()} | {error, tmux_operation:failure()}.
move(Link, Session, Options) -> place(<<"move-window">>, Link, Session, Options).

-doc """
Swap the physical windows at two checked memberships. Other links to either
window remain intact. detach maps to tmux -d and defaults true. tmux applies
its session-selection and group-synchronization rules. Returns the command
result; old rows still name their original expected windows and can become
stale. Performs I/O, with the documented gap between preflight and action.
""".
-spec swap(tmux_model:window_link(), tmux_model:window_link(), swap_options()) ->
    {ok, tmux_operation:completed()} | {error, tmux_operation:failure()}.
swap(Source, Destination, Options) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Flags} ?= tmux_args:options(Options, [{detach, flag, <<"-d">>}], #{detach => true}),
        {ok, Server} ?= tmux_target:same_owner(window_link, Source, window_link, Destination),
        {ok, _, From} ?= check(Server, Source),
        {ok, _, To} ?= check(Server, Destination),
        tmux_target:run(Server, <<"swap-window">>,
            Flags ++ [<<"-s">>, From, <<"-t">>, To])
    end.

-doc """
Remove one checked membership. force defaults false, retaining tmux's
protection for windows linked to only one session. force = true permits
removing the last link, destroying that physical window and possibly its
session. Duplicate links within one session retain tmux's native protection
rules. Performs I/O and returns the command result without refreshing rows.
""".
-spec unlink(tmux_model:window_link(), unlink_options()) ->
    {ok, tmux_operation:completed()} | {error, tmux_operation:failure()}.
unlink(Link, Options) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Flags} ?= tmux_args:options(Options, [{force, flag, <<"-k">>}], #{}),
        {ok, Server} ?= tmux_target:owner(window_link, Link),
        {ok, _, Target} ?= check(Server, Link),
        tmux_target:run(Server, <<"unlink-window">>, Flags ++ [<<"-t">>, Target])
    end.

place(Command, Link, Session, Options) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Index, Flags} ?= placement(Options),
        {ok, Server} ?= tmux_target:same_owner(window_link, Link, session, Session),
        {ok, _, Source} ?= check(Server, Link),
        {ok, SessionTarget} ?= tmux_target:selector(session, tmux_model:get(id, Session)),
        Target = <<SessionTarget/binary, Index/binary>>,
        tmux_target:run(Server, Command, Flags ++ [<<"-s">>, Source, <<"-t">>, Target])
    end.

placement(Options) when is_map(Options) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Flags} ?= tmux_args:options(maps:remove(index, Options),
            [{detach, flag, <<"-d">>}, {replace, flag, <<"-k">>}], #{detach => true}),
        {ok, Index} ?= case maps:find(index, Options) of
            {ok, Value} -> index(Value);
            error -> {error, #{code => missing_option, path => [index]}}
        end,
        {ok, Index, Flags}
    end;
placement(_) -> {error, #{code => invalid_options, path => []}}.

index(Value) when is_integer(Value, 0, 2147483647) -> {ok, integer_to_binary(Value)};
index(_) -> {error, #{code => invalid_option, path => [index]}}.

-doc false.
-spec check(tmux_server:t(), tmux_model:window_link()) ->
    {ok, tmux_model:window_link(), binary()} | {error, map()}.
check(Server, Link) ->
    SessionId = tmux_model:get(session_id, Link),
    Index = tmux_model:get(index, Link),
    Expected = tmux_model:get(window_id, Link),
    case get(Server, SessionId, Index) of
        {ok, Current} ->
            case tmux_model:get(window_id, Current) of
                Expected ->
                    {ok, Current, <<SessionId/binary, $:, (integer_to_binary(Index))/binary>>};
                Actual -> {error, #{code => stale_link, expected => Expected, actual => Actual}}
            end;
        {error, #{code := target_gone} = Cause} ->
            {error, #{code => stale_link, expected => Expected, cause => Cause}};
        {error, _} = Error -> Error
    end.

decode(<<>>, _, _) -> {error, #{code => target_gone}};
decode(Output, SessionId, Index) when byte_size(Output) =< 256 ->
    IndexBytes = integer_to_binary(Index),
    case binary:split(Output, <<"\t">>, [global]) of
        [SessionId, IndexBytes, WindowId, <<Active, $\n>>] when Active =:= $0; Active =:= $1 ->
            tmux_model:window_link(#{session_id => SessionId, index => Index,
                window_id => WindowId, active => Active =:= $1});
        _ -> {error, #{code => invalid_observation, entity => window_link}}
    end;
decode(_, _, _) -> {error, #{code => invalid_observation, entity => window_link}}.

-module(tmux_window).
-moduledoc """
Create physical windows in a session and act through their registered IDs.

`create/2` accepts name, cwd, env, launch and detach, using the
session's next available index. It defaults to detached. `get/2`
reads current fields; `rename/2` returns the command result and
leaves previous records unchanged. Launch and environment options follow
`tmux_session:create/2`. An empty shell command does not portably keep the
window alive: older tmux releases execute it as a shell command. Use a running
program when needed. Creation returns a fresh observed row or an error
retaining a completed mutation and its result if the follow-up observation
fails.

`kill/1` destroys the physical window and all its links. Use
`tmux_window_link:unlink/2` to remove one session membership. These calls
perform I/O after validating their inputs. `select_layout/2`
changes the physical window's layout across all its session links; previously
observed pane geometry remains unchanged in captured values.
""".
-export([create/2, get/2, rename/2, kill/1, respawn/2, select_layout/2]).

-export_type([create_options/0, respawn_options/0, layout/0]).
-doc "Physical-window creation options; defaults to a detached window at the next free session index.".
-type create_options() :: #{name => binary(), cwd => binary(), env => #{binary() => binary()},
    launch => tmux_command:launch_spec(), detach => boolean()}.
-doc "Physical-window respawn options. Defaults: force false, launch previous, saved cwd. A forced respawn removes other panes.".
-type respawn_options() :: #{force => boolean(), launch => tmux_command:respawn_spec(),
                             cwd => binary(), env => #{binary() => binary()}}.
-doc "A built-in arrangement, its exact binary name, or a serialized layout. Native JSON v2 requires tmux 3.8.".
-type layout() :: even_horizontal | even_vertical | main_horizontal | main_vertical |
                  tiled | binary().

-doc """
Create a physical window in the session's next free index and observe it.
Defaults to detached. Launch, cwd and environment follow
`tmux_session:create/2`. Performs I/O and retains completed-mutation details
if observation fails.
""".
-spec create(tmux_model:session(), create_options()) -> {ok, tmux_model:window()} | {error, map()}.
create(Session, Options) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Flags, Launch} ?= tmux_args:launch_options(Options, [{name, text_format, <<"-n">>}]),
        {ok, Server, Target} ?= tmux_target:resolve(session, Session),
        {ok, Result} ?= tmux_target:run(Server, <<"new-window">>,
            [<<"-P">>, <<"-F">>, <<"#{window_id}">>, <<"-t">>, Target] ++
            Flags ++ [<<"--">> | Launch]),
        tmux_observe:created(Server, window, Result)
    end.

-doc """
Explicitly read a physical window by stable ID. Returns a fresh record or
target_gone. Physical windows do not have a universal session or window index.
""".
-spec get(tmux_server:t(), tmux_model:window_id()) -> {ok, tmux_model:window()} | {error, map()}.
get(Server, Id) -> tmux_observe:get(Server, window, Id).

-doc """
Rename the registered physical window with a literal name. Performs I/O and
returns the command result. Captured rows and snapshots remain unchanged.
""".
-spec rename(tmux_model:window(), binary()) -> {ok, map()} | {error, map()}.
rename(Window, Name) ->
    maybe
        {ok, [_, Literal]} ?= tmux_args:options(#{name => Name}, [{name, text_format, <<"-n">>}]),
        tmux_target:act(window, Window, <<"rename-window">>, [Literal])
    end.

-doc """
Destroy the physical window and all of its session links. This does not unlink
only one membership. Performs I/O after origin and target validation.
""".
-spec kill(tmux_model:window()) -> {ok, map()} | {error, map()}.
kill(Window) -> tmux_target:act(window, Window, <<"kill-window">>, []).

-doc """
Respawn a registered physical window across all its session links. tmux keeps
the first pane's ID, removes the other panes and rebuilds a single-pane
layout. force defaults false: a window with a running pane normally returns
command_error. force = true permits closing existing PTYs. Command completion
does not establish former-job termination or application readiness. Other
panes can already be removed if a later spawn step fails. Respawn also selects
this window in tmux's resolved session. For a window linked into several
sessions, tmux chooses that context from the physical ID; this facade does not
pin selection or environment to a captured membership.

launch defaults to previous and reuses the retained pane's saved command.
Explicit argv and shell maps, saved cwd and fresh-spawn environment rules
follow `tmux_pane:respawn/2`, using the resolved session's environment. This
physical-window mutation affects every link. Performs I/O after validation and
returns the command result without refreshing rows. Use `get/2` or a new
snapshot for current data.
""".
-spec respawn(tmux_model:window(), respawn_options()) ->
    {ok, tmux_operation:completed()} | {error, tmux_operation:failure()}.
respawn(Window, Options) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Flags, Launch} ?= tmux_args:respawn_options(Options),
        {ok, Server, Target} ?= tmux_target:resolve(window, Window),
        tmux_target:run(Server, <<"respawn-window">>,
            Flags ++ [<<"-t">>, Target, <<"--">> | Launch])
    end.

-doc """
Select a built-in arrangement or restore a literal serialized layout for this
registered physical window. Binary names must exactly match one of the five
built-ins; abbreviations and other names are rejected. Legacy serialized
layouts need four hexadecimal checksum digits, a comma and nonempty data. This
guard avoids a malformed-header crash in tmux 3.3 and 3.3a.

Native JSON v2 layouts require a bounded JSON object with V = 2 and an L
object. They return unsupported_capability on tmux before 3.8 without
dispatching a tmux command. This preserves `get/2` layout restoration on newer
servers.

Execution unzooms the window and changes it in every linked session. tmux
validates serialized geometry; malformed geometry can return a command error.
The layout argument uses no shell or format expansion. Existing rows are not
refreshed; use `get/2` or a fresh snapshot to observe layout and pane
geometry.

Unsupported atom names fail before dispatch:

```erlang
1> tmux_window:select_layout(invalid_row, unknown_layout).
{error,#{code => invalid_layout,path => [layout]}}
```
""".
-spec select_layout(tmux_model:window(), layout()) ->
    {ok, tmux_operation:completed()} | {error, tmux_operation:failure()}.
select_layout(Window, Layout) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Argument, Kind} ?= layout_argument(Layout),
        {ok, Server, Target} ?= tmux_target:resolve(window, Window),
        ok ?= require_layout(Kind, Server),
        tmux_target:run(Server, <<"select-layout">>,
            [<<"-t">>, Target, <<"--">>, Argument])
    end.

layout_argument(even_horizontal) -> {ok, <<"even-horizontal">>, base};
layout_argument(even_vertical) -> {ok, <<"even-vertical">>, base};
layout_argument(main_horizontal) -> {ok, <<"main-horizontal">>, base};
layout_argument(main_vertical) -> {ok, <<"main-vertical">>, base};
layout_argument(tiled) -> {ok, <<"tiled">>, base};
layout_argument(Layout) when is_binary(Layout) ->
    Result = maybe
        {ok, _} ?= tmux_command:raw(<<"select-layout">>, [Layout]),
        {ok, _} ?= tmux_schema:value(#{type => text}, Layout),
        layout_kind(Layout)
    end,
    case Result of
        {ok, _, _} -> Result;
        {error, Detail} -> {error, Detail#{path => [layout]}}
    end;
layout_argument(_) -> {error, #{code => invalid_layout, path => [layout]}}.

layout_kind(Layout) ->
    Names = [<<"even-horizontal">>, <<"even-vertical">>, <<"main-horizontal">>,
             <<"main-vertical">>, <<"tiled">>],
    case lists:member(Layout, Names) orelse legacy_header(Layout) of
        true -> {ok, Layout, base};
        false ->
            case tmux_json:decode(Layout) of
                {ok, #{<<"V">> := 2, <<"L">> := Root}} when is_map(Root) ->
                    {ok, Layout, json_v2};
                _ -> {error, #{code => invalid_layout}}
            end
    end.

%% A short/nonhex header leaves an uninitialized error cause in 3.3/3.3a.
%% Require the complete legacy header before those servers can parse it.
legacy_header(<<A, B, C, D, $,, Body/binary>>) when byte_size(Body) > 0 ->
    lists:all(fun(Byte) ->
        is_integer(Byte, $0, $9) orelse is_integer(Byte, $a, $f) orelse
        is_integer(Byte, $A, $F)
    end, [A, B, C, D]);
legacy_header(_) -> false.

require_layout(base, _) -> ok;
require_layout(json_v2, Server) ->
    maybe
        {ok, Version} ?= tmux_server:version(Server),
        tmux_capability:require(Version, layout_json)
    end.
